| Status | Code | Message | Source | Raised by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_decision` | "Agent OS only sends Allow once or Deny." | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X3 |
| 404 | `approval_missing` | "That approval isn't waiting anymore." | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X3 |
| 409 | `approval_busy` | "Agent OS is already sending your answer to this approval." | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X3 |
| 409 | `approval_failed` | "OpenClaw didn't take that answer: <its text>" | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X3 |
| 404 | `change_missing` | "That file isn't in this session's changes anymore." | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X7 |
| 400 | `invalid_target` | "Agent OS can hand this only to Claude Code or Codex." | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X8, X10 |
| 400 | `hand_over_not_available` | "Only a Cursor session is handed over this way." | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X10 |
| 400 | `copy_not_available` | "OpenClaw picks its own folder, so it can't use a separate copy." | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X9 |
| 409 | `not_git` | "This folder isn't a git project, so Agent OS can't make a separate copy." | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X9 |
| 409 | `worktree_failed` | "Agent OS couldn't make the separate copy. Git said: <its text>" | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X9 |
| 404 | `no_worktree` | "This session doesn't use a separate copy." | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X9 |
| 409 | `worktree_dirty` | "The separate copy has changes that aren't committed. Commit or discard them, then try again." | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X9 |
| 409 | `session_live` | "That session is still running. Stop it first, then remove its separate copy." (new message for an existing code) | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X9 |
| 409 | `not_held` | "Keep going is offered only when the plan ran out." | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X10 |
| 409 | `keep_going_unavailable` | the option's `reason` from `continue.js` (existing sentences) | existing | X10 |
| (brainError) | `unsafe_settings` | "Agent OS stopped this session: its Claude settings had a key Agent OS never writes." (reaches a person only through a bug) | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X2a |
| 409 | `approval_failed` | "OpenClaw didn't take that answer and gave no reason." (a non-zero exit with nothing printed, or a runner that threw) (X3 #3) | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X3 |
| 409 | `approval_failed` | "OpenClaw didn't answer in time, so Agent OS can't tell whether your answer arrived." (a call cut off at the 10 s limit) (X3 #3) | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X3 |
| 409 | `worktree_failed` | "Agent OS couldn't make the separate copy: git took longer than 2 minutes." (timeout form) / "Agent OS couldn't make the separate copy, and git gave no reason." (no-text form) (X9 #3) | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X9 |
| 409 | `worktree_remove_failed` | "Agent OS couldn't remove the separate copy. Git said: <its text>", with its timeout and no-text forms as Task X9 words them (X9 #3) | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X9 |
| 409 | `session_live` | "Another session is still running in this separate copy. Stop it first, then remove the copy." (a removal while another session runs, or is starting, in the copy) (X9 #4) | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X9 |
| 409 | `not_live` | "This Cursor session has ended, so there is no screen to hand over." (`handOver` for an ended Cursor session) (X10 #4) | NEW SENTENCE (Q32) | X10 |

- Every code is a `sessionError(status, code, message)` answered with `errorBody(err)`, except `unsafe_settings` (a `brainError`, answered like the other brain errors).
- Existing codes reused (X10 #4, X9 #8, U11 #4): 409 `session_busy` (the manager's `BUSY_MESSAGE`) from `keepGoing` and `handOver` while one runs, for a start or resume in a copy that is being removed, and from `deleteRecording` while another request resumes or dismisses the session; 409 `execution_gate_off` (`LOOK_ONLY_MESSAGE`) from `keepGoing` for Claude before the stop; any brain error that `resolveBrainForRun` throws in Claude's pre-check (`openrouter_key_missing` 409 and so on), answered like the other brain errors by `routes.js`'s `answerFor`.

### Desktop shell (`desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`, X4)

- `const ALERT_LINE_PREFIX: &str = "AGENT_OS_ALERT:";`
- `fn parse_alert_line(line: &str) -> Option<AlertNote>` with `struct AlertNote { session_id: String, agent: String, kind: String, text: String }`: parses with `serde_json::Value` (no new crate); `None` unless all four are strings and `kind` is `waiting`, `approval` or `limit`; `text` cut to 200 characters.
- `fn alert_title(kind: &str, agent: &str) -> Option<String>`: waiting and approval → "<agent> is waiting for you"; limit → "<agent>'s plan ran out" (both NEW SENTENCE (Q32)).
- `fn should_notify(visible: bool, focused: bool) -> bool` → `!visible || !focused`.
- `watch_server(stdout, stderr, token, tx, app: AppHandle)`: stdout read with `read_until(b'\n')` and `String::from_utf8_lossy` (R21); a ready line as today; an alert line → when `should_notify` for the `main` window, `app.notification().builder().title(title).body(text).show()` (errors printed to stderr, never fatal).
- Builder: `.plugin(tauri_plugin_notification::init())` next to the dialog plugin. `capabilities/default.json` unchanged.
- `test/release-config.test.js`: `Cargo.toml` has `tauri-plugin-notification = "=2.7.0"`; `main.rs` registers it; `Cargo.lock` resolves 2.7.0; `package.json` has no `@tauri-apps/plugin-notification`; the capability list and description stay exactly as SP3 pinned them (no `notification:` entry).
- stderr uses the same byte-safe reader (X4 #1): the stderr loop at main.rs:259 has the same G9 bug, and the fix is the same helper call, so X4 applies it to both streams and its release-config test checks both. The contract names stdout only (R21). If the orchestrator declines, X4 keeps stderr's old loop and drops the `read_lines_lossy(BufReader::new(stderr), ` assertion.
- Internal helper names in main.rs (private, used by no other task) (X4 #2): `ALERT_KINDS`, `ALERT_TEXT_MAX`, `NOTIFICATION_TAP`, `notification_click_shows_window(action_id: &str) -> bool`, `read_lines_lossy<R: BufRead>(reader: R, each: impl FnMut(&str))`, `notify_alert(app: &AppHandle, note: &AlertNote)`, `listen_for_notification_clicks(app: &tauri::App)`.
- `parse_alert_line` also returns `None` for an empty `sessionId` or a blank `agent` (a title with no agent name would read " is waiting for you"); the server never prints either (X4 #3).
- A click on a notification shows, unminimizes and focuses the `main` window (`show_main_window`), through the plugin's Rust `on_action`, registered in `setup` before `start_server` (X4 #4; this comes from the X4 brief, and the spec has no sentence about clicks).
- The window check and `show()` run on the main thread through `AppHandle::run_on_main_thread`, so the stdout reader never waits on the window (X4 #5).
- Expected console line (X4 #7, E2 #9): in the desktop window the plugin's injected script asks `is_permission_granted` at every page load and is refused (no permission, R20), so the console shows one "not allowed" line per load. E1 Steps 9-12 and E2 S7 (its Step 13 (b)) treat that line as expected, not as a regression.
- `desktop/README.md` (X4 #6): it is outside X4's file list and now leaves out the notifications. Proposed text for E1's README check: a new section after "## Folder picker (dialog plugin)" and before "## Releasing",

  ```
  ## Notifications (notification plugin)

  `tauri-plugin-notification` (pinned to exactly 2.7.0) is registered in `src/main.rs`.
  Only the Rust shell uses it: when a session needs you, the server prints one line,
  `AGENT_OS_ALERT:<json>`, and the shell shows a notification if the window is hidden
  or not focused. Clicking the notification brings the window back. The page has no
  `notification:` permission in `capabilities/default.json` and no notification
  package, so nothing in the page can send one. macOS asks once, on the first
  notification, whether Agent OS may show them. In `npm run desktop:dev`
  notifications show up as Terminal's; try them in a built app.
  ```

  and in "How it works", after the line `  |     3. waits (max 20 s) for the server to print  AGENT_OS_READY:<port>`, the line `  |        then reads its AGENT_OS_ALERT:<json> lines (notifications)`.

### Task D1: Spec update: record the SP4 rulings

The spec's "SP4 Session extras" section was written on 2026-10-11, before anyone read the installed agents closely. The research of 2026-10-29 (`sp4/agent-facts.md`, "Differences from the spec" D1 to D22; `sp4/code-map.md`, gaps G1 to G14) found lines that cannot work as written. Three examples: Claude Code cannot send a SessionStart hook over HTTP; answering a big hook body with an error would put "hook error" into the person's own Claude transcript; and on desktop the page's notification permission call never asks anything. The orchestrator ruled on each finding (R1 to R30, `sp4/rulings.md`), and this plan's contract added the choices K1 to K22. This task writes all of them into the spec, so every later SP4 task and every reviewer argues from one document. Each replaced line is rewritten in place with its ruling or choice, the date 2026-10-29 and the research reason; R20 (`tauri-plugin-notification` 2.7.0, the Rust crate only) goes everywhere the spec talks about desktop notifications; a new Appendix A3 lists every ruling and choice with its source. The task changes one file, the spec: no code, no test file, no package, no UI. Its test is a scratch check script with 110 exact counts (it fails on today's spec and passes after the edits), the SHA-256 of the finished file, and the full suite, which keeps its baseline numbers because nothing new is pinned.

**Worker notes:**
- Run every command from the worktree root `<worktree>`. Never commit, push, tag, stash or set `CI=true`. Never start an agent or a server. Never read `.env` files or `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.cursor`, `~/.openclaw`, `~/.hermes`.
- A PreToolUse hook ("Fact-Forcing Gate") may refuse the first Write of a new file. State the facts it asks for, then retry the same call.
- `$SCRATCH` below means your own session scratchpad folder. The check script lives there, never in the repo.
- Copy every block exactly, character for character: straight quotes, `\|` inside table rows (it keeps a `|` inside a table cell), the "⚠", "—", "·" and "→" characters, and two spaces before a nested `  - ` bullet. Do not reflow: each block line is one line of the spec.

### Task X1a: Signals core: model, activity states, alert state, frames, AGENT_OS_ALERT line

Today a session's status comes from one rule: the first output makes it live, 20 s without counted output makes it idle, and counted output or a keystroke makes it live again (`markActive` in `server/runtime/sessions/manager.js`). A BEL or an OSC 9 / 99 / 777 that the screen mirror sees is passed to the windows as it is, in SP3's `{t:"alert", raw}` frame, and nothing else happens. SP4 needs much more: a session can be **waiting** for the person, **held** because its plan ran out, or **idle because its turn is done**, and it must stay that way through redraws until the right thing happens.

This task builds the core that every later SP4 task feeds:

1. a new pure module, `server/runtime/sessions/signals.js`, with the one signal shape, the activity-state machine (the spec's transition table as a function), the alert text cleaner, the `AGENT_OS_ALERT` line and the recording marker shape;
2. the session manager uses that machine for every session: it keeps each session's activity and alert in memory, sends `{t:"state"}` (with `resetAt` while held) and the new `{t:"alert", kind, text}` frames, adds a "permission asked" marker to meta.json, arms the idle, backstop and reset-time timers, and puts the alert state into `GET /api/sessions` (R22), so the page never needs a WebSocket to show a marker or a badge;
3. internal entry points for the later signal sources (`applySignal`, `markSourceSeen`, `markNewTurn`, `setHeld`, `clearHeld`, `addMarker`, `markers`, `liveAgentSessions`, `onLiveChange`);
4. `GET /api/sessions/:id/markers` for the replay (U11);
5. one single-line `AGENT_OS_ALERT:<json>` on the server's stdout when an alert starts, only when the desktop shell started the server (`AGENT_OS_PACKAGED=1`), for X4's notification.

Until Task X1b adds the per-agent rules, every BEL or OSC 9 / 99 / 777 from an agent session is a basic "May need you" alert (R19's rule, used for every agent for now). No signal ever answers, types or starts anything: signals only change what a session shows. Tests use injected fakes and W1's fake agents only; two test files start a real `server/index.js` with the fakes in a temp HOME. No real agent, no real Terminal window, no notification.

```js
  ["held, the reset time passed (held_cleared): idle", HELD, { type: "held_cleared" }, act({ status: "idle" })],
  ["live, held_cleared: no change", act({ status: "live" }), { type: "held_cleared" }, act({ status: "live" })],
  ["held, the process ends: exited, the alert and the reset time cleared", HELD, { type: "exit" }, act({ status: "exited" })],
  ["exited, user input: stays exited", act({ status: "exited" }), { type: "input" }, act({ status: "exited" })]
];

test("constants: the kinds, sources and limits the SP4 contract names", () => {
  assert.deepEqual(SIGNAL_KINDS, ["waiting", "turn_done", "limit", "approval", "resolved"]);
  assert.deepEqual(ALERT_KINDS, ["waiting", "approval", "limit"]);
  assert.deepEqual(SIGNAL_SOURCES, ["hook", "status", "poll", "osc", "bel", "title", "text", "openclaw"]);
  for (const list of [SIGNAL_KINDS, ALERT_KINDS, SIGNAL_SOURCES]) assert.equal(Object.isFrozen(list), true);
  assert.equal(ALERT_TEXT_MAX, 200);
  assert.equal(BASIC_ALERT_TEXT, "May need you");
  assert.equal(TURN_DONE_BACKSTOP_MS, 120000);
  assert.equal(HELD_CHECK_MS, 60000);
  assert.equal(MARKERS_MAX, 500);
  assert.equal(ALERT_LINE_PREFIX, "AGENT_OS_ALERT:");
});

test("cleanAlertText: control characters go, tabs and newlines become spaces, runs of spaces collapse, and the text is cut to 200 code points without an ellipsis", () => {
  assert.equal(cleanAlertText("  Wants\tto\nuse \u001b[31mBash\u0007  "), "Wants to use [31mBash");
  assert.equal(cleanAlertText("a\u0085b\u009bc\u007fd"), "abcd", "C1 and DEL go");
  assert.equal(cleanAlertText("one\r\ntwo"), "one two");
  assert.equal(cleanAlertText(null), "");
  assert.equal(cleanAlertText(undefined), "");
  assert.equal(cleanAlertText(42), "42");
  assert.equal(cleanAlertText("x".repeat(250)), "x".repeat(200));
  assert.equal(cleanAlertText("abcdef", 3), "abc");
  const faces = cleanAlertText("😀".repeat(201));
  assert.equal(Array.from(faces).length, 200, "cut by code points");
  assert.equal(faces, "😀".repeat(200), "no character is split");
  assert.equal(faces.endsWith("…"), false);
});

test("makeSignal: a frozen signal with cleaned text and an ISO time; resetAt only for a limit; a caller's bug is a TypeError", () => {
  const signal = makeSignal({ sessionId: SID, kind: "waiting", text: " Wants to use\nBash ", source: "hook", at: "2026-10-29T10:00:00Z" });
  assert.deepEqual(signal, { sessionId: SID, kind: "waiting", text: "Wants to use Bash", at: EARLIER, source: "hook", resetAt: null });
  assert.equal(Object.isFrozen(signal), true);
  assert.equal(makeSignal({ sessionId: SID, kind: "limit", source: "text", resetAt: "2026-10-29T13:00:00Z" }).resetAt, RESET);
  assert.equal(makeSignal({ sessionId: SID, kind: "limit", source: "text", resetAt: "soon" }).resetAt, null);
  assert.equal(makeSignal({ sessionId: SID, kind: "waiting", source: "bel", resetAt: RESET }).resetAt, null, "only a limit has a reset time");
  const fresh = makeSignal({ sessionId: SID, kind: "resolved", source: "title" });
  assert.ok(Math.abs(Date.parse(fresh.at) - Date.now()) < 5000, "the time defaults to now");
  assert.equal(fresh.text, "");
  for (const bad of [
    { kind: "waiting", source: "hook" },
    { sessionId: "", kind: "waiting", source: "hook" },
    { sessionId: SID, kind: "done", source: "hook" },
    { sessionId: SID, kind: "waiting", source: "email" },
    { sessionId: SID, kind: "waiting", source: "hook", at: "yesterday" }
  ]) {
    assert.throws(() => makeSignal(bad), TypeError, JSON.stringify(bad));
  }
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `server/runtime/sessions/signals.js`** with exactly this content:

```js
// Signals (SP4): one shape for everything that tells Agent OS what an agent
// in a session is doing, the activity-state machine that turns signals and
// terminal activity into a session's status and alert, and the one shape of
// the AGENT_OS_ALERT line and of a recording marker.
//
// Spec "SP4 Session extras" (Signals, Alerts UI, Recordings in Runs) and
// "Session activity states" (the transition table), with the orchestrator's
// rulings R19 (basic alerts), R21 (the alert line), R22 (alert state) and R23
// (a prompt marker holds no text), and the plan's choices K1, K4, K5, K7, K8
// and K20. Everything here is pure: no timers, no disk, no process; the only
// clock read is a default time. The session manager (manager.js) owns the
// timers, the frames and meta.json.
//
// Signals are hints (spec "Hook events are hints"): they change only what a
// session shows, its status and its alert. Nothing here answers, types or
// starts anything.

export const SIGNAL_KINDS = Object.freeze(["waiting", "turn_done", "limit", "approval", "resolved"]);
export const ALERT_KINDS = Object.freeze(["waiting", "approval", "limit"]);
export const SIGNAL_SOURCES = Object.freeze(["hook", "status", "poll", "osc", "bel", "title", "text", "openclaw"]);
// The longest alert text kept anywhere, the AGENT_OS_ALERT line included (R21).
export const ALERT_TEXT_MAX = 200;
// What a basic alert says (R19): a BEL or an OSC 9 / 99 / 777 tells Agent OS
// only that the agent wants attention, not why.
export const BASIC_ALERT_TEXT = "May need you";
// K5: a turn-done session whose turn_done never comes (an API error, Esc) is
// idle this long after its last counted output, input or new turn.
export const TURN_DONE_BACKSTOP_MS = 120 * 1000;
// K3: how often a held session compares the wall clock with its reset time.
export const HELD_CHECK_MS = 60 * 1000;
// K20: the most markers one session keeps in meta.json (the oldest go first).
export const MARKERS_MAX = 500;
// The desktop shell looks for stdout lines that start with this (spec
// "Desktop shell changes").
export const ALERT_LINE_PREFIX = "AGENT_OS_ALERT:";

const ACTIVITY_STATUSES = Object.freeze(["starting", "live", "waiting", "idle", "held", "exited"]);
const EVENT_TYPES = new Set([
  "output",
  "counted",
  "input",
  "idle_timer",
  "signal",
  "source_seen",
  "new_turn",
  "held",
  "held_cleared",
  "exit"
]);
// The signal kinds the activity takes as a "signal" event. A limit is not one:
// limit evidence goes through the agent's limit rule, which sends "held".
const ACTIVITY_SIGNAL_KINDS = Object.freeze(["waiting", "approval", "turn_done", "resolved"]);
const MARKER_TYPES = new Set(["prompt", "permission", "files"]);
// Every C0 control character, DEL and every C1 control character.
const CONTROL_CHARACTERS = /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f-\u009f]/g;
// The longest file path a "files changed" marker keeps.
const MARKER_PATH_MAX = 4096;

function isoOrNull(value) {
  if (typeof value !== "string" || value === "") return null;
  const ms = Date.parse(value);
  return Number.isFinite(ms) ? new Date(ms).toISOString() : null;
}

function countOrNull(value) {
  return Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0 ? value : null;
}

// Short, plain, one-line text: tabs and newlines become spaces, every other
// control character goes, runs of spaces collapse, and the text is cut to
// `max` code points (a character is never split, and no "…" is added).
export function cleanAlertText(value, max = ALERT_TEXT_MAX) {
  const text = String(value ?? "")
    .replace(/[\t\n]/g, " ")
    .replace(CONTROL_CHARACTERS, "")
    .replace(/ {2,}/g, " ")
    .trim();
  const limit = Number.isInteger(max) && max >= 0 ? max : ALERT_TEXT_MAX;
  const points = Array.from(text);
  return points.length > limit ? points.slice(0, limit).join("").trimEnd() : text;
}

// The one signal shape (spec: {sessionId, kind, text, at}, plus K1's source
// and, for a limit, resetAt). A wrong kind, source, id or time is a caller's
// bug, never data, so it throws.
export function makeSignal({ sessionId, kind, text = "", source, at = new Date().toISOString(), resetAt = null } = {}) {
  if (typeof sessionId !== "string" || sessionId === "") throw new TypeError("A signal needs the session's id.");
  if (!SIGNAL_KINDS.includes(kind)) throw new TypeError(`"${String(kind)}" is not a signal kind.`);
  if (!SIGNAL_SOURCES.includes(source)) throw new TypeError(`"${String(source)}" is not a signal source.`);
  const when = isoOrNull(at);
  if (!when) throw new TypeError("A signal's time must be an ISO 8601 date.");
  return Object.freeze({
    sessionId,
    kind,
    text: cleanAlertText(text),
    at: when,
    source,
    resetAt: kind === "limit" ? isoOrNull(resetAt) : null
  });
}

// What the mirror's raw alert means before the per-agent rules (Task X1b):
// a BEL or an OSC 9 / 99 / 777 is a basic "May need you" (R19). An OSC 9;4
// is a progress report (ConEmu's taskbar progress), never an alert.
export function genericMirrorSignal(raw) {
  if (raw === "bel") return { kind: "waiting", text: BASIC_ALERT_TEXT, source: "bel" };
  if (typeof raw !== "string") return null;
  if (/^9;4(;|$)/.test(raw)) return null;
  if (/^(9|99|777);/.test(raw)) return { kind: "waiting", text: BASIC_ALERT_TEXT, source: "osc" };
  return null;
}

export function freshActivity(status = "starting") {
  if (!ACTIVITY_STATUSES.includes(status)) throw new TypeError(`"${String(status)}" is not an activity state.`);
  return { status, turnDone: false, idleBy: null, resetAt: null, alert: null };
}

// The alert a waiting, approval or held event sets. The same alert again (same
// kind and text) keeps the time it began, so "waiting since" stays true.
function alertFrom(kind, event, previous) {
  const text = cleanAlertText(event.text);
  if (previous && previous.kind === kind && previous.text === text) return { ...previous };
  return { kind, text, at: isoOrNull(event.at) ?? new Date().toISOString(), source: event.source };
}

function signalInto(next, from, event) {
  const status = from.status;
  if (event.kind === "turn_done") {
    next.turnDone = true;
    // K4: a turn_done while waiting means the agent finished, so it no longer waits.
    if (status === "starting" || status === "live" || status === "waiting" || status === "idle") {
      next.status = "idle";
      next.idleBy = "turn_done";
      next.alert = null;
    }
    return;
  }
  if (event.kind === "resolved") {
    if (status === "waiting") {
      next.status = "live";
      next.alert = null;
    }
    return;
  }
  // waiting or approval
  if (status === "starting" || status === "live" || status === "idle" || status === "waiting") {
    next.status = "waiting";
    next.alert = alertFrom(event.kind, event, from.alert);
  }
}

// What only one state may carry: idleBy belongs to idle, resetAt to held, and
// an alert to waiting (a question) or held (the limit).
function settle(next) {
  if (next.status !== "idle") next.idleBy = null;
  if (next.status !== "held") next.resetAt = null;
  if (next.status !== "waiting" && next.status !== "held") next.alert = null;
  return next;
}

// The spec's transition table ("Session activity states"), with K4 (a
// turn_done while waiting is idle) and K5 (the manager's backstop timer sends
// idle_timer for a turn-done session too). Returns a new Activity and never
// changes the one it is given.
//   output        the first output of any kind (starting -> live)
//   counted       counted output: wakes starting, and idle only for a basic session
//   input         user input (never a hand-off write): live, alert cleared
//   idle_timer    20 s (basic) or the backstop (turn-done) without activity
//   signal        waiting | approval | turn_done | resolved
//   source_seen   the first signal of a turn_done source: turn-done from now on
//   new_turn      a hook that shows a new turn: idle -> live (never clears waiting)
//   held          a limit the agent's limit rule confirmed
//   held_cleared  the reset time passed, or the status shows the window cleared (R4)
//   exit          the process ended
export function activityAfter(activity, event) {
  const type = event?.type;
  if (!EVENT_TYPES.has(type)) throw new TypeError(`"${String(type)}" is not an activity event.`);
  if (type === "signal" && !ACTIVITY_SIGNAL_KINDS.includes(event.kind)) {
    throw new TypeError(
      event.kind === "limit"
        ? "A limit goes through the agent's limit rule, which sends a held event; it is never a signal event."
        : `"${String(event.kind)}" is not a signal kind the activity takes.`
    );
  }
  if ((type === "signal" || type === "held") && !SIGNAL_SOURCES.includes(event.source)) {
    throw new TypeError(`"${String(event.source)}" is not a signal source.`);
  }
  const from = activity ?? freshActivity();
  const next = {
    status: from.status,
    turnDone: from.turnDone === true,
    idleBy: from.idleBy ?? null,
    resetAt: from.resetAt ?? null,
    alert: from.alert ? { ...from.alert } : null
  };
  if (from.status === "exited") return next;
  const was = (...statuses) => statuses.includes(from.status);
  switch (type) {
    case "output":
      if (was("starting")) next.status = "live";
      break;
    case "counted":
      // Output alone never takes a turn-done session out of idle (spec).
      if (was("starting") || (was("idle") && !from.turnDone)) next.status = "live";
      break;
    case "input":
      next.status = "live";
      next.alert = null;
      break;
    case "idle_timer":
      if (was("live")) {
        next.status = "idle";
        next.idleBy = "timer";
      }
      break;
    case "signal":
      signalInto(next, from, event);
      break;
    case "source_seen":
      next.turnDone = true;
      break;
    case "new_turn":
      if (was("starting", "idle")) next.status = "live";
      break;
    case "held":
      next.status = "held";
      next.resetAt = isoOrNull(event.resetAt);
      next.alert = alertFrom("limit", event, from.alert);
      break;
    case "held_cleared":
      if (was("held")) next.status = "idle";
      break;
    case "exit":
      next.status = "exited";
      break;
  }
  return settle(next);
}

// The line the desktop shell reads (spec "Desktop shell changes", R21): the
// prefix and one JSON object with exactly these keys in this order. JSON keeps
// it on one line; the text is cleaned and cut to ALERT_TEXT_MAX code points.
export function alertLine({ sessionId, agent, kind, text } = {}) {
  return `${ALERT_LINE_PREFIX}${JSON.stringify({
    sessionId: String(sessionId ?? ""),
    agent: String(agent ?? ""),
    kind: String(kind ?? ""),
    text: cleanAlertText(text)
  })}`;
}

// Prints the line for an alert the person should see (K7: waiting, approval,
// limit). Anything else prints nothing. A closed stdout never throws here.
export function printAlertLine(payload, write = (line) => process.stdout.write(line)) {
  try {
    if (!payload || !ALERT_KINDS.includes(payload.kind)) return;
    write(`${alertLine(payload)}\n`);
  } catch {
    // stdout is gone (the shell quit first): an alert line is never worth a crash
  }
}

// A recording marker for meta.json (spec "Recordings in Runs"), or null for an
// unknown type. A prompt marker is label only: a prompt's text is never kept
// (R23, spec Security 5).
export function makeMarker(input) {
  if (!input || typeof input !== "object" || !MARKER_TYPES.has(input.type)) return null;
  const at = isoOrNull(input.at) ?? new Date().toISOString();
  if (input.type === "prompt") return { at, type: "prompt" };
  if (input.type === "permission") return { at, type: "permission", text: cleanAlertText(input.text) };
  const files = [];
  for (const file of Array.isArray(input.files) ? input.files : []) {
    if (!file || typeof file.path !== "string") continue;
    const filePath = file.path.replace(CONTROL_CHARACTERS, "").slice(0, MARKER_PATH_MAX);
    if (filePath) files.push({ path: filePath, added: countOrNull(file.added), removed: countOrNull(file.removed) });
  }
  return { at, type: "files", files, more: countOrNull(input.more) ?? 0 };
}
```

**5c.** A helper after `metaOnDisk`. After the closing `}` of `async function metaOnDisk(agentOsHome, id) { … }` add:

```js
// Waits until meta.json holds at least `count` markers. It polls with
// setImmediate, not setTimeout, because the activity tests replace setTimeout
// with Node's mock timers. Every test that makes an alert waits for its marker,
// so no meta.json write is still running when the temp folders are removed.
async function markersOnDisk(agentOsHome, id, count) {
  for (let i = 0; i < 5000; i += 1) {
    const meta = await metaOnDisk(agentOsHome, id);
    if ((meta?.markers?.length ?? 0) >= count) return meta.markers;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setImmediate(resolve));
  }
  throw new Error(`meta.json never held ${count} markers`);
}
```

```js
// ---- SP4: activity, alerts and markers (signals.js drives the table) --------------------------

test("signals: a bell makes an agent session waiting with the basic text, one alert frame, one permission marker and one alert line; more bells add nothing; output never clears it, user input does with a resolved frame; update sessions never alert", async () => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ agentOsHome, project }) => {
    const lines = [];
    const world = fakeWorld({ onAlertLine: (payload) => lines.push(payload) });
    const summary = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "claude", folder: project });
    const win = await attachFake(world.manager, summary.id, "w");
    assert.equal(world.manager.focus(summary.id, "w"), true);
    const pty = world.ptys[0];
    const mirror = world.mirrors[0];
    pty.emit("ready");
    world.clock = T0 + 5000;
    mirror.opts.onAlert("bel");
    mirror.opts.onAlert("9;4;1;50"); // a progress report is not an alert
    mirror.opts.onAlert("9;Build finished");
    mirror.opts.onAlert("bel");

    const waiting = await world.manager.get(summary.id);
    assert.equal(waiting.status, "waiting");
    assert.deepEqual(waiting.alert, { kind: "waiting", text: "May need you", at: "2026-10-14T09:00:05.000Z" });
    assert.equal(waiting.alerts, "basic", "a bell never makes a session turn-done");
    const alertFrames = () => win.frames.filter((frame) => frame.t === "alert");
    assert.deepEqual(alertFrames(), [{ t: "alert", kind: "waiting", text: "May need you" }]);
    assert.deepEqual(lines, [{ sessionId: summary.id, agent: "Claude Code", kind: "waiting", text: "May need you" }]);
    const stored = await markersOnDisk(agentOsHome, summary.id, 1);
    assert.deepEqual(stored, [{ at: "2026-10-14T09:00:05.000Z", type: "permission", text: "May need you" }]);
    assert.deepEqual(await world.manager.markers(summary.id), stored);

    pty.emit("\x1b[30;1Hredraw");
    mirror.counted();
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(summary.id)).status, "waiting", "output never clears waiting");
    assert.equal(world.manager.write(summary.id, "w", "\x1b[I"), true); // a focus report is not user input
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(summary.id)).status, "waiting");
    assert.equal(world.manager.write(summary.id, "w", "y"), true);
    const answered = await world.manager.get(summary.id);
    assert.equal(answered.status, "live");
    assert.equal(answered.alert, null);
    assert.deepEqual(alertFrames().at(-1), { t: "alert", kind: "resolved", text: "" });
    assert.deepEqual(win.frames.filter((frame) => frame.t === "state").map((frame) => frame.status), ["starting", "live", "waiting", "live"]);
    assert.equal(lines.length, 1, "clearing an alert prints nothing");

    const update = await world.manager.createUpdateSession({ agentId: "hermes", folder: project });
    world.mirrors[1].opts.onAlert("bel");
    const listed = (await world.manager.list({ includeUpdate: true })).find((session) => session.id === update.id);
    assert.notEqual(listed.status, "waiting");
    assert.equal(listed.alert, null);
    assert.equal(lines.length, 1, "an update session never alerts");
  });
});

test("activity (SP4): a turn-done session stays idle through redraws and status line refreshes and leaves idle only on user input or a new-turn hook; without a turn_done it is idle 120 s after its last counted output (K5)", async (t) => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ project }) => {
    t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["setTimeout", "setInterval"] });
    assert.equal(TURN_DONE_BACKSTOP_MS, 120000);
    const world = fakeWorld();
    const { id } = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "claude", folder: project });
    const win = await attachFake(world.manager, id, "w");
    assert.equal(world.manager.focus(id, "w"), true);
    const pty = world.ptys[0];
    const mirror = world.mirrors[0];
    const current = () => world.manager.get(id);
    pty.emit("hello");
    assert.equal(world.manager.markSourceSeen(id), true);
    assert.equal((await current()).alerts, "full");
    t.mock.timers.tick(IDLE_AFTER_MS);
    assert.equal((await current()).status, "live", "a turn-done session has no 20 s rule");

    assert.equal(world.manager.applySignal(id, { kind: "turn_done", source: "hook" }), true);
    let now = await current();
    assert.equal(now.status, "idle");
    assert.equal(now.idleBy, "turn_done");
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i += 1) {
      pty.emit("\x1b[30;1Hstatus line");
      mirror.counted();
      t.mock.timers.tick(1000);
    }
    assert.equal((await current()).status, "idle", "redraws and status line refreshes never wake it");

    assert.equal(world.manager.markNewTurn(id), true);
    now = await current();
    assert.equal(now.status, "live");
    assert.equal(now.idleBy, null);
    world.manager.applySignal(id, { kind: "turn_done", source: "hook" });
    assert.equal(world.manager.write(id, "w", "next\r"), true);
    assert.equal((await current()).status, "live", "user input wakes it");

    // K5: this turn's turn_done never comes (an API error, Esc).
    t.mock.timers.tick(TURN_DONE_BACKSTOP_MS - 1000);
    mirror.counted(); // counted output starts the 120 s again
    t.mock.timers.tick(TURN_DONE_BACKSTOP_MS - 1);
    assert.equal((await current()).status, "live");
    t.mock.timers.tick(1);
    now = await current();
    assert.equal(now.status, "idle");
    assert.equal(now.idleBy, "timer");
    world.manager.applySignal(id, { kind: "turn_done", source: "hook" });
    assert.equal((await current()).idleBy, "turn_done", "a late turn_done still says the turn is done");
    assert.deepEqual(
      win.frames.filter((frame) => frame.t === "state").map((frame) => frame.status),
      ["starting", "live", "idle", "live", "idle", "live", "idle"]
    );
    assert.deepEqual(win.frames.filter((frame) => frame.t === "alert"), [], "turn_done travels in the state frame, never as an alert (K8)");
  });
});

test("activity (SP4): a basic session keeps the 20 s rule and has no idle time while it waits; a resolved signal makes it live; a turn_done signal while waiting makes the session idle and clears its alert (K4)", async (t) => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ agentOsHome, project }) => {
    t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["setTimeout", "setInterval"] });
    const world = fakeWorld();
    const cursor = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "cursor", folder: project });
    world.ptys[0].emit("ready");
    const get = (id) => world.manager.get(id);
    assert.equal(world.manager.applySignal(cursor.id, { kind: "waiting", text: "May need you", source: "bel" }), true);
    t.mock.timers.tick(IDLE_AFTER_MS * 3);
    assert.equal((await get(cursor.id)).status, "waiting", "no idle time runs while it waits");
    assert.equal(world.manager.applySignal(cursor.id, { kind: "resolved", source: "title" }), true);
    assert.equal((await get(cursor.id)).status, "live");
    t.mock.timers.tick(IDLE_AFTER_MS - 1);
    assert.equal((await get(cursor.id)).status, "live");
    t.mock.timers.tick(1);
    const idle = await get(cursor.id);
    assert.equal(idle.status, "idle");
    assert.equal(idle.idleBy, "timer");
    assert.equal(idle.alerts, "basic");

    const codex = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "codex", folder: project });
    world.ptys[1].emit("ready");
    world.manager.applySignal(codex.id, { kind: "waiting", text: "Approval requested: npm test", source: "osc" });
    world.manager.applySignal(codex.id, { kind: "turn_done", text: "Agent turn complete", source: "osc" });
    const done = await get(codex.id);
    assert.equal(done.status, "idle");
    assert.equal(done.idleBy, "turn_done");
    assert.equal(done.alert, null);
    assert.equal(done.alerts, "full");
    await markersOnDisk(agentOsHome, cursor.id, 1);
    await markersOnDisk(agentOsHome, codex.id, 1);
  });
});

test("alert frames and the AGENT_OS_ALERT line (K7, K8): a line when an alert starts or changes kind, none for new text of the same kind, for clearing, or for a hold that only learns its reset time; a frame for every change", async () => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ agentOsHome, project }) => {
    const lines = [];
    const world = fakeWorld({ onAlertLine: (payload) => lines.push(payload) });
    const { id } = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "claude", folder: project });
    const win = await attachFake(world.manager, id, "w");
    world.ptys[0].emit("ready");
    const limitText = "Claude Code's plan limit was reached.";
    world.manager.applySignal(id, { kind: "waiting", text: "Wants to use Bash", source: "hook" });
    world.manager.applySignal(id, { kind: "waiting", text: "Wants to use Bash", source: "hook" });
    world.manager.applySignal(id, { kind: "waiting", text: "Has a question for you", source: "hook" });
    world.manager.applySignal(id, { kind: "resolved", source: "hook" });
    assert.equal(world.manager.setHeld(id, { text: limitText, source: "hook" }), true);
    world.clock = T0 + 60000;
    world.manager.setHeld(id, { resetAt: "2026-10-14T14:00:00.000Z", text: limitText, source: "status" });
    const held = await world.manager.get(id);
    assert.equal(held.resetAt, "2026-10-14T14:00:00.000Z");
    assert.deepEqual(held.alert, { kind: "limit", text: limitText, at: "2026-10-14T09:00:00.000Z" }, "the same limit keeps the time it began");
    assert.equal(world.manager.clearHeld(id), true);
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(id)).status, "idle");
    assert.deepEqual(
      win.frames.filter((frame) => frame.t === "state" || frame.t === "alert"),
      [
        { t: "state", status: "starting" },
        { t: "state", status: "live" },
        { t: "state", status: "waiting" },
        { t: "alert", kind: "waiting", text: "Wants to use Bash" },
        { t: "alert", kind: "waiting", text: "Has a question for you" },
        { t: "state", status: "live" },
        { t: "alert", kind: "resolved", text: "" },
        { t: "state", status: "held" },
        { t: "alert", kind: "limit", text: limitText },
        { t: "state", status: "held", resetAt: "2026-10-14T14:00:00.000Z" },
        { t: "state", status: "idle" },
        { t: "alert", kind: "resolved", text: "" }
      ]
    );

    const openclaw = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "openclaw" });
    world.manager.applySignal(openclaw.id, { kind: "approval", text: "exec: npm test", source: "openclaw" });
    world.mirrors[1].opts.onAlert("bel"); // another kind replaces it
    assert.deepEqual(lines, [
      { sessionId: id, agent: "Claude Code", kind: "waiting", text: "Wants to use Bash" },
      { sessionId: id, agent: "Claude Code", kind: "limit", text: limitText },
      { sessionId: openclaw.id, agent: "OpenClaw", kind: "approval", text: "exec: npm test" },
      { sessionId: openclaw.id, agent: "OpenClaw", kind: "waiting", text: "May need you" }
    ]);
    assert.deepEqual(
      (await markersOnDisk(agentOsHome, id, 1)).map((marker) => marker.text),
      ["Wants to use Bash"],
      "one marker per question that started; none for the limit"
    );
    assert.deepEqual((await markersOnDisk(agentOsHome, openclaw.id, 2)).map((marker) => marker.text), ["exec: npm test", "May need you"]);
  });
});

test("held: setHeld shows the limit alert and the reset time in the summary and the state frame; output and other signals never clear it; user input makes it live; the reset timer makes it idle; a hold without a reset time stays until clearHeld", async (t) => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ project }) => {
    t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["setTimeout", "setInterval"] });
    const world = fakeWorld();
    const { id } = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "claude", folder: project });
    const win = await attachFake(world.manager, id, "w");
    assert.equal(world.manager.focus(id, "w"), true);
    const pty = world.ptys[0];
    const mirror = world.mirrors[0];
    pty.emit("ready");
    const resetAt = "2026-10-14T09:30:00.000Z";
    const text = "Claude Code's plan limit was reached.";
    const lastState = () => win.frames.filter((frame) => frame.t === "state").at(-1);
    assert.equal(world.manager.setHeld(id, { resetAt, text, source: "hook" }), true);
    let now = await world.manager.get(id);
    assert.equal(now.status, "held");
    assert.equal(now.resetAt, resetAt);
    assert.deepEqual(now.alert, { kind: "limit", text, at: "2026-10-14T09:00:00.000Z" });
    assert.equal(now.idleBy, null);
    assert.deepEqual(lastState(), { t: "state", status: "held", resetAt });

    pty.emit("\x1b[30;1Hstatus line");
    mirror.counted();
    world.manager.applySignal(id, { kind: "turn_done", source: "hook" });
    world.manager.applySignal(id, { kind: "waiting", text: "Wants to use Bash", source: "hook" });
    world.manager.applySignal(id, { kind: "resolved", source: "hook" });
    world.manager.markNewTurn(id);
    t.mock.timers.tick(TURN_DONE_BACKSTOP_MS * 2);
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(id)).status, "held", "output, signals and time before the reset never clear a hold");

    assert.equal(world.manager.write(id, "w", "y"), true);
    now = await world.manager.get(id);
    assert.equal(now.status, "live");
    assert.equal(now.alert, null);
    assert.equal(now.resetAt, null);

    // The reset time passes while the Mac is awake: the reset timer fires.
    world.manager.setHeld(id, { resetAt, text, source: "hook" });
    t.mock.timers.tick(Date.parse(resetAt) - world.clock - 1);
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(id)).status, "held", "the 60 s checks see the clock before the reset");
    world.clock = Date.parse(resetAt);
    t.mock.timers.tick(1);
    now = await world.manager.get(id);
    assert.equal(now.status, "idle");
    assert.equal(now.idleBy, null);
    assert.equal(now.alert, null);

    // A hold whose reset time is unknown: no resetAt in the frame, and no timer.
    world.manager.setHeld(id, { text, source: "status" });
    assert.deepEqual(lastState(), { t: "state", status: "held" });
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(id)).resetAt, null);
    t.mock.timers.tick(24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(id)).status, "held");
    assert.equal(world.manager.clearHeld(id), true); // R4: the status shows the window cleared
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(id)).status, "idle");
  });
});

test("Review Focus 3: the Mac sleeps through the plan's reset time; the next 60 s wall-clock check, not the reset timer, moves the held session to idle, clears the alert and sends a resolved frame", async (t) => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ project }) => {
    t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["setTimeout", "setInterval"] });
    assert.equal(HELD_CHECK_MS, 60000);
    const world = fakeWorld();
    const { id } = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "claude", folder: project });
    const win = await attachFake(world.manager, id, "w");
    world.ptys[0].emit("ready");
    const text = "Claude Code's plan limit was reached.";
    const resetAt = new Date(T0 + 3 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
    assert.equal(world.manager.setHeld(id, { resetAt, text, source: "hook" }), true);
    t.mock.timers.tick(5 * HELD_CHECK_MS);
    world.clock += 5 * HELD_CHECK_MS;
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(id)).status, "held", "five minutes in, the reset is still ahead");

    // The lid closes and Node's timers stop. It opens five hours later: the
    // wall clock is two hours past the reset, and the reset timer (three
    // hours of timer time away) has not fired.
    world.clock = Date.parse(resetAt) + 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
    t.mock.timers.tick(HELD_CHECK_MS);
    const woke = await world.manager.get(id);
    assert.equal(woke.status, "idle");
    assert.equal(woke.alert, null);
    assert.equal(woke.resetAt, null);
    assert.equal(woke.stateSince, new Date(world.clock).toISOString());
    assert.deepEqual(win.frames.filter((frame) => frame.t === "state" || frame.t === "alert").slice(-4), [
      { t: "state", status: "held", resetAt },
      { t: "alert", kind: "limit", text },
      { t: "state", status: "idle" },
      { t: "alert", kind: "resolved", text: "" }
    ]);
  });
});

test("markers: kept in meta.json (the newest 500), read from memory while the session runs and from disk after it ends; a prompt marker never carries the prompt's text (R23); unknown ids are 404; update sessions and unknown types keep none", async () => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ agentOsHome, project }) => {
    assert.equal(MARKERS_MAX, 500);
    const world = fakeWorld();
    const { id } = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "claude", folder: project });
    assert.deepEqual(await world.manager.markers(id), []);
    world.clock = T0 + 1000;
    assert.equal(await world.manager.addMarker(id, { type: "prompt", text: "my secret prompt" }), true);
    assert.deepEqual(await world.manager.markers(id), [{ at: "2026-10-14T09:00:01.000Z", type: "prompt" }]);
    assert.deepEqual(await markersOnDisk(agentOsHome, id, 1), [{ at: "2026-10-14T09:00:01.000Z", type: "prompt" }]);
    assert.equal(JSON.stringify(await metaOnDisk(agentOsHome, id)).includes("my secret prompt"), false, "a prompt's text is never stored");

    assert.equal(await world.manager.addMarker(id, { type: "shell", text: "x" }), false);
    for (let i = 0; i < 505; i += 1) {
      assert.equal(await world.manager.addMarker(id, { type: "permission", text: `Wants to use tool ${i}` }), true);
    }
    const kept = await world.manager.markers(id);
    assert.equal(kept.length, 500);
    assert.equal(kept[0].text, "Wants to use tool 5", "the oldest go first");
    assert.equal(kept.at(-1).text, "Wants to use tool 504");
    assert.deepEqual((await metaOnDisk(agentOsHome, id)).markers, kept);

    world.ptys[0].exit(0);
    await ended(world, id);
    await waitFor(() => !world.manager.isLive(id));
    assert.deepEqual(await world.manager.markers(id), kept, "after the end, read from meta.json");
    assert.equal(await world.manager.addMarker(id, { type: "prompt" }), false, "an ended session takes no marker");

    for (const unknownId of [crypto.randomUUID(), "not-a-uuid"]) {
      await assert.rejects(world.manager.markers(unknownId), (error) => error.status === 404 && error.code === "unknown_session");
    }
    const update = await world.manager.createUpdateSession({ agentId: "hermes", folder: project });
    assert.equal(await world.manager.addMarker(update.id, { type: "prompt" }), false);
    assert.deepEqual(await world.manager.markers(update.id), []);
  });
});

test("liveAgentSessions and onLiveChange: copies of the running agent sessions only, in start order; listeners run after an agent session starts and after it ends; a listener that throws is logged and never stops anything", async (t) => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ agentOsHome, project }) => {

    world.manager.onLiveChange(() => {
      throw new Error("listener boom");
    });
    assert.throws(() => world.manager.onLiveChange("not a function"), TypeError);

    const a = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "claude", folder: project });
    const b = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "codex", folder: project });
    await world.manager.createUpdateSession({ agentId: "hermes", folder: project });
    assert.deepEqual(seen, [[a.id], [a.id, b.id]], "an update session is not an agent session");

    const all = world.manager.liveAgentSessions();
    assert.deepEqual(all.map((session) => session.id), [a.id, b.id]);
    assert.deepEqual(world.manager.liveAgentSessions("codex").map((session) => session.id), [b.id]);
    assert.deepEqual(world.manager.liveAgentSessions("hermes"), []);
    const profile = { command: "/fake/bin/claude", args: [], cwd: project, env: { TERM: "xterm-256color" } };
```

**5k.** Create `test/sessions-alert-line.test.js` with exactly this content:

```js
// The AGENT_OS_ALERT line (SP4, Task X1a; spec "Desktop shell changes" and
// "SP4 done when", R21, K7): a server the desktop shell started
// (AGENT_OS_PACKAGED=1) prints one line on stdout each time a session's alert
// starts, and the Rust shell (Task X4) turns it into a notification while the
// window is hidden. One real server/index.js with W1's fake agents in a temp
// HOME, started with a minimal environment like the Dock's (nothing from the
// test runner, so no host agent's variables); never a real agent. The other
// half (no line without AGENT_OS_PACKAGED) is in test/sessions-ws.test.js.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { mkdir, mkdtemp, realpath, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import WebSocket from "ws";
import { cookieNameFor } from "../server/runtime/local-session.js";
import { ALERT_LINE_PREFIX, BASIC_ALERT_TEXT } from "../server/runtime/sessions/signals.js";
import { FAKE_AGENT_NAMES, FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL, makeFakeAgentBin } from "./helpers/fake-agents.js";

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const SKIP_POSIX = process.platform === "win32" ? "POSIX only: W1's fake agents and stand-in login shell are sh scripts" : false;
const TOKEN = "test-token-alert-line";
// Node's own folder is left out on purpose: it can hold real agents.
const SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS = ["/usr/bin", "/bin", "/usr/sbin", "/sbin"];
const delay = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

async function waitFor(check, timeoutMs, what) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  for (;;) {
    const value = await check();
    if (value) return value;
    if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms waiting for ${what}`);
    await delay(25);
  }
}

// The server as the desktop shell starts it: AGENT_OS_PACKAGED=1 and a port
// the system picks (AGENT_OS_PORT=0), read back from the AGENT_OS_READY line.
async function startPackagedServer(home) {
  const env = {
    HOME: home,
    USERPROFILE: home,
    TMPDIR: os.tmpdir(),
    LANG: "en_US.UTF-8",
    PATH: [path.join(home, "fake-bin"), ...SYSTEM_PATH_DIRS].join(path.delimiter),
    SHELL: FAKE_LOGIN_SHELL,
    HOST: "127.0.0.1",
    AGENT_OS_PORT: "0",
    AGENT_OS_PACKAGED: "1",
    AGENT_OS_HOME: path.join(home, ".hermes-agent-os"),
    AGENT_OS_MANAGED_ROOT: path.join(home, ".agent-os"),
    AGENT_OS_TOKEN: TOKEN,
    HERMES_AGENT_OS_SCHEDULER: "0"
  };
  const child = spawn(process.execPath, ["server/index.js"], { cwd: root, env, stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] });
  const out = { stdout: "", stderr: "" };
  child.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => {
    out.stdout += chunk;
  });
  child.stderr.on("data", (chunk) => {
    out.stderr += chunk;
  });
  try {
    const ready = await waitFor(
      () => {
        if (child.exitCode != null) throw new Error(`server exited early (${child.exitCode}):\n${out.stderr.slice(-2000)}`);
        return /AGENT_OS_READY:(\d+)/.exec(out.stdout);
      },
      20000,
      "the server to start"
    );
    return { child, out, port: Number(ready[1]) };
  } catch (error) {
    child.kill("SIGKILL");
    throw error;
  }
}

// SIGTERM, then up to 10 s (the server's own hard exit is 8 s), then SIGKILL.
async function stopServer(child) {
  if (child.exitCode != null || child.signalCode != null) return;
  const exited = new Promise((resolve) => child.once("exit", resolve));
  child.kill("SIGTERM");
  const timer = setTimeout(() => child.kill("SIGKILL"), 10000);
  await exited;
  clearTimeout(timer);
}

async function api(port, method, url, body) {
  const response = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}${url}`, {
    method,
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "x-agent-os-token": TOKEN },
    body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body)
  });
  const text = await response.text();
  let json = null;
  try {
    json = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    json = null;
  }
  return { status: response.status, text, json };
}

// One window on the session: it acks every output frame and keeps the screen text.
function attach(port, id) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const ws = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/api/sessions/${id}/attach`, {
      origin: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`,
      headers: { Cookie: `${cookieNameFor(port)}=${encodeURIComponent(TOKEN)}` },
      handshakeTimeout: 5000
    });
    const client = { ws, screen: "", send: (value) => ws.send(JSON.stringify(value)) };
    ws.on("message", (data) => {
      let frame;
      try {
        frame = JSON.parse(String(data));
      } catch {
        return;
      }
      if (frame.t === "snapshot") client.screen += frame.data;
      if (frame.t === "out") {
        client.screen += frame.d;
        client.send({ t: "ack", seq: frame.seq });
      }
    });
    ws.once("open", () => resolve(client));
    ws.once("error", reject);
  });
}

test(
  "a server the desktop shell started prints one AGENT_OS_ALERT line on stdout each time a session's alert starts: the session id, the agent's short name, the kind and the short text as one JSON line, and nothing else",
  { skip: SKIP_POSIX },
  async () => {
    const home = await realpath(await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "agent-os-alert-line-")));
    await mkdir(path.join(home, "project"), { recursive: true });
    await makeFakeAgentBin(path.join(home, "fake-bin"), { names: FAKE_AGENT_NAMES });
    let server = null;
    let client = null;
    let id = null;
    try {
      server = await startPackagedServer(home);
      const { port, out } = server;
      const gate = await api(port, "POST", "/api/admin/execution-gate", { enabled: true, confirm: true });
      assert.equal(gate.status, 200, gate.text);
      const created = await api(port, "POST", "/api/sessions", { agentId: "claude", folder: path.join(home, "project") });
      assert.equal(created.status, 201, created.text);
      id = created.json.id;
      client = await attach(port, id);
      await waitFor(() => client.screen.includes("FAKE_ARGV"), 10000, "the fake agent's first line");
      client.send({ t: "focus" });
      const alertLines = () => out.stdout.split("\n").filter((line) => line.includes(ALERT_LINE_PREFIX));
      assert.deepEqual(alertLines(), [], "no line before the first alert");

      client.send({ t: "in", d: "bell\r" });
      await waitFor(() => alertLines().length === 1, 10000, "the first AGENT_OS_ALERT line");
      const [line] = alertLines();
      assert.ok(line.startsWith(ALERT_LINE_PREFIX), "the line starts with the prefix, so the shell finds it");
      const payload = JSON.parse(line.slice(ALERT_LINE_PREFIX.length));
      assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(payload), ["sessionId", "agent", "kind", "text"]);
      assert.deepEqual(payload, { sessionId: id, agent: "Claude Code", kind: "waiting", text: BASIC_ALERT_TEXT });
      assert.equal(line.includes(home), false, "no folder or path in the line");

      // The mirror passes at most one bell per 250 ms. Typing clears the alert
      // (no line); the next bell starts a new alert, which prints a new line.
      await delay(300);
      client.send({ t: "in", d: "bell\r" });
      await waitFor(() => alertLines().length === 2, 10000, "the second AGENT_OS_ALERT line");
      assert.equal(alertLines()[1], line);
      const listed = await api(port, "GET", "/api/sessions?live=1");
      assert.equal(listed.json.sessions.find((session) => session.id === id).status, "waiting");
      assert.equal(out.stderr.includes(ALERT_LINE_PREFIX), false, "the line goes to stdout only");
    } finally {
      client?.ws.close();
      if (server && id) await api(server.port, "POST", `/api/sessions/${id}/stop`, {}).catch(() => {});
      if (server) await stopServer(server.child);
      await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true });
    }
  }
);
```

```js
  // ---- activity and alerts (SP4; the transition table is activityAfter in signals.js) ----------------

  function clearIdle(state) {
    clearTimeout(state.idleTimer);
    state.idleTimer = null;
  }

  // A live session becomes idle after this long without counted output, user
  // input or a new turn: IDLE_AFTER_MS for a basic session, and
  // TURN_DONE_BACKSTOP_MS for a turn-done one, whose turn_done can fail to come
  // after an API error or Esc (K5).
  function armIdle(state) {
    clearIdle(state);
    const wait = state.activity.turnDone ? TURN_DONE_BACKSTOP_MS : IDLE_AFTER_MS;
    state.idleTimer = setTimeout(() => {
      state.idleTimer = null;
      dispatch(state, { type: "idle_timer" });
    }, wait);
    state.idleTimer.unref?.();
  }

  function clearHeldTimers(state) {
    clearTimeout(state.heldTimer);
    clearInterval(state.heldCheck);
    state.heldTimer = null;
    state.heldCheck = null;
  }

  // A held session with a known reset time (K3): a timer at the reset time,
  // and a wall-clock check every heldCheckMs, because Node's timers stop while
  // a Mac sleeps; the first check after the lid opens sees that the clock has
  // passed the reset time (Review Focus 3). Either one leaves held only once
  // now() has reached the reset time; a timer that fires a little early by the
  // wall clock is caught by the next check.
  function armHeldTimers(state) {
    clearHeldTimers(state);
    const resetMs = Date.parse(state.activity.resetAt ?? "");
    if (!Number.isFinite(resetMs)) return;
    const check = () => {
      if (state.status === "held" && now() >= resetMs) dispatch(state, { type: "held_cleared" });
    };
    const wait = Math.max(0, resetMs - now());
    if (wait < HELD_TIMER_MAX_MS) {
      state.heldTimer = setTimeout(check, wait);
      state.heldTimer.unref?.();
    }
    state.heldCheck = setInterval(check, heldCheckMs);
    state.heldCheck.unref?.();
  }

  // The one place an activity event changes a session. It keeps `status` and
  // `activity.status` equal, sends the state frame (with resetAt while held)
  // and the alert frames, and keeps the idle and held timers in step. An ended
  // session takes no event.
  function dispatch(state, event) {
    if (state.status === "exited") return false;
    const before = state.activity;
    const after = activityAfter(before, event);
    state.activity = after;
    if (after.status !== before.status) setStatus(state, after.status);
    else if (after.status === "held" && after.resetAt !== before.resetAt) broadcast(state, stateFrame(state));
    alertChanged(state, before.alert, after.alert);
    if (after.status !== "live") clearIdle(state);
    else if (before.status !== "live" || before.turnDone !== after.turnDone || REARM_EVENTS.has(event.type)) armIdle(state);
    if (after.status !== "held") clearHeldTimers(state);
    else if (before.status !== "held" || after.resetAt !== before.resetAt) armHeldTimers(state);
    return true;
  }

  // K7, K8: a frame for every change of the alert, queued like every alert
  // frame for windows still waiting for their snapshot. When an alert starts or
  // changes kind, also a "permission asked" marker (waiting and approval) and
  // the AGENT_OS_ALERT line (onAlertLine). New text of the same kind and a
  // cleared alert print nothing.
  function alertChanged(state, before, after) {
    if (!after) {
      if (before) broadcast(state, { t: "alert", kind: "resolved", text: "" }, { queue: true });
      return;
    }
    const sameKind = before?.kind === after.kind;
    if (sameKind && before.text === after.text) return;
    broadcast(state, { t: "alert", kind: after.kind, text: after.text }, { queue: true });
    if (sameKind) return;
    if (after.kind === "waiting" || after.kind === "approval") {
      addMarkerTo(state, { type: "permission", text: after.text }).catch(() => {});
    }
    if (typeof onAlertLine === "function") {
      try {
        onAlertLine({ sessionId: state.meta.id, agent: state.meta.agentLabel, kind: after.kind, text: after.text });
      } catch {
        // a notification must never stop the session
      }
    }
  }

  // Adds a recording marker to the session's meta.json (spec "Recordings in
  // Runs"), keeping the newest MARKERS_MAX (K20). Agent sessions only.
  async function addMarkerTo(state, input) {
    if (state.meta.kind !== "agent" || !input || typeof input !== "object") return false;
    const marker = makeMarker({ ...input, at: input.at ?? iso(now()) });
    if (!marker) return false;
    const kept = Array.isArray(state.meta.markers) ? state.meta.markers : [];
    state.meta.markers = [...kept, marker].slice(-MARKERS_MAX);
    await persist(state);
    return true;
  }

  // Tells every onLiveChange listener that an agent session started or ended
  // (the SP4 pollers start and stop on it). A listener's error is logged and
  // never reaches the session.
  function notifyLiveChange() {
    for (const listener of [...liveListeners]) {
      try {
        const result = listener();
        if (result && typeof result.then === "function") result.then(undefined, logListenerError);
      } catch (error) {
        logListenerError(error);
      }
    }
  }
```

```js
function iso(ms) {
  return new Date(ms).toISOString();
```

```js
// The SP4 summary fields that only memory knows (R22). An ended session sends
// the defaults: its alert, meter and hand-off ended with its process.
function memoryFields(view) {
  const memory = view.status === "exited" ? null : view.memory ?? null;
  const activity = memory?.activity ?? null;
  const alert = activity?.alert ?? null;
  return {
    alerts: activity?.turnDone === true ? "full" : "basic",
    alert: alert ? { kind: alert.kind, text: alert.text, at: alert.at } : null,
    idleBy: activity?.idleBy ?? null,
    resetAt: activity?.status === "held" ? activity.resetAt ?? null : null,
    trustNeeded: memory?.trustNeeded === true,
    hooksOff: { alerts: memory?.hooksOff?.alerts ?? null, meter: memory?.hooksOff?.meter ?? null },
    meter: memory?.meter ?? null,
    handoff: memory?.handoff ?? null
  };
}

// Markers read back from meta.json: only well-formed ones with a real time,
// the newest MARKERS_MAX.
function storedMarkers(list) {
  if (!Array.isArray(list)) return [];
  return list
    .filter((entry) => entry && typeof entry.at === "string" && Number.isFinite(Date.parse(entry.at)))
    .map((entry) => makeMarker(entry))
    .filter(Boolean)
    .slice(-MARKERS_MAX);
}

function logListenerError(error) {
  try {
    console.error(`Agent OS: a live-sessions listener failed: ${error?.message || error}`);
  } catch {
    // logging must never be the thing that throws
  }
}
```


insert:
```js
  // ---- signals, alerts and markers: the SP4 entry points ----------------------------------------------
  // The mirror (onMirrorAlert), the hooks endpoint and the pollers call these;
  // no route passes page input to them. Each takes only a running agent
  // session and answers false for any other (SP4 signals scope). A call that
  // can never be right (a limit, an unknown kind or source) is a TypeError.

  // The running agent session with this id, or null.
  function liveAgent(id) {
    if (!isSessionId(id)) return null;
    const state = live.get(id);
    return state && state.status !== "exited" && state.meta.kind === "agent" ? state : null;
  }

  function assertSource(source) {
    if (!SIGNAL_SOURCES.includes(source)) throw new TypeError(`"${String(source)}" is not a signal source.`);
  }

  // A waiting, turn_done, approval or resolved signal.
  function applySignal(id, { kind, text = "", source, resetAt = null } = {}) {
    if (!APPLIED_SIGNAL_KINDS.includes(kind)) {
      throw new TypeError(
        kind === "limit"
          ? "A limit goes through the agent's limit rule, which calls setHeld; it is never applied as a signal."
          : `"${String(kind)}" is not a signal kind applySignal takes.`
      );
    }
    assertSource(source);
    const state = liveAgent(id);
    if (!state) return false;
    const signal = makeSignal({ sessionId: id, kind, text, source, at: iso(now()), resetAt });
    dispatch(state, { type: "signal", kind: signal.kind, text: signal.text, source: signal.source, at: signal.at });
    return true;
  }

  // The session has a turn_done source and its first signal arrived (Claude's
  // first hook event, Codex's first classified OSC 9): turn-done from now on.
  function markSourceSeen(id) {
    const state = liveAgent(id);
    if (!state) return false;
    dispatch(state, { type: "source_seen" });
    return true;
  }

  // A hook that shows a new turn (UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse(Edit|Write),
  // the poller's busy): idle becomes live; waiting stays waiting.
  function markNewTurn(id) {
    const state = liveAgent(id);
    if (!state) return false;
    dispatch(state, { type: "new_turn" });
    return true;
  }

  // A limit the agent's limit rule confirmed: held, with the reset time when known.
  function setHeld(id, { resetAt = null, text = "", source } = {}) {
    assertSource(source);
    const state = liveAgent(id);
    if (!state) return false;
    const signal = makeSignal({ sessionId: id, kind: "limit", text, source, at: iso(now()), resetAt });
    dispatch(state, { type: "held", resetAt: signal.resetAt, text: signal.text, source: signal.source, at: signal.at });
    return true;
  }

  // The hold ended before its reset time (R4: the status shows the window
  // cleared, or Claude's own auto-resume fired). The reset time passing is
  // armHeldTimers' job.
  function clearHeld(id) {
    const state = liveAgent(id);
    if (!state) return false;
    dispatch(state, { type: "held_cleared" });
    return true;
  }

  async function addMarker(id, marker) {
    const state = liveAgent(id);
    if (!state) return false;
    try {
      return await addMarkerTo(state, marker);
    } catch {
      return false; // meta.json could not be written; the marker goes with the next write
    }
  }

  // A session's markers: from memory while it runs (and while its recording
  // closes), from meta.json after it ended.
  async function markers(id) {
    assertSessionId(id);
    const state = live.get(id);
    if (state) return storedMarkers(state.meta.markers);
    const meta = await readMeta(id);
    if (!meta) throw unknownSession();
    return storedMarkers(meta.markers);
  }

  // Copies of the running agent sessions, in start order (a resume moves a
  // session to the end), for the pollers and the hand-off.
  function liveAgentSessions(agentId = null) {
    const found = [];
    for (const state of live.values()) {
      if (state.status === "exited" || state.meta.kind !== "agent") continue;
      if (agentId !== null && state.meta.agentId !== agentId) continue;
      const profile = state.profile || {};
      found.push({
        id: state.meta.id,
        agentId: state.meta.agentId,
        agentSessionId: state.meta.agentSessionId ?? null,
        folder: state.meta.folder,
        status: state.status,
        alert: state.activity.alert ? { ...state.activity.alert } : null,
        pid: state.handle?.pid ?? null,
        lastInputAt: state.lastInputAt, // 0 before any user input (X2b's poller reads 0 as "no input")
        profile: {
          command: profile.command,
          args: Array.isArray(profile.args) ? [...profile.args] : [],
          cwd: profile.cwd,
          env: { ...(profile.env || {}) }
        }
      });
    }
    return found;
  }

  function onLiveChange(listener) {
    if (typeof listener !== "function") throw new TypeError("onLiveChange() needs a function.");
    liveListeners.add(listener);
    return () => {
      liveListeners.delete(listener);
    };
  }
```

#### Notes

1. **Spec sentences this task implements (word for word, from the spec at `548786d`):**
   - Signals: "Normalised into `{sessionId, kind: waiting|turn_done|limit|approval|resolved, text, at}`. They drive the activity states (waiting, idle, held) and the alerts. SP4 replaces SP3's `{t:"alert", raw}` with `{t:"alert", kind, text}`."
   - Transition table rows: "starting | live | the first output of any kind, or user input"; "live | idle | turn-done session: a turn_done signal. Basic session: 20 s without counted output"; "idle | live | turn-done session: user input, or a hook that shows a new turn (Claude's UserPromptSubmit or PostToolUse(Edit\|Write)); never output alone. Basic session: counted output, or user input"; "starting, live, idle | waiting | a waiting or approval signal (SP4)"; "waiting | live | a resolved signal, or user input"; "any but exited | held | a limit confirmed by that agent's limit rule (SP4, "Limit rule per agent")"; "held | idle | the reset time passes, or Claude's statusLine `rate_limits` falls below 100 %"; "held | live | user input"; "any | exited | the process ends".
   - "Output alone (a redraw) never clears waiting or held, and never takes a turn-done session out of idle."
   - Alerts UI: "Alerts clear when the agent resolves (signal) or there is user input in that session (SP3, Session activity states)."
   - Desktop shell changes: "When started by the shell (`AGENT_OS_PACKAGED=1`), the server prints one line per alert on stdout, `AGENT_OS_ALERT:<json>` (session id, agent, kind and the short alert text only)."
   - WebSocket protocol: "`{t:"state", status, exitCode, signal, endedBy, resetAt}`, where … resetAt only with held (when known)".
   - SP4 done when: "fake-agent OSC/BEL tests produce alerts and the right activity states, including the transition table: a turn-done session stays idle through redraws and status line refreshes and leaves idle only on user input or a new-turn hook; held clears after the reset time or on user input;" and "with the window hidden, an alert makes the server print its `AGENT_OS_ALERT:` line (automated)". (The Rust half is X4 and S7.)
   - Recordings: "permission asked (waiting or approval signals, with their text)".

2. **Rulings and choices applied:**
   - R19: every BEL / OSC 9 / 99 / 777 is waiting with "May need you", cleared by input or a resolved signal. X1a uses it for every agent until X1b's per-agent rules.
   - R21: one line of JSON, with the text cut to 200 characters by code points.
   - R22: each session's alert state is kept in memory and sent both in `GET /api/sessions` and in the frame.
   - R23: a prompt marker is label only; `makeMarker` drops any text.
   - R4, the part X1a owns: `clearHeld` and `held_cleared`, the reset-time timer and the wall-clock check. Reading a window as absent, below 100 or past `resets_at` belongs to X1b's `createClaudeLimitRule` and X2b's `parseStatusLine`, which call `clearHeld`.
   - K1 (`source`, `resetAt`), K3 (a timer plus a 60 s check) and K4 (a turn_done while waiting means idle).
   - K5: a 120 s backstop for a turn-done session. It adds a row to the spec table, which D1 records.
   - K7: one line per alert that starts or changes kind; a limit prints only when the session becomes held.
   - K8: alert frames only when the alert changes; turn_done travels in the state frame.
   - K20 (at most 500 markers) and K21 (`idleBy: "turn_done"` is set here, for U5's "Ready for the next message.").

3. **Copy for the owner's review at E1:**
   - "May need you": NEW SENTENCE (Q32) (R19's words, already in the contract's sentence table). It is the alert text a basic alert carries, and it reaches the notification body (X4) and the panel and toast (U5).
   - Developer-only, never shown to a person: the TypeError messages in `signals.js` and `manager.js` ("A signal needs the session's id.", "… is not a signal kind.", "… is not a signal source.", "A signal's time must be an ISO 8601 date.", "… is not an activity state.", "… is not an activity event.", "A limit goes through the agent's limit rule, …", "onLiveChange() needs a function.") and the log line "Agent OS: a live-sessions listener failed: …". They are listed so that E1's copy check can skip them.
   - No other user-visible sentence changes. What a person sees today: a bell in a session now makes its tab show the existing marker "Waiting for you" (spec words, already tied to `status` by SP3's `tabMarker`), and typing clears it.

4. **Decisions this task makes.** The orchestrator can overturn any of them; the task is written for the answer given here.
   1. Frame order: the state frame comes first, then the alert frame (both from one event).
   2. The same alert again (same kind and text) keeps its first `at`, so "waiting since" stays true. A frame is sent only when the kind or the text changes.
   3. `onLiveChange` fires for `agent` sessions only, synchronously: once right after the session is in `live` (start) and once right after its status becomes exited (end). A listener's throw or rejected promise is logged.
   4. `liveAgentSessions` lists sessions in start order. Its `alert` includes `source` (X3 needs the kind and the text). Each copy also carries `lastInputAt` (0 before any user input), which X2b's poller needs for "no input since 3 s before the call started".
   5. An exited session's summary sends every memory field at its default, `hooksOff` included, and `alerts: "basic"`. A session that has just exited but is still closing its recording reads the same.
   6. `applySignal` and `setHeld` throw TypeError for a limit, an unknown kind or an unknown source, because that is a caller's bug, not data. They answer false only for an unknown, ended or non-agent session.
   7. `addMarker` answers false when meta.json could not be written. The marker stays in memory and goes out with the next write.
   8. A hold whose reset time has already passed when the hold starts clears on the next tick (the window has reset).
   9. The `AGENT_OS_ALERT` print is wired in `getSessionManager()` (as the contract says), so `server/index.js` needs no edit. The line is still printed on the stdout of the process that `server/index.js` runs, as the spec asks.

5. **Risks.**
   - Inside Agent OS, Claude Code rings no bell by default (agent-facts 1.6), so Claude sessions mostly stay basic until X2a's hooks arrive. Hermes and Cursor rarely ring (D20, D21). Until X1b-X2b land, this task's alerts show up mostly with the fakes.
   - Every alert that starts writes meta.json (a marker), so a session that flips between waiting and live often writes often. The 500-marker cap keeps the file small (about 55 KB at most).
   - Between X1a and U5 the page's parser ignores the new alert frame (`parseServerFrame` returns null for a frame without `raw`). Nothing uses that frame today (`SessionsPage.tsx` passes no `onAlert`), so nothing breaks.
   - Node's mock timers do not move the injected clock, so the timer tests move `world.clock` by hand. `markersOnDisk` polls with `setImmediate`, because `waitFor` uses the mocked `setTimeout`.

6. **Open questions for the orchestrator.**
   - If D1 does not accept K5 (the backstop), remove `TURN_DONE_BACKSTOP_MS` from `armIdle`, so a turn-done session has no timer while live, and drop the K5 half of the second SP4 manager test.

### Task X1b: Signals from the mirror: OSC/BEL, Hermes title, Codex OSC 9, limit texts and limit rules

Today (after Task X1a) every BEL and every OSC 9, 99 or 777 that an agent's terminal sends becomes the same basic alert, "May need you", whatever the agent (`genericMirrorSignal` in `signals.js`, called by X1a's `onMirrorAlert` in `manager.js`). Nothing reads Hermes's window title, nothing tells a Codex approval from the end of a Codex turn, nothing looks for the plan-limit text on screen, and no session is ever held. This task turns the mirror's raw reports into the right signal for each agent and adds the two limit rules:

- **Codex's OSC 9 is read by its text** (ruling R14): Codex sends display text, not its type name, so "Approval requested: …", "Approval requested by …", "Codex wants to edit …" and "Plan mode prompt: …" mean waiting, and any other OSC 9 is the end of a turn. Its first classified OSC 9 makes it a turn-done session. The launch profile asks Codex for its third notification type, `plan-mode-prompt`, so its questions alert too (the profile snapshot test changes).
- **Basic alerts** (R12, R19): a BEL, or an OSC 9/99/777 from Claude Code, Cursor, Hermes or OpenClaw (and Codex's OSC 99/777) stays "May need you", and never makes a session turn-done.
- **Hermes's title** (R17): the mirror now reports OSC 0, 1 and 2. A Hermes title starting with "⚠" means waiting; the marker gone resolves that wait. Hermes's own config is never touched.
- **Limit texts on screen** (R13, R15): the manager reads the visible screen of Claude Code and Codex agent sessions at most once a second after output, and nothing else; this is the only screen reading in Agent OS, and its lines are labelled `// SCREEN READING (spec SP4)`. The reset time is read from the text.
- **The limit rule per agent**: Claude Code is held only when a limit hook or the limit text is confirmed by the other one, or by the status line at 100 % (K2); Codex only when its limit text is still on screen 5 s later with the process alive and no counted output since (R15); Cursor, Hermes and OpenClaw are never held. `noteLimit(id, evidence)` is the one entry point (X2a feeds it hooks, X2b the status line).
- **The mirror's SP4 API** for later tasks: `modes()`, `onModeChange()` (X8's hand-off waits for bracketed paste) and `screenText()` (X10's typed summary).

It owns these spec items: SP4 "Signals" (the Codex, Hermes and Cursor rows and the Claude fallback), "Limit rule per agent", and the "SP4 done when" line "fake-agent OSC/BEL tests produce alerts and the right activity states" together with "one limit signal alone never shows the banner, for Claude … and for Codex (limit text without the second observation)". It adds no PTY write, no environment variable and no argv change except the `plan-mode-prompt` filter value (H3 allows any `-c tui.notification*`). Its tests never start a real agent: pure functions, the manager with injected fakes, and the TUI fakes in a real PTY with a temp HOME.
