import {
  CLAUDE_SCREEN_LIMIT,
  CODEX_LIMIT_CONFIRM_MS,
  CODEX_SCREEN_LIMIT,
  CODEX_WAITING_PREFIXES,
  LIMIT_CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS,
  LIMIT_SCAN_MS,
  classifyMirrorAlert,
  classifyTitle,
  codexLimitConfirmed,
  createClaudeLimitRule,
  matchScreenLimit,
  parseResetText
} from "../server/runtime/sessions/mirror-signals.js";
import { BASIC_ALERT_TEXT, cleanAlertText } from "../server/runtime/sessions/signals.js";

const AGENTS = ["claude", "codex", "cursor", "hermes", "openclaw"];
const local = (month, day, hour, minute) => new Date(2026, month - 1, day, hour, minute, 0, 0);
const iso = (date) => date.toISOString();
// Thursday 2026-10-29, 10:00 in this computer's time zone.
const NOW = local(10, 29, 10, 0).getTime();
const BASIC = { kind: "waiting", text: BASIC_ALERT_TEXT, source: "osc", sourceSeen: false };

test("constants: the Codex waiting prefixes, the 120 s window, the 5 s Codex confirmation, the 1 s screen read, and the hold sentences", () => {
  assert.deepEqual(CODEX_WAITING_PREFIXES, ["Approval requested: ", "Approval requested by ", "Codex wants to edit ", "Plan mode prompt: "]);
  assert.ok(Object.isFrozen(CODEX_WAITING_PREFIXES));
  assert.equal(LIMIT_CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS, 120000);
  assert.equal(CODEX_LIMIT_CONFIRM_MS, 5000);
  assert.equal(LIMIT_SCAN_MS, 1000);
  assert.equal(BASIC_ALERT_TEXT, "May need you");
  assert.equal(LIMIT_MESSAGE.claude, "Claude Code's plan limit was reached.");
  assert.equal(LIMIT_MESSAGE.codex, "Codex's plan limit was reached.");
  assert.ok(CLAUDE_SCREEN_LIMIT.test("You’ve hit your weekly limit · resets Mon 12:00am"));
  assert.ok(CODEX_SCREEN_LIMIT.test("You're out of credits."));
});

test("classifyMirrorAlert: a BEL is a basic waiting alert for every agent; an OSC 9;4 progress report and anything that is not an alert mean nothing", () => {
  for (const agentId of AGENTS) {
    assert.deepEqual(classifyMirrorAlert(agentId, "bel"), { kind: "waiting", text: BASIC_ALERT_TEXT, source: "bel", sourceSeen: false }, agentId);
    assert.equal(classifyMirrorAlert(agentId, "9;4;1;50"), null, `${agentId}: a progress report`);
    assert.equal(classifyMirrorAlert(agentId, "9;4;0;"), null, `${agentId}: progress cleared`);
  }
  for (const odd of [undefined, null, 9, "", "ding", "9", "0;a title", "8;;https://example.test"]) {
    assert.equal(classifyMirrorAlert("codex", odd), null, String(odd));
  }
});

test("classifyMirrorAlert: Codex's OSC 9 is read by its text (R14): its four waiting starts mean waiting, any other text ends a turn, and both make it a turn-done session", () => {
  const waiting = [
    "Approval requested: npm test",
    "Approval requested by github",
    "Codex wants to edit src/app.ts",
    "Codex wants to edit 3 files",
    "Plan mode prompt: Which database?",
    "Plan mode prompt: 2 questions requested"
  ];
  for (const text of waiting) {
    assert.deepEqual(classifyMirrorAlert("codex", `9;${text}`), { kind: "waiting", text, source: "osc", sourceSeen: true }, text);
  }
  for (const text of ["Agent turn complete", "All 42 tests pass and the build is green.", "Approval requested", "approval requested: lower case is an answer"]) {
    assert.deepEqual(classifyMirrorAlert("codex", `9;${text}`), { kind: "turn_done", text, source: "osc", sourceSeen: true }, text);
  }
  // Codex's text is cleaned like every alert text: no control characters, at most 200 characters.
  const long = classifyMirrorAlert("codex", `9;Approval requested: ${"x".repeat(500)}\x1b[31m`);
  assert.equal(long.kind, "waiting");
  assert.equal([...long.text].length, 200);
  assert.equal(/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/.test(long.text), false);
});

test("classifyMirrorAlert: OSC 9, 99 and 777 from Claude Code, Cursor, Hermes and OpenClaw, and Codex's OSC 99 and 777, are basic alerts that never make a session turn-done (R12, R19)", () => {
  for (const agentId of ["claude", "cursor", "hermes", "openclaw"]) {
    for (const raw of ["9;Approval requested: npm test", "9;Hermes: approval", "99;i=cursor:d=0;Cursor needs your input", "777;notify;Cursor;Cursor is waiting for you"]) {
      assert.deepEqual(classifyMirrorAlert(agentId, raw), BASIC, `${agentId} ${raw}`);
    }
  }
  for (const raw of ["99;;Done", "777;notify;Codex;Waiting"]) {
    assert.deepEqual(classifyMirrorAlert("codex", raw), BASIC, raw);
  }
});

test("classifyTitle: a Hermes title starting with ⚠ means waiting, and the marker gone resolves only a wait the title started (R17); other agents' titles mean nothing", () => {
  const waiting = { kind: "waiting", text: BASIC_ALERT_TEXT, source: "title" };
  const resolved = { kind: "resolved", text: "", source: "title" };
  for (const title of ["⚠ fix-tests · glm-5.3 · ~/app", "⚠️ fix-tests · glm-5.3 · ~/app", "  ⚠ fix-tests"]) {
    assert.deepEqual(classifyTitle("hermes", title, { waitingFromTitle: false }), waiting, title);
    assert.deepEqual(classifyTitle("hermes", title, { waitingFromTitle: true }), waiting, title);
  }
  assert.deepEqual(classifyTitle("hermes", "⚠ fix-tests"), waiting, "the option may be left out");
  for (const title of ["⏳ fix-tests · glm-5.3 · ~/app", "✓ fix-tests · glm-5.3 · ~/app", "Hermes", "", "fix ⚠ later"]) {
    assert.deepEqual(classifyTitle("hermes", title, { waitingFromTitle: true }), resolved, title);
    assert.equal(classifyTitle("hermes", title, { waitingFromTitle: false }), null, title);
  }
  for (const agentId of ["claude", "codex", "cursor", "openclaw"]) {
    assert.equal(classifyTitle(agentId, "⚠ fix-tests", { waitingFromTitle: false }), null, agentId);
    assert.equal(classifyTitle(agentId, "✓ done", { waitingFromTitle: true }), null, agentId);
  }
  assert.equal(classifyTitle("hermes", null, { waitingFromTitle: true }), null);
});

test("matchScreenLimit: Claude Code's limit lines (R13) are found with their reset time; the usage warning, the reset notice and other agents' screens are not", () => {
  const cases = [
    ["You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm", "3:45pm"],
    ["You’ve hit your weekly limit · resets Mon 12:00am", "Mon 12:00am"],
    ["You've hit your Opus limit · resets 3:45pm", "3:45pm"],
    ["You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 11pm", "11pm"],
    ["  ⎿  Usage limit reached · limit resets 3:45pm", "3:45pm"],
    ["Usage limit reached · continuing automatically at 3:45pm · esc to cancel", null]
  ];
  for (const [line, resetText] of cases) {
    const screen = `╭ Claude Code\n> fix the tests\n${line}\n\n? for shortcuts`;
    assert.deepEqual(matchScreenLimit("claude", screen), { line: cleanAlertText(line), resetText }, line);
  }
  for (const line of ["You've used 85% of your session limit · resets 3:45pm", "Usage limit reset · Continuing automatically", "Your usage limit has reset"]) {
    assert.equal(matchScreenLimit("claude", `> hi\n${line}\n`), null, line);
  }
  // The newest line is the lowest one.
  const two = "You've hit your session limit · resets 1:00pm\n> again\nYou've hit your weekly limit · resets Mon 12:00am";
  assert.equal(matchScreenLimit("claude", two).resetText, "Mon 12:00am");
  const screen = "You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm\nYou've hit your usage limit. Try again at 3:45 PM.";
  for (const agentId of ["cursor", "hermes", "openclaw"]) assert.equal(matchScreenLimit(agentId, screen), null, agentId);
  assert.equal(matchScreenLimit("claude", ""), null);
  assert.equal(matchScreenLimit("claude", null), null);
});

test("matchScreenLimit: Codex's limit texts (R15) are found, with the reset time from ' Try again at <time>.' or ' or try again at <time>.', also when Codex wraps the sentence onto the next lines", () => {
  const cases = [
    ["■ You've hit your usage limit. Try again at 3:45 PM.", "3:45 PM"],
    ["■ You’ve hit your usage limit. Visit https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage to purchase more credits or try again at Oct 30th, 2026 3:45 PM.", "Oct 30th, 2026 3:45 PM"],
    ["■ You hit your spend cap set in your workspace. Try again later.", null],
    ["■ Your workspace is out of credits. Try again at 9:05 AM.", "9:05 AM"],
    ["■ You're out of credits. Try again at 9:05 AM.", "9:05 AM"],
    ["■ Usage limit reached. You've reached your usage limit. Increase your limits to continue using codex.", null]
  ];
  for (const [line, resetText] of cases) {
    const screen = `› run the tests\n\n${line}\n\n› `;
    assert.deepEqual(matchScreenLimit("codex", screen), { line: cleanAlertText(line), resetText }, line);
  }
  const wrapped = [
    "■ You've hit your usage limit. Upgrade to Pro (https://chatgpt.com/explore/pro), visit",
    "  https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage to purchase more credits or try again",
    "  at 3:45 PM.",
    "",
    "› "
  ].join("\n");
  assert.deepEqual(matchScreenLimit("codex", wrapped), { line: cleanAlertText(wrapped.split("\n")[0]), resetText: "3:45 PM" });
  // Each agent's own words only.
  assert.equal(matchScreenLimit("codex", "You've hit your session limit · resets 3:45pm"), null);
  assert.equal(matchScreenLimit("claude", "You hit your spend cap set in your workspace."), null);
});

test("parseResetText: a clock time is today or, once past, tomorrow; a weekday is the next one; a full date is that day; anything else is unknown", () => {
  assert.equal(parseResetText("3:45pm", NOW), iso(local(10, 29, 15, 45)));
  assert.equal(parseResetText("3:45 PM", NOW), iso(local(10, 29, 15, 45)));
  assert.equal(parseResetText("11pm", NOW), iso(local(10, 29, 23, 0)));
  assert.equal(parseResetText("9:05 AM", NOW), iso(local(10, 30, 9, 5)), "already past today: tomorrow");
  assert.equal(parseResetText("10:00am", NOW), iso(local(10, 30, 10, 0)), "exactly now counts as past");
  assert.equal(parseResetText("12:00am", NOW), iso(local(10, 30, 0, 0)), "midnight");
  assert.equal(parseResetText("12:30pm", NOW), iso(local(10, 29, 12, 30)), "half past noon");
  assert.equal(parseResetText("Mon 12:00am", NOW), iso(local(11, 2, 0, 0)));
  assert.equal(parseResetText("Thu 9:00am", NOW), iso(local(11, 5, 9, 0)), "today's weekday, already past: next week");
  assert.equal(parseResetText("Thu 4:00pm", NOW), iso(local(10, 29, 16, 0)), "today's weekday, still ahead: today");
  assert.equal(parseResetText("Oct 30th, 2026 3:45 PM", NOW), iso(local(10, 30, 15, 45)));
  assert.equal(parseResetText("Nov 1st, 2026 8:00 AM", NOW), iso(local(11, 1, 8, 0)));
  for (const odd of [null, undefined, "", "later", "13:00pm", "3:75pm", "15:45", "Feb 30th, 2026 3:45 PM", "Xyz 3:45pm", 42]) {
    assert.equal(parseResetText(odd, NOW), null, String(odd));
  }
});

test("Claude limit rule (K2): one signal never holds; a limit hook and the limit text within 120 s do, and so does either one with the status line at 100 %", () => {
  let clock = NOW;
  const now = () => clock;
  const at1545 = iso(local(10, 29, 15, 45));
  const at1500 = iso(local(10, 29, 15, 0));

  let rule = createClaudeLimitRule({ now });
  assert.deepEqual(rule.add({ source: "hook" }), { held: false, resetAt: null, cleared: false });
  clock += 1000;
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "hook" }).held, false, "two hooks are not two different signals");
  rule = createClaudeLimitRule({ now });
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "text", text: "You've hit your session limit", resetAt: null }).held, false);
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "text", text: "again", resetAt: null }).held, false, "two texts are not either");
  rule = createClaudeLimitRule({ now });
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "status", atLimit: true, resetAt: at1500 }).held, false, "the status line alone is not a first signal");

  rule = createClaudeLimitRule({ now });
  rule.add({ source: "hook" });
  clock += LIMIT_CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS;
  assert.deepEqual(rule.add({ source: "text", text: "x", resetAt: at1545 }), { held: true, resetAt: at1545, cleared: false });

  rule = createClaudeLimitRule({ now });
  rule.add({ source: "text", text: "x", resetAt: null });
  clock += 5000;
  assert.deepEqual(rule.add({ source: "hook" }), { held: true, resetAt: null, cleared: false });

  rule = createClaudeLimitRule({ now });
  rule.add({ source: "hook" });
  clock += LIMIT_CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS + 1;
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "text", text: "x", resetAt: null }).held, false, "more than 120 s apart");

  rule = createClaudeLimitRule({ now });
  rule.add({ source: "status", atLimit: true, resetAt: at1500 });
  clock += 10 * 60 * 1000; // a level, not a moment: still at 100 % ten minutes later
  rule.add({ source: "text", text: "x", resetAt: at1545 });
  assert.deepEqual(rule.add({ source: "hook" }), { held: true, resetAt: at1500, cleared: false }, "the status line's reset time wins");
});

test("Claude limit rule: the status line below 100 % clears a hold it confirmed, never one the hook and the text confirmed alone; reset() uses up the first signals and keeps the status level", () => {
  let clock = NOW;
  const now = () => clock;
  let rule = createClaudeLimitRule({ now });
  rule.add({ source: "hook" });
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "status", atLimit: true, resetAt: null }).held, true);
  assert.deepEqual(rule.add({ source: "status", atLimit: false }), { held: false, resetAt: null, cleared: true });
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "status", atLimit: false }).cleared, false, "only once");

  rule = createClaudeLimitRule({ now });
  rule.add({ source: "hook" });
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "text", text: "x", resetAt: null }).held, true);
  assert.deepEqual(
    rule.add({ source: "status", atLimit: false }),
    { held: true, resetAt: null, cleared: false },
    "an Opus or Sonnet limit never pushes the plan windows to 100 %, so a status line below 100 % says nothing"
  );
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "status", atLimit: true, resetAt: null }).held, true);
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "status", atLimit: false }).cleared, true, "once the status line reported the limit, its clearing ends the hold");

  rule = createClaudeLimitRule({ now });
  rule.add({ source: "hook" });
  rule.add({ source: "text", text: "x", resetAt: null });
  rule.reset();
  clock += 1000;
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "hook" }).held, false, "after reset() the old text no longer counts");

  rule = createClaudeLimitRule({ now });
  rule.add({ source: "status", atLimit: true, resetAt: null });
  rule.reset();
  assert.equal(rule.add({ source: "hook" }).held, true, "the status level is what the status line last said, so reset() keeps it");

  for (const odd of [null, undefined, {}, { source: "poll" }, { source: "osc" }]) {
    assert.deepEqual(createClaudeLimitRule({ now }).add(odd), { held: false, resetAt: null, cleared: false }, JSON.stringify(odd));
  }
});

Create `server/runtime/sessions/mirror-signals.js` with exactly this content:

```js
// Signals from the mirror (spec SP4 "Signals" and "Limit rule per agent";
// rulings R12-R15, R17 and R19; contract K2).
//
// mirror.js reports what a session's terminal sends, raw: "bel", or
// "<osc id>;<payload>" for OSC 9, 99 and 777, and window titles. This module
// says what each one means for each agent, finds the Claude Code and Codex
// limit texts on screen, and holds the two limit rules. Pure functions and one
// small rule object: no timers, no terminal and no process. The session
// manager (manager.js) wires them up and owns every timer.
//
// The limit texts are the only screen reading in Agent OS (spec SP4); the one
// line here that tests screen text is labelled.
import { BASIC_ALERT_TEXT, cleanAlertText, genericMirrorSignal } from "./signals.js";

// Codex's OSC 9 carries display text, not its type name (codex-rs
// tui/src/chatwidget/notifications.rs, 0.154.0): a text with one of these
// starts asks the person something; any other text ends a turn (the answer's
// first words, or "Agent turn complete").
export const CODEX_WAITING_PREFIXES = Object.freeze([
  "Approval requested: ",
  "Approval requested by ",
  "Codex wants to edit ",
  "Plan mode prompt: "
]);

// R13. Claude Code 2.1.292 says "You've hit your session|weekly|Opus|Sonnet
// limit · resets <time>" (2.1.312: "5-hour limit"), and its auto-wait line is
// "Usage limit reached · limit resets <time>". The warning "You've used 85% of
// your session limit" is not a limit.
export const CLAUDE_SCREEN_LIMIT = /You[’']ve hit your .+ limit|Usage limit reached/;
// R15: Codex 0.154.0's limit texts (codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs, and the TUI's own two).
export const CODEX_SCREEN_LIMIT =
  /You[’']ve hit your usage limit|You hit your spend cap|Your workspace is out of credits|You[’']re out of credits|Usage limit reached/;

export const LIMIT_CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS = 120000; // K2: a first signal counts this long
export const CODEX_LIMIT_CONFIRM_MS = 5000; // R15: the text must still be on screen this much later
export const LIMIT_SCAN_MS = 1000; // K2: the screen is read at most this often after output

// Codex wraps its long limit sentence itself, so the reset time can sit on
// the next lines.
const RESET_LOOKAHEAD_LINES = 2;
// <time> as the agents print it: "3:45pm", "3:45 PM", "11pm", "Mon 12:00am",
// "Oct 30th, 2026 3:45 PM".
const RESET_TIME = String.raw`((?:[A-Za-z]{3,9}\.? \d{1,2}(?:st|nd|rd|th)?, \d{4} )?(?:[A-Za-z]{3,9} )?\d{1,2}(?::\d{2})? ?[AaPp][Mm])\b`;
// "resets <time>" and "limit resets <time>" (Claude Code); " Try again at
// <time>." and " or try again at <time>." (Codex).
const RESET_PATTERNS = Object.freeze([
  new RegExp(String.raw`\bresets (?:at )?${RESET_TIME}`),
  new RegExp(String.raw`\b[Tt]ry again at ${RESET_TIME}`)
]);
const RESET_FORM =
  /^(?:([A-Za-z]{3})[A-Za-z]*\.? (\d{1,2})(?:st|nd|rd|th)?, (\d{4}) |([A-Za-z]{3})[A-Za-z]* )?(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))? ?([AaPp])[Mm]$/;
const MONTHS = ["jan", "feb", "mar", "apr", "may", "jun", "jul", "aug", "sep", "oct", "nov", "dec"];
const WEEKDAYS = ["sun", "mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat"];
// Hermes's Ink TUI starts its window title with this while it asks (R17).
const TITLE_WAITING_MARK = "⚠";

function isoOrNull(value) {
  return typeof value === "string" && value ? value : null;
}

// What a raw mirror alert means for this agent, or null:
//   { kind: "waiting" | "turn_done", text, source: "bel" | "osc", sourceSeen }
// sourceSeen is true only for Codex's OSC 9, which makes its session a
// turn-done session (spec "Session activity states").
export function classifyMirrorAlert(agentId, raw) {
  if (typeof raw !== "string") return null;
  // BEL and OSC 9/99/777 are basic alerts; OSC 9;4 progress and anything else are nothing.
  const basic = genericMirrorSignal(raw);
  if (!basic) return null;
  if (agentId === "codex" && raw.startsWith("9;")) {
    const payload = raw.slice(2);
    const waiting = CODEX_WAITING_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => payload.startsWith(prefix));
    return { kind: waiting ? "waiting" : "turn_done", text: cleanAlertText(payload), source: "osc", sourceSeen: true };
  }
  // Every other notification: the agent may need the person, and Agent OS
  // can't tell more (R12, R19).
  return { kind: basic.kind, text: basic.text, source: basic.source, sourceSeen: false };
}

// Hermes's title: "⚠" at its start means it asks; the marker gone resolves a
// wait the title started. Other agents' titles mean nothing.
export function classifyTitle(agentId, title, { waitingFromTitle = false } = {}) {
  if (agentId !== "hermes" || typeof title !== "string") return null;
  if (title.trimStart().startsWith(TITLE_WAITING_MARK)) return { kind: "waiting", text: BASIC_ALERT_TEXT, source: "title" };
  if (waitingFromTitle === true) return { kind: "resolved", text: "", source: "title" };
  return null;
}

// The newest (lowest) limit line on a Claude Code or Codex screen, cleaned,
// with the text of its reset time when that line or the two below it give one.
export function matchScreenLimit(agentId, screenText) {
  const pattern = agentId === "claude" ? CLAUDE_SCREEN_LIMIT : agentId === "codex" ? CODEX_SCREEN_LIMIT : null;
  if (!pattern || typeof screenText !== "string" || !screenText) return null;
  const lines = screenText.split("\n");
  for (let index = lines.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
    if (!pattern.test(lines[index])) continue; // SCREEN READING (spec SP4)
    const around = lines.slice(index, index + 1 + RESET_LOOKAHEAD_LINES).join(" ").replace(/\s+/g, " ");
    return { line: cleanAlertText(lines[index]), resetText: resetTextFrom(around) };
  }
  return null;
}

function resetTextFrom(text) {
  for (const pattern of RESET_PATTERNS) {
    const match = pattern.exec(text);
    if (match) return match[1];
  }
  return null;
}

// A reset time as the agents print it, read in this computer's time zone
// (where the agent printed it), as an ISO string; null when it can't be read.
export function parseResetText(resetText, now = Date.now()) {
  if (typeof resetText !== "string") return null;
  const match = RESET_FORM.exec(resetText.trim().replace(/\s+/g, " "));
  if (!match) return null;
  const [, monthName, dayText, yearText, weekdayName, hourText, minuteText = "0", half] = match;
  const hour12 = Number(hourText);
  const minute = Number(minuteText);
  if (hour12 < 1 || hour12 > 12 || minute > 59) return null;
  const hour = (hour12 % 12) + (half.toLowerCase() === "p" ? 12 : 0);
  const base = new Date(now);
  if (Number.isNaN(base.getTime())) return null;
  let date;
  if (monthName) {
    const month = MONTHS.indexOf(monthName.toLowerCase());
    if (month < 0) return null;
    date = new Date(Number(yearText), month, Number(dayText), hour, minute, 0, 0);
    if (date.getMonth() !== month) return null; // Feb 30th and the like
  } else if (weekdayName) {
    const weekday = WEEKDAYS.indexOf(weekdayName.toLowerCase());
    if (weekday < 0) return null;
    date = new Date(base.getFullYear(), base.getMonth(), base.getDate(), hour, minute, 0, 0);
    let ahead = (weekday - date.getDay() + 7) % 7;
    if (ahead === 0 && date.getTime() <= base.getTime()) ahead = 7;
    date.setDate(date.getDate() + ahead);
  } else {
    // A clock time already past today means tomorrow.
    date = new Date(base.getFullYear(), base.getMonth(), base.getDate(), hour, minute, 0, 0);
    if (date.getTime() <= base.getTime()) date.setDate(date.getDate() + 1);
  }
  return Number.isNaN(date.getTime()) ? null : date.toISOString();
}

// Claude Code's limit rule (spec "Limit rule per agent", K2): a limit signal
// (the StopFailure hook with rate_limit or billing_error, or the limit text
// appearing on screen) is confirmed by a second, different signal: the other
// first signal within LIMIT_CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS, or the status line at 100 %.
// The status line is a level (what it last said), not a moment. Below 100 %
// it ends a hold it confirmed (R4); it never ends a hold the hook and the text
// confirmed alone, because an Opus or Sonnet limit leaves the plan windows
// under 100 %.
//   add(evidence) → { held, resetAt, cleared }
//     held     the rule holds after this evidence
//     resetAt  while held: the status line's reset time, else the text's, else null
//     cleared  this status report ended the hold
//   reset()    a hold that ended elsewhere used up its first signals; the
//              status level stays
export function createClaudeLimitRule({ now = Date.now } = {}) {
  let hookAt = null;
  let textAt = null;
  let textResetAt = null;
  let statusAtLimit = false;
  let statusResetAt = null;
  let holding = false;
  let holdUsedStatus = false;

  const recent = (at, t) => at !== null && t >= at && t - at <= LIMIT_CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS;
  const answer = (cleared = false) => ({
    held: holding,
    resetAt: holding ? (statusAtLimit && statusResetAt) || textResetAt || null : null,
    cleared
  });

  function reset() {
    hookAt = null;
    textAt = null;
    textResetAt = null;
    holding = false;
    holdUsedStatus = false;
  }

  function add(evidence) {
    const t = now();
    const source = evidence && typeof evidence === "object" ? evidence.source : null;
    if (source === "hook") {
      hookAt = t;
    } else if (source === "text") {
      textAt = t;
      textResetAt = isoOrNull(evidence.resetAt);
    } else if (source === "status") {
      statusAtLimit = evidence.atLimit === true;
      statusResetAt = statusAtLimit ? isoOrNull(evidence.resetAt) : null;
      if (!statusAtLimit) {
        if (!holding || !holdUsedStatus) return answer();
        reset();
        return answer(true);
      }
    } else {
      return answer();
    }
    const hook = recent(hookAt, t);
    const text = recent(textAt, t);
    if (!holding && ((hook && text) || (statusAtLimit && (hook || text)))) holding = true;
    // Once the status line reports the limit during a hold, its clearing ends that hold.
    if (holding && statusAtLimit) holdUsedStatus = true;
    return answer();
  }

  return Object.freeze({ add, reset });
}

// Codex's limit rule (R15): it has no hook and no status line, so its limit
// text is the only signal, confirmed only when that text is still on screen
// CODEX_LIMIT_CONFIRM_MS later, the process is alive and no output was counted
// since. (A failed Codex turn sends no OSC 9, so the spec's other observation
// can't happen.)
export function codexLimitConfirmed({ stillOnScreen, alive, countedSince } = {}) {
  return stillOnScreen === true && alive === true && countedSince !== true;
}
```

```js
  function noteModes() {
    modesDirty = true;
  }

  // Runs once a write has been read, so the listener sees what xterm.js
  // applied; a change and its undo in one write are no change.
  function checkModes() {
    if (!modesDirty || disposed) return;
    modesDirty = false;
    const next = currentModes();
    if (MODE_KEYS.every((key) => next[key] === lastModes[key])) return;
    lastModes = next;
    for (const listener of [...modeListeners]) safeCall(listener, { ...next });
  }

  // Modes the serializer leaves out: the mouse encoding and the kitty keyboard
  // flags. Every handler returns false, so xterm.js still applies the
  // sequence itself; this copy follows xterm.js's own rules.
  function trackPrivateModes(params, on) {
    noteModes();
    for (let index = 0; index < params.length; index += 1) {
      const mode = param(params, index, -1);
      if (mode === 1006) mouseEncoding = on ? "sgr" : "default";
      else if (mode === 1016) mouseEncoding = on ? "sgr-pixels" : "default";
      else if (ALT_SCREEN_MODES.has(mode)) {
        // Each screen keeps its own kitty flags.
        if (on) {
          kitty.mainFlags = kitty.flags;
          kitty.flags = kitty.altFlags;
        } else {
          kitty.altFlags = kitty.flags;
          kitty.flags = kitty.mainFlags;
        }
      }
    }
    return false;
  }

  function kittyStack() {
    return term.buffer.active.type === "alternate" ? kitty.altStack : kitty.mainStack;
  }

  disposables.push(
    term.parser.registerCsiHandler({ prefix: "?", final: "h" }, (params) => trackPrivateModes(params, true)),
    term.parser.registerCsiHandler({ prefix: "?", final: "l" }, (params) => trackPrivateModes(params, false)),
    // CSI = flags ; mode u: 1 replaces, 2 sets bits, 3 clears bits.
    term.parser.registerCsiHandler({ prefix: "=", final: "u" }, (params) => {
      noteModes();
      const value = param(params, 0, 0);
      const how = params.length > 1 ? param(params, 1, 1) || 1 : 1;
      if (how === 1) kitty.flags = value;
      else if (how === 2) kitty.flags |= value;
      else if (how === 3) kitty.flags &= ~value;
      return false;
    }),
    // CSI > flags u: push the current flags, then use the new ones.
    term.parser.registerCsiHandler({ prefix: ">", final: "u" }, (params) => {
      noteModes();
      const stack = kittyStack();
      if (stack.length >= KITTY_STACK_LIMIT) stack.shift();
      stack.push(kitty.flags);
      kitty.flags = param(params, 0, 0);
      return false;
    }),
    // CSI < count u: pop; an emptied stack means no flags.
    term.parser.registerCsiHandler({ prefix: "<", final: "u" }, (params) => {
      noteModes();
      const count = Math.max(1, param(params, 0, 1) || 1);
      const stack = kittyStack();
      for (let index = 0; index < count && stack.length > 0; index += 1) kitty.flags = stack.pop();
      if (stack.length === 0) kitty.flags = 0;
      return false;
    }),
    // ESC c (RIS, full reset) clears every mode.
    term.parser.registerEscHandler({ final: "c" }, () => {
      noteModes();
      mouseEncoding = "default";
      kitty = freshKitty();
      return false;
    }),
    // CSI ! p (DECSTR, soft reset): xterm.js clears the kitty keyboard flags
    // and both stacks with it (and leaves the mouse encoding alone).
    term.parser.registerCsiHandler({ intermediates: "!", final: "p" }, () => {
      noteModes();
      kitty = freshKitty();
      return false;
    }),
    // xterm.js's own replies to terminal questions arrive here.
    term.onData((data) => {
      if (disposed || writerAttached) return;
      if (STANDARD_REPLY.test(data)) safeCall(reply, data);
    }),
    // At most one BEL alert per 250 ms: a program that prints thousands of
    // BEL bytes must not become thousands of frames for every window.
    term.onBell(() => {
      if (disposed) return;
      const at = now();
      const since = at - lastBelAt;
      if (lastBelAt !== null && since >= 0 && since < BEL_ALERT_GAP_MS) return;
      lastBelAt = at;
      safeCall(alert, "bel");
    }),
    ...ALERT_OSC_IDS.map((id) =>
      term.parser.registerOscHandler(id, (payload) => {
        // Raw: mirror-signals.js says what each one means for each agent
        // (SP4). OSC 9;4 progress reports are forwarded too and mean nothing there.
        if (!disposed) safeCall(alert, `${id};${payload}`.slice(0, ALERT_RAW_LIMIT));
        return true;
      })
    ),
    // Window titles, raw (SP4, ruling R17: Hermes marks a question with "⚠").
    // Returning false lets xterm.js set the title as it always does.
    ...TITLE_OSC_IDS.map((id) =>
      term.parser.registerOscHandler(id, (payload) => {
        if (!disposed) safeCall(titled, String(payload).slice(0, ALERT_RAW_LIMIT));
        return false;
      })
    ),
    term.onWriteParsed(() => {
      checkModes();
      markDirty();
    })
  );
```

  // A copy of the modes now (after dispose: the last ones).
  function modes() {
    if (disposed) return { ...(finalModes || DEFAULT_MODES) };
    return currentModes();
  }

  function onModeChange(listener) {
    if (typeof listener !== "function" || disposed) return () => {};
    modeListeners.add(listener);
    return () => {
      modeListeners.delete(listener);
    };
  }

  // Every row of the visible screen, right-trimmed, one line each (spec SP4:
  // read only for the Claude Code and Codex limit texts and the typed summaries).
  // translateToString(true) drops only empty cells, so spaces the program
  // wrote at a row's end are trimmed here.
  function screenText() {
    if (disposed) return "";
    const buffer = term.buffer.active;
    const lines = [];
    for (let y = 0; y < term.rows; y += 1) {
      lines.push((buffer.getLine(buffer.baseY + y)?.translateToString(true) ?? "").trimEnd());
    }
    return lines.join("\n");
  }

test("X1b limit rule, Claude Code: its limit text alone never holds; a limit hook within 120 s confirms it with the text's reset time; input ends the hold and uses up that evidence", async () => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ project }) => {
    const world = fakeWorld({ limitScanMs: 5 });
    const { id } = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "claude", folder: project });
    const pty = world.ptys[0];
    const mirror = world.mirrors[0];
    pty.emit("╭ Claude Code\r\n");
    await waitFor(() => mirror.screenReads >= 1); // the first read: nothing there
    mirror.screen = `> fix the tests\n${CLAUDE_LIMIT_LINE}\n\n? for shortcuts`;
    pty.emit(CLAUDE_LIMIT_LINE);
    await waitFor(() => mirror.screenReads >= 2); // the read that sees it appear
    assert.notEqual((await world.manager.get(id)).status, "held", "the text alone never holds");

    world.clock += 60 * 1000;
    assert.equal(world.manager.noteLimit(id, { source: "hook", text: "rate_limit" }), true);
    const summary = await world.manager.get(id);
    assert.equal(summary.status, "held");
    assert.equal(summary.resetAt, parseResetText("3:45pm", T0));
    assert.deepEqual([summary.alert.kind, summary.alert.text], ["limit", LIMIT_MESSAGE.claude]);

    await attachFake(world.manager, id);
    assert.equal(world.manager.focus(id, "w"), true);
    assert.equal(world.manager.write(id, "w", "k"), true);
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(id)).status, "live", "user input ends the hold");
    world.clock += 1000;
    assert.equal(world.manager.noteLimit(id, { source: "hook" }), true);
    pty.emit("."); // the same text is still on screen, so it did not appear again
    await waitFor(() => mirror.screenReads >= 3);
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(id)).status, "live", "the hold used up its evidence");

    mirror.screen = "> ";
    pty.emit(".");
    await waitFor(() => mirror.screenReads >= 4);
    mirror.screen = `> try again\n${CLAUDE_LIMIT_LINE}`;
    pty.emit(".");
    await waitFor(async () => (await world.manager.get(id)).status === "held"); // it appeared again, within 120 s of the last hook
  });
});

test("X1b limit rule, Claude Code: a limit hook alone never holds; the status line at 100 % confirms it with its own reset time, and below 100 % ends that hold", async () => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ project }) => {
    const world = fakeWorld({ limitScanMs: 5 });
    const { id } = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "claude", folder: project });
    world.ptys[0].emit("> ");
    assert.equal(world.manager.noteLimit(id, { source: "hook" }), true);
    assert.equal((await world.manager.get(id)).status, "live");

    const resetAt = "2026-10-14T14:00:00.000Z";
    world.clock += 30 * 1000;
    assert.equal(world.manager.noteLimit(id, { source: "status", atLimit: true, resetAt }), true);
    let summary = await world.manager.get(id);
    assert.deepEqual([summary.status, summary.resetAt, summary.alert.text], ["held", resetAt, LIMIT_MESSAGE.claude]);

    assert.equal(world.manager.noteLimit(id, { source: "status", atLimit: false }), true);
    summary = await world.manager.get(id);
    assert.deepEqual([summary.status, summary.alert, summary.resetAt], ["idle", null, null], "held → idle when the status line drops below 100 %");

    assert.equal(world.manager.noteLimit(id, { source: "poll" }), false);
    assert.equal(world.manager.noteLimit(id, null), false);
    assert.equal(world.manager.noteLimit("00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000", { source: "hook" }), false);
  });
});

test("X1b limit rule, Codex: its limit text holds only when it is still on screen after the confirm time, the process is alive and nothing was counted since (R15); a hook or the status line means nothing for it", async () => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ project }) => {
    // Each case gets its own manager, so one case's clock never moves another's.
    async function codexSession() {
      const world = fakeWorld({ limitScanMs: 5, codexConfirmMs: 40 });
      const { id } = await world.manager.create({ agentId: "codex", folder: project });
      const pty = world.ptys[0];
      const mirror = world.mirrors[0];
      pty.emit("› run the tests\r\n");
      await waitFor(() => mirror.screenReads >= 1); // the first read: nothing there
      return { world, id, pty, mirror };
    }
    async function showLimit({ pty, mirror }) {
      mirror.screen = `› run the tests\n\n${CODEX_LIMIT_LINE}\n\n› `;
      pty.emit(`\r\n${CODEX_LIMIT_LINE}\r\n`);
      await waitFor(() => mirror.screenReads >= 2); // the read that sees it appear
    }
    const statusOf = async ({ world, id }) => (await world.manager.get(id)).status;

    let session = await codexSession();
    await showLimit(session);
    await waitFor(async () => (await statusOf(session)) === "held");
    const summary = await session.world.manager.get(session.id);
    assert.equal(summary.resetAt, parseResetText("3:45 PM", T0));
    assert.deepEqual([summary.alert.kind, summary.alert.text], ["limit", LIMIT_MESSAGE.codex]);

    session = await codexSession();
    await showLimit(session);
    session.world.clock += 1000;
    session.mirror.counted();
    await waitFor(() => session.mirror.screenReads >= 3); // the confirmation's read
    await afterScan(20);
    assert.notEqual(await statusOf(session), "held", "output was counted after the text appeared");

    session = await codexSession();
    await showLimit(session);
    session.mirror.screen = "› ";
    await waitFor(() => session.mirror.screenReads >= 3);
    await afterScan(20);
    assert.notEqual(await statusOf(session), "held", "the text is gone");

    session = await codexSession();
    await showLimit(session);
    session.pty.exit(1);
    await ended(session.world, session.id);
    await afterScan(100);
    assert.equal(await statusOf(session), "exited", "the process ended first: never held, and nothing fails later");

    session = await codexSession();
    assert.equal(session.world.manager.noteLimit(session.id, { source: "hook" }), false);
    assert.equal(session.world.manager.noteLimit(session.id, { source: "status", atLimit: true }), false);
    assert.equal(await statusOf(session), "live");
  });
});

test("X1b limit rule: Cursor, Hermes and OpenClaw are never held, and their screens are never read", async () => {
  await withSessionEnv(async ({ project }) => {

  });
});

with this block (if X1a's comment words differ, replace the comment and function that hold `const found = genericMirrorSignal(raw);`):
```js
  // ---- signals from the mirror (Task X1b) ---------------------------------------------------------
  //
  // Spec SP4 "Signals" and "Limit rule per agent"; rulings R12-R15, R17, R19.
  // The mirror reports BELs, OSC 9/99/777 notifications and window titles raw;
  // mirror-signals.js says what they mean for each agent; these functions hand
  // the result to the activity state (applySignal, markSourceSeen, setHeld,
  // clearHeld). Update and setup sessions never alert.

  function onMirrorAlert(state, raw) {
    if (state.meta.kind !== "agent") return;
    const signal = classifyMirrorAlert(state.meta.agentId, raw);
    if (!signal) return;
    // Codex's first classified OSC 9 makes it a turn-done session.
    if (signal.sourceSeen) markSourceSeen(state.meta.id);
    applySignal(state.meta.id, { kind: signal.kind, text: signal.text, source: signal.source });
  }

  function onMirrorTitle(state, title) {
    if (state.meta.kind !== "agent") return;
    const signal = classifyTitle(state.meta.agentId, title, { waitingFromTitle: state.titleWaiting === true });
    if (!signal) return;
    if (signal.kind === "waiting") {
      // Hermes sends the same title twice (OSC 1 and OSC 2) and again on each
      // refresh: only the change to "⚠" is a new question, so a person who
      // already typed is not asked again by a repeated title.
      if (state.titleWaiting) return;
      state.titleWaiting = true;
    } else {
      state.titleWaiting = false;
    }
    applySignal(state.meta.id, { kind: signal.kind, text: signal.text, source: signal.source });
  }

  // Claude Code and Codex agent sessions have a limit rule. Cursor, Hermes and
  // OpenClaw have no limit signal, so they are never held (spec).
  function limitWatchFor(meta) {
    if (meta.kind !== "agent" || (meta.agentId !== "claude" && meta.agentId !== "codex")) return null;
    return {
      agentId: meta.agentId,
      rule: meta.agentId === "claude" ? createClaudeLimitRule({ now }) : null,
      holding: false, // this rule put the session in held
      lastLine: null, // the limit line the last screen read found, or null
      scanTimer: null,
      confirmTimer: null,
      seenAt: 0, // Codex: when a screen read saw its text appear
      resetAt: null // Codex: the reset time its text gave
    };
  }

  function stopLimitWatch(state) {
    const watch = state.limitWatch;
    if (!watch) return;
    clearTimeout(watch.scanTimer);
    clearTimeout(watch.confirmTimer);
    watch.scanTimer = null;
    watch.confirmTimer = null;
  }

  // At most one screen read per limitScanMs after output (K2). It trails the
  // output, so the mirror has read that output by then.
  function scheduleLimitScan(state) {
    const watch = state.limitWatch;
    if (watch.scanTimer || state.exitSeen) return;
    watch.scanTimer = setTimeout(() => {
      watch.scanTimer = null;
      scanForLimitText(state);
    }, limitScanMs);
    watch.scanTimer.unref?.();
  }

  // A limit text counts once, when it appears: on screen now and not at the
  // previous read (K2), so a line that stays on screen is one signal.
  function scanForLimitText(state) {
    const watch = state.limitWatch;
    if (!watch || state.exitSeen) return;
    const match = readLimitLine(state, watch.agentId);
    const appeared = match !== null && watch.lastLine === null;
    watch.lastLine = match ? match.line : null;
    if (!appeared) return;
    noteLimit(state.meta.id, { source: "text", text: match.line, resetAt: parseResetText(match.resetText, now()) });
  }

  function readLimitLine(state, agentId) {
    try {
      return matchScreenLimit(agentId, state.mirror.screenText()); // SCREEN READING (spec SP4)
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }

  // Limit evidence for a Claude Code or Codex agent session (spec "Limit rule
  // per agent"): { source: "hook" | "text" | "status", ... }. It holds a
  // session only through that agent's rule, never on one signal. True when
  // the evidence was taken; false for an unknown, ended or non-agent session,
  // an agent with no limit rule, or a source that agent's rule does not use.
  function noteLimit(id, evidence) {
    const state = live.get(id);
    const watch = state?.limitWatch;
    if (!watch || state.exitSeen || !evidence || typeof evidence !== "object") return false;
    if (watch.holding && state.activity.status !== "held") {
      // The hold ended some other way (input, the reset time, Claude's own
      // auto-resume): its evidence is used up, so a status line that still says
      // 100 % cannot hold the session again on its own.
      watch.holding = false;
      watch.rule?.reset();
    }
    return watch.agentId === "claude" ? noteClaudeLimit(state, watch, evidence) : noteCodexLimit(state, watch, evidence);
  }

  // Claude Code: a limit hook or the limit text, confirmed by the other one or
  // by the status line at 100 % (K2); below 100 % the status line ends a hold
  // it confirmed (R4).
  function noteClaudeLimit(state, watch, evidence) {
    if (!["hook", "text", "status"].includes(evidence.source)) return false;
    const result = watch.rule.add(evidence);
    if (result.cleared) {
      watch.holding = false;
      if (state.activity.status === "held") clearHeld(state.meta.id);
      return true;
    }
    if (result.held && (state.activity.status !== "held" || state.activity.resetAt !== result.resetAt)) {
      watch.holding = true;
      setHeld(state.meta.id, { resetAt: result.resetAt, text: LIMIT_MESSAGE.claude, source: evidence.source });
    }
    return true;
  }

  // Codex: no hook and no status line, so its limit text is the only signal,
  // confirmed only by the same text still on screen codexConfirmMs later, the
  // process alive and no counted output since (R15).
  function noteCodexLimit(state, watch, evidence) {
    if (evidence.source !== "text") return false;
    clearTimeout(watch.confirmTimer);
    watch.seenAt = now();
    watch.resetAt = typeof evidence.resetAt === "string" ? evidence.resetAt : null;
    watch.confirmTimer = setTimeout(() => confirmCodexLimit(state), codexConfirmMs);
    watch.confirmTimer.unref?.();
    return true;
  }

  function confirmCodexLimit(state) {
    const watch = state.limitWatch;
    watch.confirmTimer = null;
    const alive = !state.exitSeen;
    const stillOnScreen = alive && readLimitLine(state, "codex") !== null;
    // The text's own output is counted at most COUNTED_CHECK_MS after the
    // mirror read it, and the mirror read it before the screen read that saw it.
    const countedSince = Number(state.lastCountedAt) > watch.seenAt + COUNTED_CHECK_MS;
    if (!codexLimitConfirmed({ stillOnScreen, alive, countedSince })) return;
    watch.holding = true;
    setHeld(state.meta.id, { resetAt: watch.resetAt, text: LIMIT_MESSAGE.codex, source: "text" });
  }

```

2. **Rulings and contract choices applied:** R12, R13, R14, R15, R17, R19; K1 (`source` on every signal and hold), K2 (120 s window, a text counts when it appears, at most one screen read per second after output, status as a level, status clearing only for a hold it confirmed). Closes code-map gaps G4 and G5 for the mirror's part.
3. **Decisions this task makes** (the orchestrator can overturn any of them; the task is written for these answers):
   - (a) Hermes's ⚠ title alerts only on the change to ⚠: the repeated OSC 1/OSC 2 pair and later refreshes of the same marker do not alert again, so a person who already typed is not asked twice. Cost if wrong: a second Hermes question with no title change in between is missed (the bell, when on, still alerts).
   - (b) A hold uses up its evidence: when a held session leaves held any other way (input, the reset time, `quota_auto_resume_fired`), the next `noteLimit` resets the Claude rule's first signals and keeps the status level. Without it, a status line that still says 100 % right after the person typed would hold the session again at once. Cost if wrong: after the person types, a fresh first signal is needed before the next hold.
   - (c) Extension of K2: once the status line reports 100 % during a hold, the hold counts as status-confirmed, so the status line below 100 % then ends it. Cost if wrong: a pair-confirmed hold that Claude's status line also reported clears when the plan window drops below 100 %, which is when the limit is over anyway.
   - (d) "No counted output since" ignores counted output that lands within `COUNTED_CHECK_MS` (250 ms) of the screen read that saw the Codex text: the mirror counts the text's own output up to 250 ms after reading it, and it read it before that screen read. Cost if wrong: genuinely new output within those 250 ms does not cancel the confirmation.
   - (e) The reset time is looked for on the limit line and the two lines below it (Codex wraps its long sentence itself); the newest (lowest) limit line on screen is the one used.
   - (f) `classifyMirrorAlert` reuses X1a's `genericMirrorSignal` for every basic case (no second copy of the BEL and OSC rules) and cleans Codex's text with `cleanAlertText`; the four waiting prefixes are tested on the raw payload.
   - (g) `limitScanMs` is a new factory option for tests only (contract addition requested below).
   - (h) The screen read is scheduled by every output of a Claude Code or Codex agent session, bottom-row redraws included, because Claude's auto-wait line ("Usage limit reached · limit resets …") sits in the bottom rows.
4. **Copy for the owner's review at E1:** this task adds no new user-facing sentence. Where its results are seen: the hold's alert text uses the existing sentences "Claude Code's plan limit was reached." and "Codex's plan limit was reached." (`limits.js`); a basic alert's text is "May need you", which is X1a's constant (NEW SENTENCE (Q32), R19's words, already listed in the contract); a Codex waiting alert shows Codex's own words (for example "Approval requested: npm test"), cleaned and cut to 200 characters. That vendor text reaches the panel and, through X4, a notification body; E1 should know it is not Agent OS's sentence.
5. **Risks.**
   - Codex's OSC 9 texts and limit texts come from its 0.154.0 source; spike S3 never saw an OSC 9 live (the owner's Codex model failed every turn). E2 checks them live; a change in Codex's wording would silently turn a waiting into a turn_done.
   - Hermes's title marker comes from its Ink TUI's code (v0.22.5); its classic CLI sets no title and sends BEL and OSC 9 only when its bell settings are on (off by default), so most Hermes users get no alert at all (R17's stated cost). E2's S4 checks both.
   - A quoted limit sentence can count as one signal (R13, R15). For Codex, a quoted limit text left on screen for 5 s with no counted output holds the session; the person's input clears it.
   - Codex's rule sees a limit text only when it appears: a second identical limit message while the first is still on screen is not seen again.
   - A very narrow terminal can split the first words of a limit sentence across two lines, so the pattern does not match; at the usual widths it fits on one line.

### Task X2a: Hook endpoints and the Claude per-session settings

Today Claude Code starts in a session with `--session-id <uuid>` and, only on an OpenRouter or Local brain, `--settings <AGENT_OS_HOME>/sessions/<id>/claude-settings.json` holding the brain keys (SP3). Nothing tells Agent OS when Claude asks the person something, finishes a turn or runs into its plan limit. After X1a and X1b the session manager has the whole signal machinery (`applySignal`, `markSourceSeen`, `markNewTurn`, `noteLimit`, `setHeld`, `clearHeld`, `addMarker`, the alert state and the `AGENT_OS_ALERT` line), but no Claude hook can reach it.

This task builds that path and nothing else. `server/runtime/sessions/hooks.js` answers `POST /hooks/sessions/:id` (and `/status`, whose processing Task X2b adds) outside the cookie-gated `/api/` prefix: refused (403) outside local mode, 404 for anything that is not a live Claude Code agent run, 401 without that run's own bearer token, then the body read by the router itself (never by the 2 MB parser), at most 256 KB kept, a 204 with an empty body, and only then the work, on `setImmediate`. A body over 256 KB is dropped and still answered 204, because any other answer prints "hook error" in the person's Claude transcript (R5). The router never logs (R27). `server/runtime/sessions/claude-session.js` builds the per-session settings file: eight observe-only HTTP hooks that post to the literal hook URL of this run (R7), with the header `Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_OS_HOOK_TOKEN` filled in by Claude through `allowedEnvVars`, a 3 s timeout on every event hook and none on SessionEnd (R8, K9), and no failure option (R6). From now on Claude Code agent sessions always get `--settings` (H3, SP4) and the two variables `AGENT_OS_HOOK_URL` and `AGENT_OS_HOOK_TOKEN` (H2); no other agent, kind or portless start does. The token is new at every start and resume, lives in the manager's memory only and dies with the run (spec Security 4). The manager maps each hook event to a signal (waiting, turn done), a new turn, a label-only "Prompt" moment (R23), a limit hint (never a hold on its own), the auto-continue that clears held (R4), and the re-link of Claude's own session id, only to a UUID whose transcript exists in this folder's Claude project folder (R1). `assertSafeClaudeSettings` gets a key allowlist (R27).

It owns these spec items: SP4 "Hook endpoints"; "Hook events are hints" (re-link rule, one limit signal never holds, the 256 KB rule as R5 replaces it); the Claude Code row of "Signals" except the statusLine wrapper, the poller and the OSC fallback (X2b, X1b); Security 1 (`/hooks/sessions/*` refused outside local mode), Security 4 (the hook token), Security 5 (the settings file 0600); H2 (hook variables for Claude Code only), H3 (`--settings` always for Claude Code; the snapshot test's SP4 expectations), H5 (204, no decision, fast); SP4 done-when items 1, 2 (Claude half) and 3, and the "prompt" and "permission asked" markers of item 10. It also covers Review Focus items 1 and 2.

Its tests never start a real agent and never read the person's `~/.claude`: the manager tests run the real manager and the real launch profile on a fake terminal, one test runs W1's fake Claude Code and Codex in a real PTY, and one starts the real server with temp folders.

    | missing or wrong `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or another session's token | 401, `Connection: close` |
    | the right token, body up to 256 KB | 204; then on `setImmediate`: JSON parsed (broken or not an object: dropped), event → `manager.onHook(id, mapHookEvent(body))`, `/status` → `manager.onStatusLine(id, body)` when the manager has it |
    | the right token, body over 256 KB (by `Content-Length` or as it arrives) | 204, `Connection: close`; nothing kept, nothing processed |
    | any other path or method under `/hooks` | 404, `Connection: close` |

#### Notes

1. **Rulings applied.** R1 (re-link from `session_id` of every event, no SessionStart hook, the transcript rule; SessionEnd `clear`/`resume` registered as the hint), R2 (PermissionRequest incl. `AskUserQuestion` and `ExitPlanMode`, Elicitation, the backup Notification hook), R3 (every StopFailure is turn done; `rate_limit`/`billing_error` also a limit hint), R4 (`quota_auto_resume_fired` clears held), R5 (over 256 KB: dropped, still 204; 401/404/403 as listed), R6 (204 with an empty body; no failure option), R7 (the literal URL, rewritten at every start and resume; only the header uses the variable), R8 and K9 (3 s; SessionEnd without a timeout key), R23 (label-only Prompt moment), R27 (quiet router; key allowlist), K6 (backup waiting dropped when waiting or within 3 s of input).
2. **Spec sentences used word for word:** "Alerts start after you trust this folder in Claude" (a code comment here; U5 shows it); "Waiting for you" (the spec's tab marker words, used as the fallback alert text below).
3. **Copy for the owner's review at E1** (each is NEW SENTENCE (Q32), already listed in the contract's sentence table):
   - "Has a question for you" — NEW SENTENCE (Q32)
   - "Has a plan for you to approve" — NEW SENTENCE (Q32)
   - "Wants to use <tool>" — NEW SENTENCE (Q32)
   - "<server> asks for input" — NEW SENTENCE (Q32)
   - "Agent OS stopped this session: its Claude settings had a key Agent OS never writes." (`unsafe_settings`; reaches a person only through a bug) — NEW SENTENCE (Q32)
   - The TypeErrors in `claude-session.js`, `hooks.js` and `profiles.js` are developer-only and never reach a person. The fake's `HOOK …` lines are test output.
4. **Decisions this task makes** (the orchestrator can overturn any; the first four are also under "Contract additions requested"):
   - Every hook answer is sent once the request body has been read (and thrown away past 256 KB), not before. Node closes a `Connection: close` socket as soon as the answer is written (`resOnFinish` calls `socket.destroySoon()`), so an answer sent while Claude is still uploading reaches it as a reset, which Claude shows as "hook error" (the very thing R5 avoids). On localhost a 3 MB upload ends in a few milliseconds, so H5's 50 ms target holds.
   - The router passes a good `/status` body to `manager.onStatusLine` when the manager has that method, so X2b adds only the method.
   - An event name the settings file never registers (`SessionStart`, a missing name; only a forged post can carry one) is ignored entirely by `onHook`, before `markSourceSeen`, so it can neither turn on full alerts nor end `trustNeeded`.
   - When a PermissionRequest has no tool name, an Elicitation no server name or a backup Notification no message, the alert text is "Waiting for you" (spec words), never a new sentence. A server name is cut to 60 characters, like a tool name.
   - `MappedHook.limit.text` is the StopFailure `error` code (`rate_limit` or `billing_error`). It is evidence only: a hold's text is `LIMIT_MESSAGE` (X1b).
   - `relinkHint` changes nothing in `onHook` (the contract's list does not use it): SessionEnd carries the ending conversation's own id, and the next event carries the new one, which re-links under the transcript rule.
   - The 50 ms test takes the median of 11 posts (and every post under 500 ms), so a garbage-collection pause on a busy CI machine cannot fail it.
   - A malformed `hook` given to `buildSessionProfile` is a caller's bug (TypeError) before anything is read or written; the manager only ever passes a port from `getServerPort()` and a generated 43-character token.
   - A Claude Code run started without a port (tests, or before `listen`) has no token, so a hook post for it answers 404, as for any session that is not a hooked Claude run.
   - `checkHookToken` and `onHook` reuse X1a's internal `liveAgent(id)` (running, `agent` kind) and add only the Claude and token checks, so the "which sessions take signals" rule lives in one place.
5. **Risks.** Live facts S1 still has to confirm: PermissionRequest for `AskUserQuestion` and `ExitPlanMode`; which StopFailure `error` a real plan limit reports; that Claude's exact-list matchers (`a|b`) filter Notification and SessionEnd as the docs say; that Claude's HTTP client takes an empty 204. Claude may shorten very long folder names in `projects/` (a hash suffix in newer versions): such a folder never re-links (cost: Resume keeps the original id). A `/clear` re-links one event later when the first event comes before Claude writes the new transcript.
6. **Open questions for the orchestrator.** None blocking; the task is written for the decisions in item 4.

```js
// A small HTTP client for the hook endpoint tests (SP4, Task X2a). Not a test
// file: the runner only runs test/*.test.js. It posts the way Claude Code's
// "type": "http" hooks do (POST, a JSON body, "Authorization: Bearer
// <token>"), over a keep-alive connection so a test can tell a normal answer
// from one that closes the connection, and it times the answer.
import http from "node:http";

// postHook(options) → { status, body, headers, ms }.
//   body          sent as JSON (default {}); rawBytes (a string or Buffer) is sent as it is instead
//   path          added after /hooks/sessions/<sessionId> (for example "/status"); urlPath replaces the whole path
//   token         sends "Authorization: Bearer <token>"; authorization sends that exact header value instead
//   host          the Host header (default: Node's own, 127.0.0.1:<port>)
//   chunked       sends the body in 16 KB pieces without a Content-Length
export function postHook({
  port,
  sessionId,
  token,
  authorization,
  body,
  rawBytes,
  path: suffix = "",
  urlPath,
  host,
  chunked = false,
  method = "POST",
  timeoutMs = 10000
} = {}) {
  const payload = rawBytes !== undefined ? Buffer.from(rawBytes) : Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(body ?? {}), "utf8");
  const headers = { "Content-Type": "application/json" };
  if (!chunked) headers["Content-Length"] = String(payload.length);
  if (host !== undefined) headers.Host = host;
  if (authorization !== undefined) headers.Authorization = authorization;
  else if (token !== undefined && token !== null) headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
  const agent = new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 1 });
  const started = process.hrtime.bigint();
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    let settled = false;
    const finish = (error, value) => {
      if (settled) return;
      settled = true;
      agent.destroy();
      if (error) reject(error);
      else resolve(value);
    };
    const request = http.request(
      { host: "127.0.0.1", port, method, path: urlPath ?? `/hooks/sessions/${sessionId}${suffix}`, headers, agent },
      (response) => {
        const chunks = [];
        response.on("data", (chunk) => chunks.push(chunk));
        response.on("end", () =>
          finish(null, {
            status: response.statusCode,
            body: Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8"),
            headers: response.headers,
            ms: Number(process.hrtime.bigint() - started) / 1e6
          })
        );
        response.on("error", (error) => finish(error));
      }
    );
    request.setTimeout(timeoutMs, () => request.destroy(new Error(`postHook: no answer within ${timeoutMs} ms`)));
    request.on("error", (error) => finish(error));
    if (chunked) {
      for (let at = 0; at < payload.length; at += 16 * 1024) request.write(payload.subarray(at, at + 16 * 1024));
      request.end();
    } else {
      request.end(payload);
    }
  });
}
```

const V1_UUID = "3b4c5d6e-7f8a-1b9c-8d0e-1f2a3b4c5d6e";
const TOKEN_A = `tokenA_${"a".repeat(36)}`;
const TOKEN_B = `tokenB_${"b".repeat(36)}`;
const CLAUDE_ID = "8d3e7f10-2b4c-4d5e-8f60-718293a4b5c6";
const T0 = Date.parse("2026-10-29T09:00:00.000Z");
const UNSAFE_SETTINGS_MESSAGE = "Agent OS stopped this session: its Claude settings had a key Agent OS never writes.";
const MODE_KEYS = {
  DEMO_PUBLIC: undefined,
  HERMES_AGENT_OS_DEMO_PUBLIC: undefined,
  HERMES_AGENT_OS_REQUIRE_AUTH: undefined,
  HERMES_AGENT_OS_PUBLIC_MODE: undefined
};
const NOT_LOCAL_MODES = [
  { DEMO_PUBLIC: "1" },
  { HERMES_AGENT_OS_DEMO_PUBLIC: "yes" },
  { HERMES_AGENT_OS_REQUIRE_AUTH: "1" },
  { HERMES_AGENT_OS_PUBLIC_MODE: "1" }
];
const EMPTY_MAP = {
  signals: [],
  limit: null,
  newTurn: false,
  promptMarker: false,
  refreshChanges: false,
  heldCleared: false,
  relinkHint: false
};

const delay = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

async function waitFor(check, timeoutMs = 10000, what = "a condition") {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  for (;;) {
    const value = await check();
    if (value) return value;
    if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms waiting for ${what}`);
    await delay(20);
  }
}

async function withEnv(vars, fn) {
  const previous = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(vars)) previous[key] = process.env[key];
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(vars)) {
    if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
    else process.env[key] = String(value);
  }
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(previous)) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[key];
      else process.env[key] = value;
    }
  }
}

// Every console method, recorded instead of printed, so a test can prove the
// hooks router wrote no log line (R27).
function spyConsole() {
  const lines = [];
  const saved = {};
  for (const name of ["log", "info", "warn", "error", "debug"]) {
    saved[name] = console[name];
    console[name] = (...args) => lines.push(`${name}: ${args.map(String).join(" ")}`);
  }
  return {
    lines,
    restore() {
      Object.assign(console, saved);
    }
  };
}

// What hooks.js needs from the manager: SESSION_A and SESSION_B are live Claude
// Code runs with their own tokens; nothing else is. `replied` records whether
// the event's 204 had been written when the event was processed.
function stubManager() {
  const tokens = new Map([
    [SESSION_A, TOKEN_A],
    [SESSION_B, TOKEN_B]
  ]);
  const stub = {
    lastRes: null,
    hooks: [],
    statuses: [],
    checkHookToken(id, presented) {
      if (!tokens.has(id)) return "unknown_session";
      return presented === tokens.get(id) ? "ok" : "bad_token";
    },
    onHook(id, mapped) {
      stub.hooks.push({ id, mapped, replied: stub.lastRes?.writableEnded === true && stub.lastRes.statusCode === 204 });
    },
    onStatusLine(id, json) {
      stub.statuses.push({ id, json });
    }
  };
  return stub;
}

// The hooks router mounted the way server/index.js mounts it: after the Host
// allowlist and the Origin check, before a JSON parser (a small one when a
// test asks, so a body that reached it would show), with a route and an error
// handler behind it that record anything a hook request should never reach.
// isLocal: null leaves the router's own default (the real local-mode check).
async function startApp(manager, { isLocal = () => true, jsonLimit = "2mb" } = {}) {
  const app = express();
  app.set("case sensitive routing", true);
  const reached = [];
  app.use(hostAllowlistMiddleware());
  app.use(originCheckMiddleware());
  app.use((_req, res, next) => {
    if (Object.hasOwn(manager, "lastRes")) manager.lastRes = res;
    next();
  });
  app.use("/hooks", createHooksRouter(isLocal === null ? { manager } : { manager, isLocal }));
  app.use(express.json({ limit: jsonLimit }));
  app.use((req, res) => {
    reached.push(`${req.method} ${req.path}`);
    res.status(418).end();
  });
  app.use((error, _req, res, _next) => {
    reached.push(error?.type || error?.message || "error");
    res.status(500).end();
  });
  const server = await new Promise((resolve) => {
    const listening = app.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => resolve(listening));
  });
  return {
    port: server.address().port,
    reached,
    close: () =>
      new Promise((resolve) => {
        server.closeAllConnections?.();
        server.close(() => resolve());
      })
  };
}

// A Stop event padded to exactly `bytes` bytes of JSON.
function bodyOfSize(bytes) {
  const body = { hook_event_name: "Stop", session_id: CLAUDE_ID, pad: "" };
  body.pad = "x".repeat(bytes - Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(body)));
  const raw = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(body));
  assert.equal(raw.length, bytes);
  return raw;
}

// The contract's settings file ("The per-session Claude settings file"), written out by hand.
function expectedSettings(hookUrl) {
  const http = (timeout) => ({
    type: "http",
    url: hookUrl,
    ...(timeout ? { timeout } : {}),
    headers: { Authorization: "Bearer $AGENT_OS_HOOK_TOKEN" },
    allowedEnvVars: ["AGENT_OS_HOOK_TOKEN"]
  });
  return {
    hooks: {
      PermissionRequest: [{ hooks: [http(3)] }],
      Elicitation: [{ hooks: [http(3)] }],
      Notification: [{ matcher: "permission_prompt|elicitation_dialog|elicitation_url_dialog|quota_auto_resume_fired", hooks: [http(3)] }],
      Stop: [{ hooks: [http(3)] }],
      StopFailure: [{ hooks: [http(3)] }],
      UserPromptSubmit: [{ hooks: [http(3)] }],
      PostToolUse: [{ matcher: "Edit|Write", hooks: [http(3)] }],
      SessionEnd: [{ matcher: "clear|resume", hooks: [http(null)] }]
    }
  };
}

// Comments out of a source file, so a word in an explanation never counts.
function codeOnly(source) {
  return source
    .replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, "")
    .replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, "")
    .replace(/\s\/\/ .*$/gm, "");
}

test("bearerToken: the token after \"Bearer \" (any case of the word, exactly one space), else null", () => {
  assert.equal(bearerToken(`Bearer ${TOKEN_A}`), TOKEN_A);
  assert.equal(bearerToken(`bearer ${TOKEN_A}`), TOKEN_A);
  assert.equal(bearerToken(`BEARER ${TOKEN_A}`), TOKEN_A);
  for (const bad of [undefined, null, "", "Bearer", "Bearer ", `Bearer  ${TOKEN_A}`, `Basic ${TOKEN_A}`, TOKEN_A, `Bearer ${TOKEN_A} extra`, `Bearer\t${TOKEN_A}`, ` Bearer ${TOKEN_A}`, 42, [`Bearer ${TOKEN_A}`]]) {
    assert.equal(bearerToken(bad), null, JSON.stringify(bad));
  }
});

test("mapHookEvent: each Claude Code event becomes signals and hints; a prompt and a written file's content are never copied (R2, R3, R4, R23)", () => {
  const map = (body) => mapHookEvent({ session_id: CLAUDE_ID, transcript_path: "/t.jsonl", cwd: "/p", ...body });
  const waiting = (text, backup = false) => ({ kind: "waiting", text, backup });
  const turnDone = { kind: "turn_done", text: "", backup: false };
  const cases = [
    [{ hook_event_name: "PermissionRequest", tool_name: "AskUserQuestion", tool_input: { questions: [] } }, { signals: [waiting("Has a question for you")] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "PermissionRequest", tool_name: "ExitPlanMode", tool_input: { plan: "1. do it" } }, { signals: [waiting("Has a plan for you to approve")] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "PermissionRequest", tool_name: "Bash", tool_input: { command: "rm -rf build" } }, { signals: [waiting("Wants to use Bash")] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "PermissionRequest", tool_name: "mcp__github__create_issue" }, { signals: [waiting("Wants to use mcp__github__create_issue")] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "PermissionRequest", tool_name: "T".repeat(100) }, { signals: [waiting(`Wants to use ${"T".repeat(60)}`)] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "PermissionRequest", tool_name: "Bad\u001b[31m\nname" }, { signals: [waiting("Wants to use Bad[31m name")] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "PermissionRequest" }, { signals: [waiting("Waiting for you")] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "PermissionRequest", tool_name: { name: "Bash" } }, { signals: [waiting("Waiting for you")] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "Elicitation", mcp_server_name: "github", message: "Pick a repository", mode: "form" }, { signals: [waiting("github asks for input")] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "Elicitation", message: "?" }, { signals: [waiting("Waiting for you")] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "Notification", notification_type: "permission_prompt", message: "Claude needs your permission to use Bash" }, { signals: [waiting("Claude needs your permission to use Bash", true)] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "Notification", notification_type: "elicitation_dialog", message: "github needs your input" }, { signals: [waiting("github needs your input", true)] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "Notification", notification_type: "elicitation_url_dialog", message: "Open a link" }, { signals: [waiting("Open a link", true)] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "Notification", notification_type: "permission_prompt", message: "" }, { signals: [waiting("Waiting for you", true)] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "Notification", notification_type: "quota_auto_resume_fired", message: "Continuing" }, { heldCleared: true }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "Notification", notification_type: "quota_auto_resume_stale", message: "x" }, {}],
    [{ hook_event_name: "Notification", notification_type: "idle_prompt", message: "Claude is waiting for your input" }, {}],
    [{ hook_event_name: "Stop", last_assistant_message: "Done." }, { signals: [turnDone] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "StopFailure", error: "overloaded" }, { signals: [turnDone] }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "StopFailure", error: "rate_limit", last_assistant_message: "API Error: Rate limit reached" }, { signals: [turnDone], limit: { text: "rate_limit" } }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "StopFailure", error: "billing_error" }, { signals: [turnDone], limit: { text: "billing_error" } }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "UserPromptSubmit", prompt: "PRIVATE-PROMPT-TEXT" }, { newTurn: true, promptMarker: true }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "PostToolUse", tool_name: "Write", tool_input: { file_path: "/p/a.txt", content: "PRIVATE-FILE-CONTENT" }, tool_response: {} }, { newTurn: true, refreshChanges: true }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "SessionEnd", reason: "clear" }, { relinkHint: true }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "SessionEnd", reason: "resume" }, { relinkHint: true }],
    [{ hook_event_name: "SessionEnd", reason: "prompt_input_exit" }, {}],
    [{ hook_event_name: "SessionStart", source: "startup" }, {}],
    [{ hook_event_name: "PreToolUse", tool_name: "Bash" }, {}]
  ];
  for (const [body, expected] of cases) {
    const mapped = map(body);
    assert.deepEqual(mapped, { event: body.hook_event_name, claudeSessionId: CLAUDE_ID, ...EMPTY_MAP, ...expected }, JSON.stringify(body));
    assert.ok(!JSON.stringify(mapped).includes("PRIVATE-"), `${body.hook_event_name}: a prompt or a file's content is never copied`);
