### Task X4: Desktop notifications in the Rust shell

Today the desktop shell (`desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`) reads the server's stdout only for the ready line, and it reads it with `BufRead::lines().map_while(Result::ok)` (main.rs:259 for stderr, :270 for stdout), which stops at the first line that is not UTF-8. After that nothing drains the pipe, so a chatty server would block on a full pipe (gap G9). The shell has no notification plugin (code-map 13). From Task X1a on, the packaged server prints one `AGENT_OS_ALERT:<json>` line per alert. This task makes the shell turn each of those lines into a desktop notification, but only when the person is not looking at the window, as the spec asks:

- **The plugin, Rust only (R20):** the crate `tauri-plugin-notification = "=2.7.0"` (exact pin; official Tauri, `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`; 2.8.0 is one day old), registered next to the dialog plugin. No npm package, no `notification:*` permission for the page, and `capabilities/default.json` does not change.
- **A byte-safe reader (R21):** a small helper, `read_lines_lossy`, reads each pipe with `read_until(b'\n')` and decodes with `String::from_utf8_lossy`, so a bad byte becomes "�" and the reader goes on. Both pipes use it (stdout is R21; stderr has the same bug, see "Contract additions requested" 1).
- **Alert lines:** `parse_alert_line` reads the line; on the main thread, `notify_alert` checks the `main` window and shows the notification only when `should_notify(visible, focused)` (hidden, minimized or behind another app). Title: "<agent> is waiting for you" or "<agent>'s plan ran out"; body: the server's alert text.
- **A click shows the window:** the plugin's Rust `on_action` handler (a click is the action `"tap"`) calls the existing `show_main_window`. It is registered in `setup` before the server starts, because the plugin reports clicks only for notifications shown after a handler exists.
- **Tests:** 9 new Rust unit tests (`cargo test`, 19 → 28) for the line parsing, the title, the window rule, the click rule and the byte-safe reader; 5 new tests in `test/release-config.test.js` (30 → 35) for the crate pin, the lock, the registration, no page package or permission, the reader, the wiring, and that the shell and the server (X1a's `alertLine`) agree on the exact line.

The real notification (and macOS asking once whether Agent OS may show notifications) is checked live in Task E2, spike S7, with the built app; it cannot be checked by a unit test.

**Rust words used below (for the owner):** `Option` is "a value or nothing" (`Some(x)` or `None`); `?` after something that may be `None` means "give up and return `None` here". `|line| { … }` is a small unnamed function (a closure), like `(line) => { … }` in JavaScript. `r#"…"#` is a raw string: the text exactly as written, quotes and backslashes included. `#[allow(dead_code)]` tells the compiler a field that is never read is on purpose. `#[cfg(test)]` code only exists when running `cargo test`.

When started by the shell (`AGENT_OS_PACKAGED=1`), the server prints one line per alert on stdout, `AGENT_OS_ALERT:<json>` (session id, agent, kind and the short alert text only). The shell already reads the server's stdout for `AGENT_OS_READY:<port>`; it shows the notification when the window is hidden or not focused." Done when: "with the window hidden, an alert makes the server print its `AGENT_OS_ALERT:` line (automated), and the Rust shell shows the notification (live check under S7);"

3. **"Clicking it shows the window"** comes from this task's brief, not from a spec sentence. It adds no visible text. Without it a click on the notification would only bring the app forward (macOS activates the app), leaving a window that was closed with the red button hidden.
4. **New user-visible sentences (R28, owner review at E1):** the two notification titles, "<agent> is waiting for you" (waiting and approval) NEW SENTENCE (Q32) and "<agent>'s plan ran out" (limit) NEW SENTENCE (Q32). `<agent>` is the server's short name ("Claude Code", "Codex", "Cursor", "Hermes", "OpenClaw"; only Claude Code and Codex are ever held). The body is the alert text the server sends ("May need you", "Wants to use <tool>", "Claude Code's plan limit was reached.", …), whose sentences are marked in X1a, X1b and X2a; X4 adds no body text and shows no body when the text is empty. The two stderr lines ("Agent OS couldn't show a notification: …", "Agent OS couldn't listen for notification clicks: …") go to the app's stderr only and are never shown to the person; they are listed here for completeness.
5. **R21, applied to both pipes.** The stdout reader is the ruling. The stderr reader at main.rs:259 has the same bug (one non-UTF-8 line ends it; then a server writing to stderr fills the pipe: on Linux, where Node writes to pipes synchronously, the server would freeze). The fix is the same one helper call, so this task applies it to stderr too and asks the orchestrator to confirm ("Contract additions requested" 1). If the orchestrator declines, keep stderr's old loop and drop the `read_lines_lossy(BufReader::new(stderr), ` assertion from the release-config test.
6. **Why the window check runs on the main thread.** `is_visible()` and `is_focused()` called from the reader thread would wait for the main thread to answer. While the main thread is busy (a system dialog, for example) the reader would stop draining the server's output. `run_on_main_thread` only posts the work, so the reader never waits; on the main thread the two checks are answered at once (Interfaces, Tauri).
7. **What the plugin does around this (owner FYI, not changeable without a fork):**
   - Once a click handler exists, macOS and Windows keep one small waiting thread per shown notification until the person clicks or dismisses it (`show_tracked`/`wait`, desktop.rs:474-485 and 718-730). K7 prints one line per transition into an alert, so this stays a handful of threads.
   - A notification stays in Notification Center after the person answers in the terminal; the plugin cannot remove one on macOS or Windows (`remove_active` does nothing there, desktop.rs:226-231). Clicking an old one just shows the window.
   - Windows reports a click only while the toast is on screen, not from the Action Center; Linux reports it only when the notification server supports it.
   - The plugin injects a small script into every page the window loads that replaces `window.Notification` and asks the plugin whether notifications are allowed. The page has no `notification:*` permission (R20), so that call is refused and the desktop window's console shows one "not allowed" line per page load. This is expected; it also proves no page script can send a notification. E1 and E2 must not count that console line as a regression ("Contract additions requested" 7).
   - In `npm run desktop:dev` notifications show as Terminal's (the plugin uses `com.apple.Terminal` in dev builds); S7 uses the built app, launched from an `env -i` shell (SP3 S7 finding A).
8. **Fresh crates (owner FYI, R20):** `tauri-plugin-notification` 2.7.0 was published 2026-10-14; it needs `tauri ^2.12` (locked 2.12.1) and the build dependency `tauri-plugin ^2.7.1` (locked 2.7.1), so no locked version changes. It brings `notify-rust` 4.18 (macOS: `mac-notification-sys`, which compiles one small Objective-C file with the Xcode command line tools, already needed for any Tauri build; Windows: a WinRT toast crate; Linux: `zbus` 5, already in the lock at 5.19.0), `rand` 0.9 and `serde_repr` (already locked). `Cargo.lock` lists every platform's crates, so Windows and Linux crates appear in it on a Mac too.
9. **Rulings applied:** R20 (crate only, exact pin, no page package or capability), R21 (byte-safe reader; lines are one line of JSON with text at most 200 characters, and the shell cuts to 200 characters again), K7 (one line per transition, no de-duplication in the shell), R28 (Q32 marks), R30 (Critical/Important findings fixed in this task, Minors logged). K17 is U5's. Global Constraints: "Packages", "Copy", "Owner rules, workers" (never commit, never read `~/.tauri/agent-os.key`), "Verify, desktop (X4)".

```js
  const between = (from, to) => {

    assert.ok(start >= 0 && end > start, `main.rs has ${from} and, after it, ${to}`);
    return main.slice(start, end);

    }

    assert.doesNotMatch(capability.description, /notification/i, "the description claims no notification IPC for the page");
```

```rust
/// What the server prints on stdout once it is listening.
const READY_LINE_PREFIX: &str = "AGENT_OS_READY:";
/// What the server prints on stdout when a session needs the person (only when it runs with
/// AGENT_OS_PACKAGED=1; server/runtime/sessions/signals.js, printAlertLine): this prefix, then
/// one line of JSON, {"sessionId","agent","kind","text"}.
const ALERT_LINE_PREFIX: &str = "AGENT_OS_ALERT:";
/// The alert kinds that raise a notification (the server prints no others).
const ALERT_KINDS: [&str; 3] = ["waiting", "approval", "limit"];
/// The longest alert text a notification shows, in characters (the server cuts it the same way).
const ALERT_TEXT_MAX: usize = 200;
/// The action the notification plugin reports for a click on the notification itself.
const NOTIFICATION_TAP: &str = "tap";
```

(b) Insert right after `parse_ready_line` (after its closing `}`, the line after `    line.strip_prefix(READY_LINE_PREFIX)?.trim().parse().ok()`), with one blank line before:

```rust
/// One alert from the server, read from its `AGENT_OS_ALERT:` line.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
struct AlertNote {
    /// Not shown in the notification; a line without one is not an alert.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    session_id: String,
    agent: String,
    kind: String,
    text: String,
}

/// Reads one `AGENT_OS_ALERT:<json>` line. Anything else is not an alert: another line, broken
/// JSON, a missing or non-string field, an empty session id or agent, or a kind other than
/// waiting, approval or limit. The text is cut to 200 characters (characters, not bytes, so no
/// letter is split).
fn parse_alert_line(line: &str) -> Option<AlertNote> {
    let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(line.strip_prefix(ALERT_LINE_PREFIX)?).ok()?;
    let field = |name: &str| -> Option<String> { value.get(name)?.as_str().map(str::to_owned) };
    let session_id = field("sessionId")?;
    let agent = field("agent")?;
    let kind = field("kind")?;
    let text = field("text")?;
    if session_id.is_empty() || agent.trim().is_empty() || !ALERT_KINDS.contains(&kind.as_str()) {
        return None;
    }
    Some(AlertNote {
        session_id,
        agent,
        kind,
        text: text.chars().take(ALERT_TEXT_MAX).collect(),
    })
}

/// The notification's title (both forms are new sentences for the owner's review, SP4 Q32).
fn alert_title(kind: &str, agent: &str) -> Option<String> {
    match kind {
        "waiting" | "approval" => Some(format!("{agent} is waiting for you")),
        "limit" => Some(format!("{agent}'s plan ran out")),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// A notification only when the person is not looking at the window (spec SP4, Alerts UI): it is
/// hidden (macOS: closed with the red button, or Agent OS hidden), minimized, or another app is in
/// front. While the window is in front, the page itself shows the alert.
fn should_notify(visible: bool, focused: bool) -> bool {
    !visible || !focused
}

/// A click on the notification itself brings the window back. Agent OS's notifications carry no
/// action buttons, so a click is the only action that can arrive.
fn notification_click_shows_window(action_id: &str) -> bool {
    action_id == NOTIFICATION_TAP
}

/// Calls `each` with every line `reader` gives, without its line ending ("\n" or "\r\n"), until
/// the end of the input or a read error. Bytes that are not UTF-8 become U+FFFD instead of ending
/// the loop (SP4 ruling R21): `BufRead::lines()` stops at the first such line, and then nobody
/// drains the pipe, so a chatty server would block on a full pipe.
fn read_lines_lossy<R: BufRead>(mut reader: R, mut each: impl FnMut(&str)) {
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    loop {
        buf.clear();
        match reader.read_until(b'\n', &mut buf) {
            Ok(0) | Err(_) => return,
            Ok(_) => {
                if buf.last() == Some(&b'\n') {
                    buf.pop();
                    if buf.last() == Some(&b'\r') {
                        buf.pop();
                    }
                }
                each(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf));
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Reads the server's output for one startup attempt. Both pipes are drained
/// for the server's whole life: if nobody read them, a chatty server would
/// eventually block on a full pipe (or hit a broken one) and hang or crash.
/// Both are read as bytes (read_lines_lossy), so a line that is not UTF-8
/// never stops the draining (SP4 ruling R21).
/// stderr is kept as a short tail for the error page, with the login token
/// scrubbed out in case anything ever echoes it. On stdout the ready line is
/// reported once, and every alert line goes to notify_alert.
fn watch_server(
    stdout: ChildStdout,
    stderr: ChildStderr,
    token: String,
    tx: mpsc::Sender<ServerStartup>,
    app: AppHandle,
) {
    let tail: Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<String>>> = Arc::new(Mutex::new(VecDeque::new()));
    {
        let tail = Arc::clone(&tail);
        let token = token.clone();
        thread::spawn(move || {
            read_lines_lossy(BufReader::new(stderr), |line| {
                let mut tail = tail.lock().unwrap();
                if tail.len() >= STDERR_TAIL_LINES {
                    tail.pop_front();
                }
                tail.push_back(line.replace(&token, "[hidden]"));
            });
        });
    }

    let mut reported = false;
    read_lines_lossy(BufReader::new(stdout), |line| {
        if !reported {
            if let Some(port) = parse_ready_line(line) {
                reported = true;
                let _ = tx.send(ServerStartup::Ready(port));
                return;
            }
        }
        if let Some(note) = parse_alert_line(line) {
            // The window check and the notification run on the main thread, so this reader
            // never waits on the window and keeps draining the server's output.
            let handle = app.clone();
            let _ = app.run_on_main_thread(move || notify_alert(&handle, &note));
        }
    });

    if !reported {
        let text = tail
            .lock()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .cloned()
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("\n");
        let _ = tx.send(ServerStartup::Exited(text));
    }
}

/// Shows one alert as a desktop notification, only when the person is not looking at the window
/// (should_notify). Runs on the main thread (see watch_server), where the window answers at once.
/// A notification that cannot be shown is reported on stderr and otherwise ignored: an alert must
/// never stop the app.
fn notify_alert(app: &AppHandle, note: &AlertNote) {
    let Some(title) = alert_title(&note.kind, &note.agent) else {
        return;
    };
    // A window that cannot be asked (or none at all) counts as hidden.
    let (visible, focused) = app
        .get_webview_window("main")
        .map(|window| {
            (
                window.is_visible().unwrap_or(false),
                window.is_focused().unwrap_or(false),
            )
        })
        .unwrap_or((false, false));
    if !should_notify(visible, focused) {
        return;
    }
    let mut notification = app.notification().builder().title(title);
    if !note.text.is_empty() {
        notification = notification.body(note.text.as_str());
    }
    if let Err(err) = notification.show() {
        eprintln!("Agent OS couldn't show a notification: {err}");
    }
}

/// A click on one of Agent OS's notifications brings the window back (it may be hidden). The
/// plugin calls the handler on a background thread; showing the window does not wait there. It is
/// registered before the server starts, because the plugin reports clicks only on notifications
/// shown after a handler exists.
fn listen_for_notification_clicks(app: &tauri::App) {
    let handle = app.handle().clone();
    let registered = app.notification().on_action(move |performed: &ActionPerformed| {
        if notification_click_shows_window(performed.action_id()) {
            show_main_window(&handle);
        }
    });
    if let Err(err) = registered {
        // Never on desktop (the plugin says so). Notifications still show; a click then only
        // brings the app to the front.
        eprintln!("Agent OS couldn't listen for notification clicks: {err}");
    }
}
```

### Task U5: Alerts UI and the Live meter (types, alert frame, panel lines, badge, Home strip, Orbit amber, Safety approvals, OpenClaw card, browser toast, desktop note, Help alerts lane)

After Tasks X1a to X3, the server knows when a session needs the person. Every summary in `GET /api/sessions` carries `alert`, `alerts`, `idleBy`, `resetAt`, `trustNeeded`, `hooksOff` and `meter` (ruling R22). The attached tab gets `{t:"alert", kind, text}` frames (K8). `GET /api/sessions/approvals` lists OpenClaw's pending approvals (R16).

The page shows none of this yet:
- the client still expects SP3's `{t:"alert", raw}`;
- the top bar has only a comment where the badge goes;
- Home's strip renders nothing, and the Orbit is never amber;
- Safety's Pending approvals is an SP3 empty state with a disabled example card;
- the panel says "Working." and every Live meter figure is "—".

This task builds every place in the page where an alert shows (spec "Alerts UI": tab marker, Home strip, top-bar badge count, Safety Pending approvals, and an in-app toast in browser mode). It also fills the Live meter from Claude Code's status line (spec "Side panel": Model, Context used, Plan used · 5-hour limit and Cost so far; warn at 70 %, critical at 100 %, with the reset time). On top of that it adds:
- the panel's alert lines: hooks switched off and why (R9), the trust line, and basic alerts for Hermes and Cursor (R18);
- OpenClaw's approval card with Allow once and Deny, each confirmed first, with OpenClaw's own error shown when it refuses;
- the desktop app's one-time notifications note (K17);
- the alerts lane, in words, on the Help page.

Why it is built this way, in plain words:
- Every surface reads the one shared sessions poll (`useSessionsList`), so the tab marker, the badge, the strip and the Orbit never disagree (R22).
- The attached tab reads the list again the moment an alert frame arrives, so the panel changes at once instead of up to 5 s later.
- All the words and counting rules live in pure files that a Node test loads straight from `src/`. The probe checks the pages in a real browser against the fakes: a real Hermes bell, and real OpenClaw approvals from the fake CLI.
- Nothing in this task answers anything. An approval is sent only after the person's click and a confirm, and it is exactly the answer they picked.

What its tests never do: start a real agent, talk to a real OpenClaw Gateway, or send a desktop notification (the page never sends one, R20; the Rust shell does, Task X4).

**Worker notes:**
- Run every command from the worktree root `<worktree>`. Never commit, push, tag, stash or set `CI=true`. Never start a real agent. Never read `.env` files or `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.cursor`, `~/.openclaw`, `~/.hermes`.
- A PreToolUse hook ("Fact-Forcing Gate") may refuse the first Bash command, the first Write of a new file or an `rm`. State the facts it asks for, then retry the same call.
- In zsh:
  - quote separator strings such as `"====="`;
  - quote glob options such as `--include='*.ts'`;
  - pass a probe path as its own argument;
  - each Bash call is a fresh shell, so set variables again in every block.
- The probe files are git-ignored (`.git/info/exclude`), so `git diff` never shows them. The report lists every edit to an older probe (file, line, before, after).
- Run one UI audit at a time and build first. Afterwards, `lsof -nP -iTCP:8791 -sTCP:LISTEN | wc -l` must print 0.
- Retry until every listed check is green; report anything that could not be done.

```js
test("the panel's alert lines: hooks off and why, the trust line, basic alerts for Hermes and Cursor (R9, R18)", () => {
  const lines = (over) => alerts.panelAlertLines(session(over));
  const TRUST = "Alerts start after you trust this folder in Claude";
  assert.equal(alerts.TRUST_LINE, TRUST);
  assert.deepEqual(lines({}), []);
  assert.deepEqual(lines({ trustNeeded: true }), [TRUST]);
  assert.deepEqual(lines({ trustNeeded: true, status: "idle" }), [TRUST]);
  assert.deepEqual(lines({ trustNeeded: true, status: "starting" }), [], "the line waits until the session is up");
  assert.deepEqual(lines({ trustNeeded: true, status: "exited" }), []);
  assert.deepEqual(
    lines({ trustNeeded: true, hooksOff: { alerts: "http_hook_urls", meter: null } }),
    ["Alerts are off for this session: your Claude settings allow hooks to reach only the addresses they list."],
    "with hooks off, trusting the folder would not bring alerts, so the trust line is not shown"
  );
  assert.deepEqual(
    lines({ hooksOff: { alerts: "all_hooks_disabled", meter: "all_hooks_disabled" } }),
    ["Alerts and the Live meter are off for this session: your Claude settings turn off all hooks."],
    "one sentence when both are off for the same reason"
  );
  assert.deepEqual(lines({ hooksOff: { alerts: "http_hook_env_vars", meter: "managed_status_line" } }), [
    "Alerts are off for this session: your Claude settings don't let hooks use Agent OS's token.",
    "The Live meter is off for this session: your organization's Claude settings set the status line."
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(lines({ trustNeeded: true, hooksOff: { alerts: null, meter: "managed_status_line" } }), [
    "The Live meter is off for this session: your organization's Claude settings set the status line.",
    TRUST
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(lines({ ...hermes, status: "live" }), [], "Hermes's live line already says its alerts are basic");
  assert.deepEqual(lines({ ...hermes, status: "idle" }), ["Alerts for Hermes are basic."]);
  assert.deepEqual(lines({ agentId: "cursor", agentLabel: "Cursor", status: "waiting" }), ["Alerts for Cursor are basic."]);
  assert.deepEqual(lines({ kind: "update", trustNeeded: true }), [], "update sessions never alert");
  assert.deepEqual(lines({ hooksOff: undefined, trustNeeded: undefined }), [], "a summary without the SP4 fields shows nothing");
});

});

  assert.equal(alerts.alertToast(before, [waiting("Approval requested: npm test.", { id: "a" }), before[1]]), "Claude Code · my-app is waiting for you. Approval requested: npm test.");
  assert.equal(alerts.alertToast(before, [session({ id: "a", status: "held", resetAt: at(17, 30) }), before[1]]), "Plan ran out for Claude Code · my-app.");
  assert.equal(alerts.alertToast(before, [waiting("x", { id: "a" }), waiting("May need you", { id: "b", ...hermes })]), "2 sessions need you.");
  assert.equal(alerts.alertToast([waiting("Wants to use Bash", { id: "a" })], [waiting("Has a question for you", { id: "a" })]), null, "still waiting: no second message for new words");
  assert.equal(alerts.alertToast([], [waiting("Wants to use Bash", { id: "a" })]), "Claude Code · my-app is waiting for you. Wants to use Bash.", "a session that appears already waiting is news");
  assert.equal(alerts.alertToast([], [waiting("x", { id: "u", kind: "update" })]), null, "update sessions never alert");
});

test("the desktop note (K17): the desktop app only, until dismissed; macOS adds that it asks once", () => {
  assert.equal(alerts.NOTIFY_NOTE_KEY, "agentos.notifyNote.v1");
  assert.equal(
    alerts.notifyNote({ desktop: true, isMac: true, dismissed: false }),
    "Agent OS shows a notification when a session needs you and its window is hidden. macOS asks once whether to allow it."
  );
  assert.equal(alerts.notifyNote({ desktop: true, isMac: false, dismissed: false }), "Agent OS shows a notification when a session needs you and its window is hidden.");
  assert.equal(alerts.notifyNote({ desktop: true, isMac: true, dismissed: true }), null);
  assert.equal(alerts.notifyNote({ desktop: false, isMac: true, dismissed: false }), null, "a browser tab gets messages, not notifications");
});

test("OpenClaw cards: matched to their session or shown in every OpenClaw panel; the words for each kind and answer (R16)", () => {
  const cards = [card({ id: "mine", sessionId: "s1" }), card({ id: "other", sessionId: "s2" }), card({ id: "loose", sessionId: null })];
  assert.deepEqual(alerts.approvalsForSession(cards, "s1").map((c) => c.id), ["mine", "loose"]);
  assert.deepEqual(alerts.approvalsForSession(cards, "s3").map((c) => c.id), ["loose"]);
  assert.equal(alerts.approvalHeading(card()), "OpenClaw wants to run");
  assert.equal(alerts.approvalHeading(card({ kind: "plugin" })), "OpenClaw asks for approval");
  assert.equal(alerts.approvalHeading(card({ kind: "system-agent" })), "OpenClaw asks for approval");
  assert.deepEqual(alerts.approvalConfirm(card(), "allow-once"), { title: "Allow this once?", body: "OpenClaw runs npm test this one time. It asks again next time.", confirm: "Allow once" });
  assert.equal(alerts.approvalConfirm(card({ summary: "ls ." }), "allow-once").body, "OpenClaw runs ls . this one time. It asks again next time.", "a command is shown as it is");
  assert.equal(alerts.approvalConfirm(card({ summary: "" }), "allow-once").body, "OpenClaw runs it this one time. It asks again next time.");
  assert.equal(
    alerts.approvalConfirm(card({ kind: "plugin", summary: "Deploy: push the site." }), "allow-once").body,
    "OpenClaw goes ahead with this one time: Deploy: push the site. It asks again next time."
  );
  assert.deepEqual(alerts.approvalConfirm(card(), "deny"), { title: "Deny this?", body: "OpenClaw is told no.", confirm: "Deny" });
  assert.equal(alerts.approvalDoneHeading("allow-once"), "You allowed it once");
  assert.equal(alerts.approvalDoneHeading("deny"), "You said no");
  assert.equal(alerts.FROM_OPENCLAW, "from OpenClaw");
  assert.equal(alerts.APPROVAL_NO_ANSWER, "Agent OS hasn't answered. OpenClaw may have your answer already: the card goes once it has.");
});

test("an answered card shows its answer, then leaves a few seconds after OpenClaw drops it", () => {
  const a = card({ id: "a" });
  const b = card({ id: "b", summary: "rm -rf build" });
  assert.deepEqual(alerts.approvalView([a, b], {}, NOW), [{ card: a, answered: null }, { card: b, answered: null }]);
  const answered = { a: { decision: "allow-once", at: NOW - 1000, card: a } };
  assert.deepEqual(alerts.approvalView([a, b], answered, NOW), [{ card: a, answered: "allow-once" }, { card: b, answered: null }]);
  assert.deepEqual(alerts.approvalView([b], answered, NOW), [{ card: b, answered: null }, { card: a, answered: "allow-once" }], "gone from OpenClaw's list: still shown as answered for a moment");
  assert.deepEqual(alerts.approvalView([b], answered, NOW - 1000 + alerts.ANSWER_SHOWN_MS), [{ card: b, answered: null }], "then it goes");
  assert.equal(alerts.ANSWER_SHOWN_MS, 6000);
});

test("the Live meter fills Model, Context used, Plan used and Cost so far from Claude's status line (spec Side panel, R11)", () => {
  const rows = page.meterRows(session({ meter }), NOW);
  assert.deepEqual(rows.map((r) => [r.id, r.label, r.value]), [
    ["brain", "Brain", "Plan"], ["model", "Model", "Opus 4.7"], ["time", "Running for", "12 m 40 s"], ["context", "Context used", "42%"], ["plan", "Plan used", "71%"]
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(rows[3].gauge, { percent: 42, tone: "accent" });
  assert.deepEqual(rows[4].gauge, { percent: 71, tone: "warn", detail: "Resets 5:30 pm" });
  assert.equal(rows[4].dim, "5-hour limit");
  const full = page.meterRows(session({ meter: { ...meter, contextPercent: 100, plan: { usedPercent: 100, resetsAt: null } } }), NOW);
  assert.deepEqual(full[3].gauge, { percent: 100, tone: "danger" });
  assert.deepEqual(full[4].gauge, { percent: 100, tone: "danger" }, "no reset words when the time is not known");
  assert.equal(page.meterRows(session({ meter: { ...meter, contextPercent: 69.6 } }), NOW)[3].gauge.tone, "warn", "70 % after rounding warns");
  const odd = page.meterRows(session({ meter: { ...meter, contextPercent: -5, model: "  " } }), NOW);
  assert.deepEqual([odd[1].value, odd[3].value, odd[3].gauge], [null, null, undefined], "a figure that is not a figure is —");
  // R11: OpenRouter and Local brains get no plan window from Claude, so Plan used is "—"; an OpenRouter brain's cost is
  // Claude's own estimate.
  const openrouter = page.meterRows(session({ brain: { kind: "openrouter", label: "OpenRouter" }, meter: { ...meter, plan: null } }), NOW);
  assert.deepEqual(openrouter.map((r) => [r.id, r.value]), [["brain", "OpenRouter"], ["model", "Opus 4.7"], ["time", "12 m 40 s"], ["context", "42%"], ["plan", null], ["cost", "$1.23 (estimate)"]]);
  const local = page.meterRows(session({ brain: { kind: "local", label: "Local" }, meter: { ...meter, plan: null } }), NOW);
  assert.deepEqual(local.map((r) => [r.id, r.value]), [["brain", "Local"], ["model", "Opus 4.7"], ["time", "12 m 40 s"], ["context", "42%"], ["plan", null]], "a Local brain: Plan used is —, and there is no cost row");
  assert.deepEqual(local.at(-1), { id: "plan", label: "Plan used", dim: "5-hour limit", value: null }, "the — row keeps its label and has no gauge");
  assert.equal(page.meterRows(session({ brain: { kind: "openrouter", label: "OpenRouter" }, meter: { ...meter, plan: null, costUsd: 0.003 } }), NOW).at(-1).value, "under $0.01 (estimate)");
  assert.equal(page.meterRows(session({ brain: { kind: "openrouter", label: "OpenRouter" }, meter: { ...meter, plan: null, costUsd: null } }), NOW).at(-1).value, null);
  const unknown = page.meterRows(session({ meter: { model: null, contextPercent: null, contextTokens: null, plan: null, weekly: null, costUsd: null, at: iso(1000) } }), NOW);
  assert.deepEqual(unknown.map((r) => [r.id, r.value]), [["brain", "Plan"], ["model", null], ["time", "12 m 40 s"], ["context", null], ["plan", null]]);
  assert.equal(unknown.some((r) => r.gauge), false);
  assert.deepEqual(page.meterRows(session({ status: "exited", endedAt: iso(160_000), meter }), NOW).map((r) => r.value), ["Plan", null, "10 m 00 s", null, null], "an ended session shows no live figures");
  assert.deepEqual(page.meterRows(session({ agentId: "hermes", brain: null, meter: null }), NOW).map((r) => r.id), ["brain", "model", "time", "context"], "no status line: most of the meter stays —");
  assert.deepEqual([69, 70, 99, 100].map(page.meterTone), ["accent", "warn", "warn", "danger"]);
  assert.equal(page.costWords(0), "$0.00");
  assert.equal(page.costWords(12.345), "$12.35");
});

test("Home: a waiting session turns its agent's line amber; the note, the label, the lede and the row say so", () => {
  const sessions = [
    session({ id: "a", agentId: "codex", status: "waiting" }),
    session({ id: "b", agentId: "codex", status: "live" }),
    session({ id: "c", agentId: "claude", status: "live" }),
    session({ id: "d", agentId: "hermes", status: "held" }),
    session({ id: "e", agentId: "cursor", kind: "update", status: "waiting" })
  ];
  const states = home.orbitStates([], sessions);
  assert.deepEqual(states, { codex: "waiting", claude: "live" }, "waiting wins over live; held stays dim; an update session is never shown");
  assert.equal(home.orbitNote(states), "A line lights only while that agent works. Amber means it needs you.");
  assert.equal(home.orbitNote({ claude: "live" }), "A line lights only while that agent works.");
  assert.equal(home.orbitLabel(states, true), "Agent OS at the centre with five agents around it. Waiting for you: Codex CLI. Working now: Claude Code.");
  assert.equal(home.orbitLabel({ codex: "waiting" }, true), "Agent OS at the centre with five agents around it. Waiting for you: Codex CLI.");
  assert.equal(home.orbitLabel(states, false), "Agent OS at the centre with five agents around it. What each agent is doing is not known right now.");
  const agents = { state: "ok", data: [] };
  assert.equal(home.homeLede({ agents, states, runsKnown: true }), "Codex CLI is waiting for you. Claude Code is working.");
  assert.equal(home.homeLede({ agents, states: { codex: "waiting", hermes: "waiting" }, runsKnown: false }), "Hermes Agent and Codex CLI are waiting for you.");
  const codex = installed("codex");
  assert.deepEqual(home.agentLine({ agents: "ok", runs: "ok", summary: codex, session: session({ agentId: "codex", status: "waiting" }), now: NOW }), { state: "waiting", where: "Session in my-app" });
  assert.deepEqual(home.agentLine({ agents: "ok", runs: "ok", summary: codex, session: session({ agentId: "codex", status: "held" }), now: NOW }), { state: "held", where: "Session in my-app" });
});

});
```

```ts

// SP4 (Task U5 adds these; the server fills them from Task X1a on): every session's alert state travels in GET
// /api/sessions as well as on the WebSocket (ruling R22), so a tab that is not attached still shows its marker.
export type SignalKind = "waiting" | "turn_done" | "limit" | "approval" | "resolved";
export type AlertKind = "waiting" | "approval" | "limit";

export interface SessionAlert {
  kind: AlertKind;
  // The server's cleaned short text (at most 200 characters): "Wants to use Bash", "May need you", OpenClaw's summary.
  text: string;
  at: string;
}

// Why Claude Code's own settings keep Agent OS's hooks or status line out of this session (ruling R9, K10).
export type HooksOffCode = "managed_hooks_only" | "all_hooks_disabled" | "http_hook_urls" | "http_hook_env_vars" | "managed_status_line";

// What Claude Code's own status line reports (Task X2b), for the Live meter.
export interface SessionMeter {
  model: string | null;
  // 0-100.
  contextPercent: number | null;
  contextTokens: number | null;
  // rate_limits.five_hour and .seven_day; absent on OpenRouter and Local brains (R11).
  plan: { usedPercent: number; resetsAt: string | null } | null;
  weekly: { usedPercent: number; resetsAt: string | null } | null;
  // Claude's own estimate at list prices (R11).
  costUsd: number | null;
  at: string;
}

// A hand-off typed into this session (Task X8), kept in the server's memory only.
export interface SessionHandoff {
  state: "pending" | "typed" | "copy";
  text: string;
  fromId: string | null;
  at: string;
}

// One of OpenClaw's pending approvals (Task X3). It never names a folder: OpenClaw's list has none (R16). `sessionId` is
// the Agent OS session it came from, or null when OpenClaw did not say (then it shows in every OpenClaw panel, K11).
export interface ApprovalCard {
  id: string;
  kind: "exec" | "plugin" | "system-agent";
  summary: string;
  createdAt: string;
  expiresAt: string;
  sessionId: string | null;
}

export interface ApprovalListResponse {
  approvals: ApprovalCard[];
  // The server's sentence while OpenClaw's approvals can't be read, else null.
  error: string | null;
}

// The only two answers Agent OS ever sends to OpenClaw (R16).
export type ApprovalDecision = "allow-once" | "deny";

// A moment in a session's recording (meta.json): a prompt (label only, R23), a permission asked, files changed.
export type SessionMarker =
  | { at: string; type: "prompt" }
  | { at: string; type: "permission"; text: string }
  | { at: string; type: "files"; files: Array<{ path: string; added: number | null; removed: number | null }>; more: number };
```

```ts
// OpenClaw's pending approvals (Task X3): the cards and, while OpenClaw can't be asked, the server's sentence.
export async function listApprovals(): Promise<ApprovalListResponse> {
  const body = await withTimeout(request<ApprovalListResponse>("/api/sessions/approvals"), SESSION_LIMITS_MS.approvals);
  if (!body || !Array.isArray(body.approvals)) throw new Error(UNREADABLE);
  return { approvals: body.approvals, error: typeof body.error === "string" && body.error ? body.error : null };
}

// Sends exactly the answer the person picked and confirmed (ruling R16). When OpenClaw refuses, the server answers 409
// approval_failed with OpenClaw's own words (an ApiError whose detail is that sentence).
export function resolveApproval(id: string, decision: ApprovalDecision): Promise<{ ok: true; message: string | null }> {
  return withTimeout(
    request<{ ok: true; message: string | null }>("/api/sessions/approvals/resolve", postJson({ id, decision })),
    SESSION_LIMITS_MS.approvalResolve
  );
}
```

Replace the whole block from `// The side panel's one line for the state, SP3 versions (spec, Session activity states). Before alerts` down to the closing `}` of `sessionPanelLine` (lines 95-124) with:

```ts
// "2:21 am" for a time today, "Oct 30, 2:21 am" for another day; "" when it isn't a time. The Runs page's
// formatResetTime words (src/ui/builderShared.ts), kept here as a copy because that file imports at run time and this
// one must not (test/sessions-alerts-ui-logic.test.js pins the words).
export function resetWords(iso: string | null | undefined, now: number): string {
  if (!iso) return "";
  const date = new Date(iso);
  if (Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) return "";
  const time = date
    .toLocaleTimeString("en-US", { hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit" })
    .replace(/\s?(AM|PM)$/i, (match) => ` ${match.trim().toLowerCase()}`);
  if (date.toDateString() === new Date(now).toDateString()) return time;
  return `${date.toLocaleDateString("en-US", { month: "short", day: "numeric" })}, ${time}`;
}

// What the line reads besides the SP3 fields. Each SP4 field is optional here, so a summary without it reads as basic.
// (trustNeeded and hooksOff are read by panelAlertLines in alertsShared.ts, the lines under this one.)
type PanelLineFields = Pick<SessionSummary, "status" | "agentLabel" | "recordingBytes"> &
  EndFields & {
    stateSince?: string | null;
    agentId?: string;
    alerts?: SessionSummary["alerts"];
    idleBy?: SessionSummary["idleBy"];
    resetAt?: string | null;
    alert?: SessionSummary["alert"];
  };

// The side panel's one line for the state (spec, Session activity states; the prototype's info()). Live says whether
// Agent OS hears this agent's questions: "full" once a turn-done session's first signal arrived, otherwise basic.
// OpenClaw's approval question is a card in the panel. Idle entered by a turn_done signal is "Ready for the next
// message." (K21). An ended session's recording holds at least its header line, so 0 bytes means the 1 GB cap (Q38) or a
// delete removed it: then Runs has no row for it, and the line does not send the person there.
export function sessionPanelLine(s: PanelLineFields, now: number): string {
  switch (s.status) {
    case "starting":
      return `Starting ${s.agentLabel}…`;
    case "live":
      return s.alerts === "full" ? "Working. Agent OS alerts you when it asks you something." : `Working. Alerts for ${s.agentLabel} are basic.`;
    case "waiting":
      return s.agentId === "openclaw" && s.alert?.kind === "approval"
        ? "The question is in the card below."
        : "The question is in the terminal. Agent OS never answers for you.";
    case "idle": {
      if (s.idleBy === "turn_done") return "Ready for the next message.";
      const time = sessionDuration(s.stateSince, now);
      return time === "—" ? "Idle. Nothing is running." : `Idle for ${time}. Nothing is running.`;
    }
    case "held": {
      const when = resetWords(s.resetAt, now);
      return when ? `Plan limit reached. Resets ${when}.` : "Plan limit reached.";
    }
    case "exited":
      return s.recordingBytes > 0 ? `${endedLine(s)} The recording is in Runs.` : `${endedLine(s)} Its recording was removed.`;
    default:
      return "";
  }
}
```

```ts
// Alerts (SP4, Task U5): the words and small rules around the tab markers. The top-bar badge, the Home strip, Safety's
// list of questions asked in a terminal, the message a browser tab shows, the session panel's alert lines (hooks switched
// off and why, the trust line, basic alerts), OpenClaw's approval cards and the desktop app's one-time note. Every alert
// comes from the server: each session's alert is in GET /api/sessions (ruling R22) and OpenClaw's pending approvals in
// GET /api/sessions/approvals (Task X3); nothing here decides that something waits. `import type` only, plus the
// sessionsShared.ts import below, so test/sessions-alerts-ui-logic.test.js loads this file straight from src/.
import type { ApprovalCard, ApprovalDecision, HooksOffCode, SessionSummary } from "../types";
// Node cannot follow an extensionless import when a test loads this file straight from src/; tsconfig does not allow the
// extension, so TypeScript's only complaint (TS5097) is silenced on this one line (the homeShared.ts pattern).
// @ts-expect-error TS5097
import { resetWords, sessionTitle } from "./sessionsShared.ts";

// The per-viewer key that remembers the desktop note was dismissed (K17).
export const NOTIFY_NOTE_KEY = "agentos.notifyNote.v1";
// The server's words for a basic alert (signals.js BASIC_ALERT_TEXT, ruling R19): a bell or a title sign from Hermes or
// Cursor, which may also mean the agent finished.
export const BASIC_ALERT_TEXT = "May need you";
// Spec, Session activity states: until the person trusts the folder inside Claude (Task X2a's trustNeeded).
export const TRUST_LINE = "Alerts start after you trust this folder in Claude";
// R16: a card OpenClaw could not match to one session shows in every open OpenClaw panel with these words.
export const FROM_OPENCLAW = "from OpenClaw";
// A resolve that got no answer at all may still have reached OpenClaw.
export const APPROVAL_NO_ANSWER = "Agent OS hasn't answered. OpenClaw may have your answer already: the card goes once it has.";
// How long a card you answered stays as "You allowed it once" or "You said no" after OpenClaw's list drops it.
export const ANSWER_SHOWN_MS = 6000;
// The Home strip shows at most this many rows; the rest are counted.
export const STRIP_MAX = 3;

type Listed = Pick<SessionSummary, "id" | "kind" | "status" | "agentId" | "agentLabel" | "folderName" | "folderShown"> & {
  alert?: SessionSummary["alert"];
  resetAt?: string | null;
};

// Signals scope: only agent sessions alert; update and setup sessions never do.
function needsYou(s: Pick<SessionSummary, "kind" | "status">, status: "waiting" | "held"): boolean {
  return s.kind === "agent" && s.status === status;
}

// K22: the badge counts agent sessions that wait for the person. A held session shows on its tab and the Home strip.
export function waitingCount(sessions: ReadonlyArray<Pick<SessionSummary, "kind" | "status">>): number {
  return sessions.filter((s) => needsYou(s, "waiting")).length;
}

export function waitingBadgeText(n: number): string {
  return Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 ? `Waiting for you (${n})` : "";
}

export interface StripItem {
  id: string;
  kind: "waiting" | "held";
  title: string;
  text: string;
}

function askedText(s: Listed): string {
  const text = typeof s.alert?.text === "string" ? s.alert.text.trim() : "";
  return text || "Waiting for you";
}

function askedAt(s: Listed): number {
  const time = s.alert?.at ? Date.parse(s.alert.at) : NaN;
  return Number.isFinite(time) ? time : Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
}

// The Home strip: every agent session that waits for you, the one that has waited longest first, then every one whose
// plan ran out, with its reset time when known (spec, Alerts UI and Session activity states).
export function homeStripItems(sessions: ReadonlyArray<Listed>, now: number = Date.now()): StripItem[] {
  const waiting = sessions
    .filter((s) => needsYou(s, "waiting"))
    .map((s, index) => ({ s, index }))
    .sort((a, b) => askedAt(a.s) - askedAt(b.s) || a.index - b.index)
    .map(({ s }): StripItem => ({ id: s.id, kind: "waiting", title: sessionTitle(s), text: askedText(s) }));
  const held = sessions
    .filter((s) => needsYou(s, "held"))
    .map((s): StripItem => {
      const when = resetWords(s.resetAt, now);
      return { id: s.id, kind: "held", title: sessionTitle(s), text: when ? `Plan ran out. Resets ${when}.` : "Plan ran out." };
    });
  return [...waiting, ...held];
}

export function stripMore(n: number): string {
  return Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 ? `${n} more in Sessions.` : "";
}

// Safety's rows for questions asked inside an agent's own terminal: every waiting session except an OpenClaw session
// whose question is a card on that page (its alert is an approval).
export function terminalQuestions(sessions: ReadonlyArray<Listed>): StripItem[] {
  const asCard = new Set(sessions.filter((s) => s.agentId === "openclaw" && s.alert?.kind === "approval").map((s) => s.id));
  return homeStripItems(sessions).filter((item) => item.kind === "waiting" && !asCard.has(item.id));
}

const HOOKS_OFF: Record<HooksOffCode, string> = {
  all_hooks_disabled: "Alerts and the Live meter are off for this session: your Claude settings turn off all hooks.",
  managed_hooks_only: "Alerts and the Live meter are off for this session: your organization's Claude settings allow only its own hooks.",
  http_hook_urls: "Alerts are off for this session: your Claude settings allow hooks to reach only the addresses they list.",
  http_hook_env_vars: "Alerts are off for this session: your Claude settings don't let hooks use Agent OS's token.",
  managed_status_line: "The Live meter is off for this session: your organization's Claude settings set the status line."
};

// R9: why alerts or the Live meter are off in this session; "" for anything that is not a code this version knows.
export function hooksOffLine(code: unknown): string {
  return typeof code === "string" && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(HOOKS_OFF, code) ? HOOKS_OFF[code as HooksOffCode] : "";
}

type PanelAlertFields = Pick<SessionSummary, "kind" | "status" | "agentId" | "agentLabel"> & {
  trustNeeded?: boolean;
  hooksOff?: SessionSummary["hooksOff"] | null;
};

// The lines under the panel's state line, in this order: why alerts are off (R9), why the Live meter is off when that
// is a different reason, the trust line (live or idle, and only when hooks are not switched off: trusting the folder
// would then bring nothing), and for Hermes and Cursor that their alerts are basic (R18) whenever the state line does
// not already say so.
export function panelAlertLines(s: PanelAlertFields): string[] {
  if (s.kind !== "agent" || s.status === "exited") return [];
  const off = s.hooksOff ?? { alerts: null, meter: null };
  const lines: string[] = [];
  const alertsOff = hooksOffLine(off.alerts);
  const meterOff = off.meter !== off.alerts ? hooksOffLine(off.meter) : "";
  if (alertsOff) lines.push(alertsOff);
  if (meterOff) lines.push(meterOff);
  if (!alertsOff && s.trustNeeded === true && (s.status === "live" || s.status === "idle")) lines.push(TRUST_LINE);
  if ((s.agentId === "hermes" || s.agentId === "cursor") && s.status !== "live" && s.status !== "starting") {
    lines.push(`Alerts for ${s.agentLabel} are basic.`);
  }
  return lines;
}

// The browser tab's message (spec, Alerts UI: "In browser mode, an in-app toast only"): one for each change between two
// reads of the list into waiting or held. The first read is not news, and new words for an alert that was already
// there are not either. Several at once give one message.
export function alertToast(prev: ReadonlyArray<Listed> | null, next: ReadonlyArray<Listed>): string | null {
  if (!prev) return null;
  const before = new Map(prev.map((s) => [s.id, s.status]));
  const fresh = next.filter((s) => (needsYou(s, "waiting") || needsYou(s, "held")) && before.get(s.id) !== s.status);
  if (fresh.length === 0) return null;
  if (fresh.length > 1) return `${fresh.length} sessions need you.`;
  const s = fresh[0];
  const title = sessionTitle(s);
  if (s.status === "held") return `Plan ran out for ${title}.`;
  const text = typeof s.alert?.text === "string" ? s.alert.text.trim() : "";
  if (text === BASIC_ALERT_TEXT) return `${title} may need you.`;
  if (!text || text === "Waiting for you") return `${title} is waiting for you.`;
  return `${title} is waiting for you. ${/[.!?…]$/.test(text) ? text : `${text}.`}`;
}

// K17: the desktop app explains its notifications once on the Sessions page (the page itself never asks for or sends
// one, R20; macOS asks by itself on the first notification the shell shows).
export function notifyNote({ desktop, isMac, dismissed }: { desktop: boolean; isMac: boolean; dismissed: boolean }): string | null {
  if (!desktop || dismissed) return null;
  const first = "Agent OS shows a notification when a session needs you and its window is hidden.";
  return isMac ? `${first} macOS asks once whether to allow it.` : first;
}

// R16, K11: a session's panel shows its own cards and every card OpenClaw could not match to one session.
export function approvalsForSession(cards: ReadonlyArray<ApprovalCard>, sessionId: string): ApprovalCard[] {
  return cards.filter((card) => card.sessionId === sessionId || card.sessionId === null);
}

export function approvalHeading(card: Pick<ApprovalCard, "kind">): string {
  return card.kind === "exec" ? "OpenClaw wants to run" : "OpenClaw asks for approval";
}

export interface ApprovalConfirm {
  title: string;
  body: string;
  confirm: string;
}

// The confirm before an answer is sent. A command is shown exactly as OpenClaw gave it; another kind's summary loses a
// trailing full stop so the sentence reads once.
export function approvalConfirm(card: Pick<ApprovalCard, "kind" | "summary">, decision: ApprovalDecision): ApprovalConfirm {
  if (decision === "deny") return { title: "Deny this?", body: "OpenClaw is told no.", confirm: "Deny" };
  const summary = String(card.summary ?? "").trim();
  if (card.kind === "exec") {
    return { title: "Allow this once?", body: `OpenClaw runs ${summary || "it"} this one time. It asks again next time.`, confirm: "Allow once" };
  }
  const what = summary.replace(/[.\s]+$/, "") || "it";
  return { title: "Allow this once?", body: `OpenClaw goes ahead with this one time: ${what}. It asks again next time.`, confirm: "Allow once" };
}

export function approvalDoneHeading(decision: ApprovalDecision): string {
  return decision === "allow-once" ? "You allowed it once" : "You said no";
}

export interface Answered {
  decision: ApprovalDecision;
  at: number;
  card: ApprovalCard;
}

export interface ApprovalItem {
  card: ApprovalCard;
  answered: ApprovalDecision | null;
}

// What the cards show: OpenClaw's list, a card answered here marked with its answer, and an answered card OpenClaw
// already dropped kept for ANSWER_SHOWN_MS after the answer, so it does not vanish the moment you press.
export function approvalView(cards: ReadonlyArray<ApprovalCard>, answered: Readonly<Record<string, Answered>>, now: number): ApprovalItem[] {
  const items: ApprovalItem[] = cards.map((card) => ({ card, answered: answered[card.id]?.decision ?? null }));
  const listed = new Set(cards.map((card) => card.id));
  for (const [id, done] of Object.entries(answered)) {
    if (!listed.has(id) && now - done.at < ANSWER_SHOWN_MS) items.push({ card: done.card, answered: done.decision });
  }
  return items;
}
```

Replace `MeterRow` and `meterRows` (from `export interface MeterRow {` through the closing `}` of `meterRows`) with:

```ts
export interface MeterRow {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  // null: not known, shown as "—" (with "unknown" for screen readers).
  value: string | null;
  dim?: string;
  // A figure drawn as a gauge (Context used, Plan used): its percent, its tone (spec, Side panel: warn at 70 %, critical
  // at 100 %) and, for the plan, when it resets ("Resets 2:21 am").
  gauge?: { percent: number; tone: MeterTone; detail?: string };
}

export type MeterTone = "accent" | "warn" | "danger";

export function meterTone(percent: number): MeterTone {
  if (percent >= 100) return "danger";
  return percent >= 70 ? "warn" : "accent";
}

// "$1.23"; "under $0.01" for a cost above nothing that would read $0.00.
export function costWords(amount: number): string {
  return amount > 0 && amount < 0.005 ? "under $0.01" : `$${amount.toFixed(2)}`;
}

const percentOf = (value: unknown): number | null =>
  typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value) && value >= 0 ? Math.round(value) : null;

// Every Live meter row (spec, Side panel). Model, Context used, Plan used · 5-hour limit and Cost so far come from Claude
// Code's status line (Task X2b's `meter`, only while the session runs); anything not known is "—". Plan used is there
// for every brain: a gauge whenever the status line reports the 5-hour window, else "—". OpenRouter and Local brains
// always show "—" there, because Claude sends them no rate_limits (R11). Cost so far is for an OpenRouter brain, as in
// the prototype, and is Claude's own estimate.
export function meterRows(
  s: Pick<SessionSummary, "brain" | "status" | "startedAt" | "endedAt"> & { meter?: SessionMeter | null },
  now: number
): MeterRow[] {
  const brain = brainWords(s.brain);
  const ended = s.status === "exited";
  const endMs = ended ? (s.endedAt ? Date.parse(s.endedAt) : NaN) : now;
  const time = durationWords(s.startedAt, endMs);
  const m = ended ? null : s.meter ?? null;
  const model = m && typeof m.model === "string" && m.model.trim() ? m.model.trim() : null;
  const context = m ? percentOf(m.contextPercent) : null;
  const plan = m && m.plan ? percentOf(m.plan.usedPercent) : null;
  const rows: MeterRow[] = [
    brain ? { id: "brain", label: "Brain", value: brain.main, dim: brain.dim } : { id: "brain", label: "Brain", value: null },
    { id: "model", label: "Model", value: model },
    { id: "time", label: ended ? "Ran for" : "Running for", value: time === "—" ? null : time },
    context === null
      ? { id: "context", label: "Context used", value: null }
      : { id: "context", label: "Context used", value: `${context}%`, gauge: { percent: context, tone: meterTone(context) } }
  ];
  if (plan !== null) {
    const when = resetWords(m?.plan?.resetsAt, now);
    rows.push({
      id: "plan",
      label: "Plan used",
      dim: "5-hour limit",
      value: `${plan}%`,
      gauge: { percent: plan, tone: meterTone(plan), ...(when ? { detail: `Resets ${when}` } : {}) }
    });
  } else if (s.brain) {
    // R11's "—": the window is not known yet, or the brain is OpenRouter or Local, where Claude sends no rate_limits.
    rows.push({ id: "plan", label: "Plan used", dim: "5-hour limit", value: null });
  }
  if (s.brain?.kind === "openrouter") {
    const cost = m && typeof m.costUsd === "number" && Number.isFinite(m.costUsd) && m.costUsd >= 0 ? m.costUsd : null;
    rows.push({ id: "cost", label: "Cost so far", value: cost === null ? null : `${costWords(cost)} (estimate)` });
  }
  return rows;
}
```

```ts
// A line lights only while that agent works: a live agent run, or a session whose state is live. It is amber while one
// of the agent's sessions waits for you, which wins over live (spec: Home Orbit is lit only while live, amber for
// waiting; starting, idle, held and exited stay dim). An update session never shows on Home.
export function orbitStates(runs: RunMeta[], sessions: SessionSummary[] = []): OrbitStates {
  const out: OrbitStates = {};
  for (const id of Object.keys(liveRunsByAgent(runs)) as HomeAgentId[]) out[id] = "live";
  for (const session of sessions) {
    const id = session.agentId;
    if (session.kind === "update" || !isHomeAgent(id)) continue;
    if (session.status === "waiting") out[id] = "waiting";
    else if (session.status === "live" && out[id] !== "waiting") out[id] = "live";
  }
  return out;
}
```

```ts
function namesOf(states: OrbitStates, state: "live" | "waiting" = "live"): string[] {
  return HOME_AGENTS.filter((a) => states[a.id] === state).map((a) => a.name);
}

// `runsKnown` is false until the runs list has loaded once: then nothing is claimed.
export function orbitLabel(states: OrbitStates, runsKnown: boolean): string {
  const lit = namesOf(states);
  const waiting = namesOf(states, "waiting");
  const known = [waiting.length ? `Waiting for you: ${waiting.join(", ")}.` : "", lit.length ? `Working now: ${lit.join(", ")}.` : ""].filter(Boolean);
  const what = !runsKnown ? "What each agent is doing is not known right now." : known.length ? known.join(" ") : "No agent is working right now.";
  return `Agent OS at the centre with five agents around it. ${what}`;
}

// "Amber means it needs you." only while a line is amber (the prototype's Home note).
export function orbitNote(states: OrbitStates): string {
  const base = "A line lights only while that agent works.";
  return Object.values(states).includes("waiting") ? `${base} Amber means it needs you.` : base;
}
```

```ts
  if (lit.length || waiting.length) {

      waiting.length ? `${joinNames(waiting)} ${waiting.length === 1 ? "is" : "are"} waiting for you.` : "",
      lit.length ? `${joinNames(lit)} ${lit.length === 1 ? "is" : "are"} working.` : ""
    ]
      .filter(Boolean)
      .join(" ");
  }
```

```js
// Task U5 (SP4): the alerts UI and the Live meter, in a real browser against the throwaway server.
// Run (after `npm run build`), from the worktree root:
//   node .superpowers/ui-audit/audit.mjs probe .superpowers/ui-audit/probes/alerts.mjs
// Real: sessions are W1's TUI-like fake through fake-bin/; a Hermes session's typed `bell` becomes "May need you" on the
// server (Task X1b) and comes back through GET /api/sessions and the WebSocket (Task X1a); OpenClaw's approvals come from
// the fake CLI through Task X3's poller, driven by the knobs FAKE_OPENCLAW_APPROVALS and FAKE_OPENCLAW_RESOLVE in
// HOME/.fake-knobs. Stubbed (page.route) only what a fake cannot give here: the Live meter figures, a held session, the
// trust line and hooks switched off, by patching one Claude session in the GET /api/sessions answer. The desktop app is
// the same fake bridge as sessions.mjs. Nothing here starts a real agent; every session it starts is stopped at the end.
import { mkdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

const W = 1470, H = 956;
const POLL = "Agent OS couldn't read OpenClaw's approvals. Check that the OpenClaw Gateway is running on Agents.";
const realErrors = (errors) => errors.filter((e) => !/Failed to load resource/.test(e));

// The desktop shell's event bridge, faked (the same stand-in as sessions.mjs, without the updater).
function fakeDesktopBridge() {
  const callbacks = new Map();
  let next = 1;
  window.__fake = { listeners: [], emitted: [], invoked: [] };
  window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__ = {
    transformCallback(callback) {
      const id = next++;
      callbacks.set(id, callback);
      return id;
    },
    async invoke(cmd, args) {
      window.__fake.invoked.push(cmd);
      if (cmd === "plugin:updater|check") return null;
      if (cmd === "plugin:event|listen") {
        window.__fake.listeners.push({ event: args.event, handler: args.handler });
        return args.handler;
      }
      if (cmd === "plugin:event|unlisten") {
        window.__fake.listeners = window.__fake.listeners.filter((l) => l.handler !== args.eventId);
        return null;
      }
      if (cmd === "plugin:event|emit") {
        window.__fake.emitted.push({ event: args.event, payload: args.payload ?? null });
        return null;
      }
      throw new Error(`fake desktop bridge: ${cmd} is not available here`);
    }
  };
  window.__TAURI_EVENT_PLUGIN_INTERNALS__ = { unregisterListener() {} };
}

export default async function ({ browser, openPage, shot, pass, fail, api, BASE, TOKEN, HOME }) {
  const check = (ok, name, why = "") => (ok ? pass(name) : fail(name, String(why)));
  if (!HOME) {
    fail("harness", "audit.mjs does not pass HOME to probes");
    return;
  }
  const notes = path.join(HOME, "projects", "notes");
  const myApp = path.join(HOME, "projects", "my-app");

  const clearKnob = (name) => rmSync(path.join(knobDir, name), { force: true });
  const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
  const waitFor = async (fn, ms = 10000) => {
    const end = Date.now() + ms;
    while (Date.now() < end) {
      try { if (await fn()) return true; } catch {}
      await sleep(200);
    }
    return false;
  };

    await tab.keyboard.type(text);
    await tab.keyboard.press("Enter");
  }
  const started = [];

      check(await visible(section.locator(".os-approval").getByRole("button", { name: "Allow once" })), "Safety: Allow once on the card");
      check(!(await sideways(tab)), "Safety at 1280x720: no sideways scroll");
      await shot(tab, "alerts", 1280, 720, "safety-card");
      setKnob("FAKE_OPENCLAW_APPROVALS", "fail");
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await textOf(section)).includes(POLL), 20000), "a failed read of OpenClaw's approvals is said in words", await textOf(section));
      setKnob("FAKE_OPENCLAW_APPROVALS", pendingJson([]));
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await textOf(section)).includes("Nothing from OpenClaw is waiting here"), 20000), "nothing pending: Nothing from OpenClaw is waiting here", await textOf(section));
      check(await visible(tab.getByText(/example, not real/)), "the example card says it is an example");
      check((await tab.getByText(/Nothing is waiting for you/).count()) === 0, "it never claims nothing is waiting (a Team Room may be)");
      check(realErrors(errors).length === 0, "console clean (OpenClaw)", realErrors(errors).join(" / "));
      await context.close();
    }

    // 4. The desktop app: the one-time note, kept dismissed; a bell shows the badge but no in-app message (the shell
    //    notifies instead, Task X4).
    if (hermes) {
      const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: W, height: H } });
      await context.addInitScript(fakeDesktopBridge);
      const tab = await context.newPage();
      const errors = [];
      tab.on("console", (m) => { if (m.type() === "error") errors.push(m.text()); });
      tab.on("pageerror", (e) => errors.push(String(e)));
      await tab.goto(`${BASE}/?launch=${TOKEN}`);
      await tab.goto(`${BASE}/?page=sessions&session=${hermes}`);
      const note = tab.locator(".os-sess__notify");
      check(await visible(note), "desktop app: the notifications note shows on the Sessions page");
      check((await textOf(note)).includes("Agent OS shows a notification when a session needs you and its window is hidden."), "the note, word for word", await textOf(note));
      await shot(tab, "alerts", W, H, "desktop-note");
      if (await tryClick(note.getByRole("button", { name: "Got it" }), "Got it on the note")) {
        check(await waitFor(async () => (await note.count()) === 0), "Got it hides the note");
        await tab.reload();
        await waitFor(async () => (await termText(tab)).includes("FAKE_ARGV"), 15000);
        await afterPaint(tab);
        check((await note.count()) === 0, "and it stays hidden after a reload (kept in this browser)");
      }
      await typeInTerminal(tab, "bell");
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await textOf(badge(tab))) === "Waiting for you (1)", 10000), "desktop app: the badge shows");
      await sleep(1500);
      check(!(await textOf(tab.locator(".os-toast"))).includes("may need you"), "desktop app: no in-app message (the shell notifies)");
      await typeInTerminal(tab, "x");
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await badge(tab).count()) === 0, 10000), "desktop app: typing clears it");
      check(realErrors(errors).length === 0, "console clean (desktop app)", realErrors(errors).join(" / "));
      await context.close();
    }

    // 5. Help: the alerts lane in words, browser version, and no hand-off promise yet.
    {
      const { context, tab } = await openPage(browser, W, H, "help");
      const text = (await tab.locator(".os-help").innerText()) || "";
      check(text.includes("Alerts, in words"), "Help: Alerts, in words");
      check(text.includes("Agent OS turns it into an alert: an amber tab marker, the Home strip, the top-bar badge and a message at the bottom of this page."), "browser tab: the lane says a message, not a notification");
      check(!/hand-off|send to codex/i.test(text), "no hand-off promise yet (Task X8)");
      await context.close();
    }
  } finally {
    clearKnob("FAKE_OPENCLAW_APPROVALS");
    clearKnob("FAKE_OPENCLAW_RESOLVE");
    for (const id of started) await api("POST", `/api/sessions/${id}/stop`).catch(() => {});
  }
}
```

Create `src/ui/useApprovals.ts`:

```ts
// OpenClaw's pending approvals (Task X3's GET /api/sessions/approvals) for the Safety page and an open OpenClaw session's
// panel: read every 3 s while `active` (paused while the window is hidden, useInterval), one read at a time with the
// newest answer winning (latestRead.ts), each with a time limit (sessionsApi.ts). After a good read a failed one keeps
// the last list marked stale. Where sessions do not run (404 not_available) nothing can be pending, so the answer is an
// empty list, which is true. The server itself asks OpenClaw every 3 s, so a card shows at most about 6 s after OpenClaw
// asks.
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { ApiError } from "../api";
import { listApprovals, sessionProblem } from "../sessionsApi";
import type { ApprovalListResponse } from "../types";
import { useInterval } from "./components/useInterval";
import { failedLoad, loaded } from "./homeShared";
import type { Source } from "./homeShared";
import { createLatestRead } from "./latestRead";

export const APPROVALS_POLL_MS = 3000;
const NONE: ApprovalListResponse = { approvals: [], error: null };

export interface ApprovalsRead {
  source: Source<ApprovalListResponse>;
  // Read again now (after an answer was sent). The same function on every render while `active` stays the same.
  refresh: () => void;
}

export function useApprovals(active: boolean): ApprovalsRead {
  const [source, setSource] = useState<Source<ApprovalListResponse>>({ state: "loading" });
  const [reads] = useState(createLatestRead);
  const load = useCallback(
    (fresh: boolean) => {
      if (!active) return;
      if (fresh) reads.cancel();
      void reads.run(
        () => listApprovals(),
        (outcome) => {
          if (outcome.ok) {
            setSource(loaded(outcome.value));
            return;
          }
          if (outcome.error instanceof ApiError && outcome.error.status === 404 && outcome.error.message === "not_available") {
            setSource(loaded(NONE));
            return;
          }
          setSource((prev) => failedLoad(prev, sessionProblem(outcome.error)));
        }
      );
    },
    [active, reads]
  );
  useEffect(() => {
    load(true);
    // A read still waiting when the page goes away must not update it.
    return () => reads.cancel();
  }, [load, reads]);
  useInterval(() => load(false), active ? APPROVALS_POLL_MS : null);
  const refresh = useCallback(() => load(true), [load]);
  return { source, refresh };
}
```

Create `src/ui/components/ApprovalCard.tsx`:

```tsx
// OpenClaw's approval cards (SP4, ruling R16), on the Safety page and in an open OpenClaw session's panel. A card says
// what OpenClaw asks: "OpenClaw wants to run" with the command for an exec approval, OpenClaw's own summary for the
// other kinds. Allow once and Deny each ask first in Agent OS's own dialog; only after that confirm does exactly that
// answer go to `openclaw approvals resolve <id> allow-once|deny` (Task X3's POST /api/sessions/approvals/resolve). When
// OpenClaw refuses, its own words are shown in the dialog. Nothing is ever answered for you, and a card never names a
// folder (OpenClaw's list has none). A card OpenClaw could not match to one session says "from OpenClaw" where
// `showFrom` asks for it (the session panel). An answered card reads "You allowed it once" or "You said no" until a few
// seconds after OpenClaw's list drops it (approvalView, alertsShared.ts).
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { Check, CircleCheck, CircleHelp, CircleX, X } from "lucide-react";
import { resolveApproval, sessionGotNoAnswer, sessionProblem } from "../../sessionsApi";
import type { ApprovalCard as Card, ApprovalDecision } from "../../types";
import { APPROVAL_NO_ANSWER, FROM_OPENCLAW, approvalConfirm, approvalDoneHeading, approvalHeading, approvalView } from "../alertsShared";
import type { Answered } from "../alertsShared";
import AgentConfirmModal from "./AgentConfirmModal";
import { useInterval } from "./useInterval";
import "../alerts.css";

export default function ApprovalCard({
  card,
  answered,
  from,
  busy,
  onAnswer
}: {
  card: Card;
  answered: ApprovalDecision | null;
  from: boolean;
  busy: boolean;
  onAnswer: (decision: ApprovalDecision) => void;
}) {
  const heading = answered ? approvalDoneHeading(answered) : approvalHeading(card);
  const Icon = answered === "allow-once" ? CircleCheck : answered === "deny" ? CircleX : CircleHelp;
  return (
    <article className={`os-approval${answered ? " is-done" : ""}`} aria-label={heading}>
      <h3 className="os-approval__title">
        <Icon size={18} aria-hidden="true" />
        <span>{heading}</span>
        {from ? <span className="os-approval__from">{FROM_OPENCLAW}</span> : null}
      </h3>
      {card.kind === "exec" ? (
        <p className="os-approval__cmd os-mono">
          <span aria-hidden="true">$ </span>
          {card.summary}
        </p>
      ) : (
        <p className="os-approval__summary">{card.summary}</p>
      )}
      {answered ? null : (
        <>
          <div className="os-approval__acts">
            <button type="button" className="os-btn os-btn--secondary" disabled={busy} onClick={() => onAnswer("allow-once")}>
              <Check size={16} aria-hidden="true" />
              Allow once
            </button>
            <button type="button" className="os-btn os-btn--secondary" disabled={busy} onClick={() => onAnswer("deny")}>
              <X size={16} aria-hidden="true" />
              Deny
            </button>
          </div>
          <p className="os-approval__why">Agent OS never answers for you.</p>
        </>
      )}
    </article>
  );
}

type Asking = { card: Card; decision: ApprovalDecision; busy: boolean; error: string };

// The cards in a list, the confirm, and the answers given here. `empty` is drawn when there is no card (Safety's empty
// state); `onAnswered` reads OpenClaw's list again after an answer went through.
export function ApprovalList({
  cards,
  showFrom,
  empty = null,
  onAnswered
}: {
  cards: Card[];
  showFrom: boolean;
  empty?: ReactNode;
  onAnswered?: () => void;
}) {
  const [answered, setAnswered] = useState<Record<string, Answered>>({});
  const [asking, setAsking] = useState<Asking | null>(null);
  const [now, setNow] = useState(() => Date.now());
  const alive = useRef(true);
  useEffect(() => {
    alive.current = true;
    return () => {
      alive.current = false;
    };
  }, []);
  // A one-second clock only while an answered card waits to leave.
  useInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), Object.keys(answered).length > 0 ? 1000 : null);
  // A question about a card OpenClaw no longer lists (answered elsewhere, or it expired) goes with it, unless its answer
  // is on its way or the dialog shows OpenClaw's error, which the person should be able to read.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (asking && !asking.busy && !asking.error && !cards.some((card) => card.id === asking.card.id)) setAsking(null);
  }, [cards, asking]);
  const items = approvalView(cards, answered, now);

  async function send() {
    if (!asking || asking.busy) return;
    const { card, decision } = asking;
    setAsking({ card, decision, busy: true, error: "" });
    try {
      await resolveApproval(card.id, decision);
      if (!alive.current) return;
      const at = Date.now();
      setAnswered((prev) => ({ ...prev, [card.id]: { decision, at, card } }));
      setNow(at);
      setAsking(null);
      onAnswered?.();
    } catch (error) {
      if (!alive.current) return;
      // No answer at all is not a refusal: OpenClaw may have the answer already (Q31).
      const words = sessionGotNoAnswer(error) ? APPROVAL_NO_ANSWER : sessionProblem(error);
      setAsking((current) => (current && current.card.id === card.id ? { ...current, busy: false, error: words } : current));
    }
  }

  const copy = asking ? approvalConfirm(asking.card, asking.decision) : null;
  if (items.length === 0 && !asking) return <>{empty}</>;
  return (
    <>
      {items.length > 0 ? (
        <ul className="os-approvals" aria-label="OpenClaw approvals">
          {items.map((item) => (
            <li key={item.card.id}>
              <ApprovalCard
                card={item.card}
                answered={item.answered}
                from={showFrom && item.card.sessionId === null}
                busy={asking?.busy === true && asking.card.id === item.card.id}
                onAnswer={(decision) => setAsking({ card: item.card, decision, busy: false, error: "" })}
              />
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      ) : (
        empty
      )}
      {asking && copy ? (
        <AgentConfirmModal
          title={copy.title}
          confirmLabel={copy.confirm}
          busy={asking.busy}
          onConfirm={() => void send()}
          onClose={() => {
            if (!asking.busy) setAsking(null);
          }}
        >
          <p>{copy.body}</p>
          {asking.error ? (
            <p className="os-approval__error" role="alert">
              {asking.error}
            </p>
          ) : null}
        </AgentConfirmModal>
      ) : null}
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Pending approvals (SP4): OpenClaw's approval cards (its terminal can't show its own prompts, so Agent OS does), each
// answered only after your click and a confirm (ruling R16; ApprovalCard.tsx), then one row for every other agent
// session that waits for you, which you answer in its own terminal in Sessions. Agent OS never answers for you.
//
// The words say only what is known. Safety does not read Team Rooms, and a Team Room can be paused for the person's
// decision to save a file, so this page never says "nothing is waiting for you": it says nothing from OpenClaw is
// waiting here (and only when OpenClaw could be asked), and where a decision that exists today is made.
import { ArrowRight, CircleHelp, Eye, Inbox } from "lucide-react";
import { navigateTo } from "../../nav";
import { terminalQuestions } from "../alertsShared";
import { useApprovals } from "../useApprovals";
import { useSessionsList } from "../useSessionsList";
import { ApprovalList } from "./ApprovalCard";
import Banner from "./Banner";
import EmptyState from "./EmptyState";
import StatusWord from "./StatusWord";

function ApprovalsEmpty() {
  return (
    <div className="os-saf-approvals">
      <EmptyState
        icon={Inbox}
        title="Nothing from OpenClaw is waiting here"
        body="When OpenClaw wants to run a command, a card with the exact command shows up here and in its session. You choose Allow once or Deny. Agent OS never answers for you. A Team Room that is waiting to save a file asks in that Team Room."
      />
      <div className="os-saf-ghost" role="group" aria-label="Example of a request card, not a real request">
        <p className="os-saf-ghost__cap"><Eye size={14} aria-hidden="true" /> What a request will look like (example, not real)</p>
        <p className="os-saf-ghost__title"><CircleHelp size={16} aria-hidden="true" /> OpenClaw wants to run</p>
        <p className="os-saf-ghost__cmd os-mono">$ npm test</p>
        <div className="os-saf-ghost__acts">
          <button type="button" className="os-btn os-btn--secondary" disabled>Allow once</button>
          <button type="button" className="os-btn os-btn--secondary" disabled>Deny</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

export default function SafetyApprovals() {
  const approvals = useApprovals(true);
  const { source } = useSessionsList();
  const asks = terminalQuestions(source.state === "ok" && !source.stale ? source.data.sessions : []);
  const read = approvals.source;
  const cards = read.state === "ok" ? read.data.approvals : [];
  const pollError = read.state === "ok" ? read.data.error : null;
  // "Nothing from OpenClaw is waiting here" only when that is known: the last read worked and OpenClaw could be asked.
  const known = read.state === "ok" && !read.stale && !pollError;
  return (
    <section className="os-saf-section" aria-labelledby="os-saf-approvals-title">
      <div className="os-saf-section__head">
        <h2 id="os-saf-approvals-title">Pending approvals</h2>
        <p className="os-saf-section__quiet">What agents are asking you</p>
      </div>
      {pollError ? <Banner tone="warn">{pollError}</Banner> : null}
      {read.state === "error" ? <Banner tone="warn">{read.message}</Banner> : null}
      {read.state === "loading" ? (
        <p className="os-saf-approvals__loading">
          <StatusWord state="loading" />
        </p>
      ) : (
        <ApprovalList cards={cards} showFrom={false} empty={known ? <ApprovalsEmpty /> : null} onAnswered={approvals.refresh} />
      )}
      {asks.length > 0 ? (
        <ul className="os-saf-waits" aria-label="Sessions waiting for you">
          {asks.map((item) => (
            <li key={item.id} className="os-saf-wait">
              <CircleHelp size={18} aria-hidden="true" />
              <p>
                <b>{item.title}</b> · {item.text}
                <span className="os-saf-wait__sub">It asks in its own terminal, so you answer it in Sessions. Agent OS never answers for you.</span>
              </p>

                Open session
                <ArrowRight size={16} aria-hidden="true" />
              </button>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      ) : null}
    </section>
  );
}
```
