- [ ] **Step 14: Home's strip.**

Rewrite `src/ui/components/WaitingStrip.tsx` with exactly this content. FleetPage already mounts it first and already passes the sessions to the Orbit, so FleetPage needs no change.

```tsx
// The "Waiting for you" strip above Home's heading (the prototype's index.html strip): one row for each agent session
// that waits for you, the longest wait first, then each one whose plan ran out, at most STRIP_MAX rows, each with Open
// session. It reads the shared sessions list, so it agrees with the tab markers, the top-bar badge and the Orbit (ruling
// R22). Nothing shows while nothing needs you, or while the list could not be refreshed (Home's own banner says so then).
import { ArrowRight, CircleHelp, CirclePause } from "lucide-react";
import { navigateTo } from "../../nav";
import { STRIP_MAX, homeStripItems, stripMore } from "../alertsShared";
import { useSessionsList } from "../useSessionsList";
import "../alerts.css";

export default function WaitingStrip() {
  const { source } = useSessionsList();
  const items = homeStripItems(source.state === "ok" && !source.stale ? source.data.sessions : []);
  if (items.length === 0) return null;
  const shown = items.slice(0, STRIP_MAX);
  const more = stripMore(items.length - shown.length);
  return (
    <section className="os-strip" aria-label="Waiting for you">
      {shown.map((item) => (
        <div key={item.id} className={`os-strip__row os-strip__row--${item.kind}`} role="group" aria-label={item.title}>
          {item.kind === "waiting" ? <CircleHelp size={20} aria-hidden="true" /> : <CirclePause size={20} aria-hidden="true" />}
          <p className="os-strip__text">
            <b className="os-trunc">{item.title}</b>
            <span className="os-strip__what">{item.text}</span>
            {item.kind === "waiting" ? <span className="os-strip__quiet">Agent OS never answers for you.</span> : null}
          </p>
          <button type="button" className="os-btn os-btn--secondary" onClick={() => navigateTo("sessions", { session: item.id })}>
            Open session
            <ArrowRight size={16} aria-hidden="true" />
          </button>
        </div>
      ))}
      {more ? <p className="os-strip__more">{more}</p> : null}
    </section>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 16: The session panel: alert lines, OpenClaw's cards, the gauges (`SessionSidePanel.tsx`, `sessions.css`).**

Rewrite `src/ui/components/SessionSidePanel.tsx` with exactly this content. The SP3 parts are unchanged. Keep `recordingKept(session.recordingBytes) ? (` exactly as it is, because test/sessions-page-logic.test.js reads it.

```tsx
// The right-hand side of the Sessions page for the selected session (the prototype's panel): the folder and agent, the
// state in words and its one line, the alert lines under it (hooks switched off and why, the trust line, basic alerts;
// panelAlertLines in alertsShared.ts), OpenClaw's approval cards for an open OpenClaw session (its own, and every card
// OpenClaw could not match to one session, marked "from OpenClaw", ruling R16), the Live meter (every row; Model,
// Context used, Plan used and Cost so far from Claude Code's status line, Task X2b; "—" where nothing is known, with the
// hint "— means unknown") and the footer with Recorded, Stop session and the keyboard hints (desktop app only). An ended
// session shows Resume conversation (or why it can't) and Open recording instead of Stop. The panel keeps its own
// one-second clock for "Running for", so the page (and its terminal) is not re-rendered for it. `note` is the Stop result
// note the page picks (panelStopNote: the server's own answer right after a Stop here, otherwise the session's own rule),
// shown under the state line.
import { useState } from "react";
import type { RefObject } from "react";
import { CircleDot, Folder, GitBranch, History, Info, OctagonX } from "lucide-react";
import type { SessionSummary } from "../../types";
import { collapseHomePath } from "../agentsShared";
import { approvalsForSession, panelAlertLines } from "../alertsShared";
import { resumeConfirmCopy, sessionPanelLine, sessionStateWord } from "../sessionsShared";
import { meterRows, panelFolder, recordingKept } from "../sessionsPageShared";
import { useApprovals } from "../useApprovals";
import { ApprovalList } from "./ApprovalCard";
import Meter from "./Meter";
import StatusWord from "./StatusWord";
import { useInterval } from "./useInterval";

export default function SessionSidePanel({
  session,
  note,
  hints,
  headingRef,
  onStop,
  onResume,
  onOpenRecording
}: {
  session: SessionSummary;
  note: string | null;
  hints: Array<{ keys: string; word: string }>;
  headingRef: RefObject<HTMLHeadingElement>;
  onStop: () => void;
  onResume: () => void;
  onOpenRecording: () => void;
}) {
  const [now, setNow] = useState(() => Date.now());
  const ended = session.status === "exited";
  useInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), ended ? null : 1000);
  const word = sessionStateWord(session);
  const rows = meterRows(session, now);
  const alertLines = panelAlertLines(session);
  // OpenClaw's cards are read only while this panel shows an open OpenClaw session (useApprovals asks every 3 s).
  const clawOpen = session.kind === "agent" && session.agentId === "openclaw" && !ended;
  const approvals = useApprovals(clawOpen);
  const listed = clawOpen && approvals.source.state === "ok" ? approvals.source.data : null;
  const cards = listed ? approvalsForSession(listed.approvals, session.id) : [];
  // Why Resume can't be pressed: the server's reason (decision Q36), as the Resume confirm words it (Task U1).
  const blocked = ended ? resumeConfirmCopy(session).blocked : null;
  const where = panelFolder(session);
  return (
    <aside className="os-sess-panel" aria-label="Session details">
      <div className="os-sess-panel__scroll">
        <header className="os-sess-panel__head">
          <div className="os-sess-panel__folder">
            <Folder size={20} aria-hidden="true" />
            <h2 ref={headingRef} tabIndex={-1} className="os-trunc" title={session.folderShown === false ? where : collapseHomePath(session.folder)}>
              {where}
            </h2>
            <span className="os-sess-panel__agent">{session.agentLabel}</span>
          </div>
          {session.branch ? (
            <p className="os-sess-panel__branch">
              <GitBranch size={16} aria-hidden="true" />
              <code className="os-mono os-trunc" title={session.branch}>
                {session.branch}
              </code>
            </p>
          ) : null}
          <p className="os-sess-panel__stat">
            <StatusWord state={word.state} label={word.label} />
          </p>
          <p className="os-sess-panel__line">{sessionPanelLine(session, now)}</p>
          {alertLines.map((line) => (
            <p key={line} className="os-sess-panel__alert">
              <Info size={15} aria-hidden="true" />
              <span>{line}</span>
            </p>
          ))}
          {note ? (
            <p className="os-sess-panel__note" role="status">
              {note}
            </p>
          ) : null}
          {ended ? (
            <div className="os-sess-panel__ended">
              <button
                type="button"
                className="os-btn os-btn--primary"
                onClick={onResume}
                disabled={blocked !== null}
                aria-describedby={blocked ? "os-sess-resume-why" : undefined}
              >
                <History size={16} aria-hidden="true" />
                Resume conversation
              </button>
              {/* A removed recording (0 bytes) has no row in Runs; the line above already says so. */}
              {recordingKept(session.recordingBytes) ? (
                <button type="button" className="os-btn os-btn--secondary" onClick={onOpenRecording}>
                  <CircleDot size={16} aria-hidden="true" />
                  Open recording
                </button>
              ) : null}
              {blocked ? (
                <p id="os-sess-resume-why" className="os-sess-panel__why">
                  {blocked}
                </p>
              ) : null}
            </div>
          ) : null}
        </header>
        {clawOpen ? (
          // Hidden by CSS while empty (no card, no error).
          <div className="os-sess-panel__asks">
            <ApprovalList cards={cards} showFrom onAnswered={approvals.refresh} />
            {listed?.error ? <p className="os-sess-panel__why">{listed.error}</p> : null}
          </div>
        ) : null}
        <section className="os-sess-panel__sec" aria-label="Live meter">
          <div className="os-sess-panel__rh">
            Live meter<span className="os-sess-panel__hint">— means unknown</span>
          </div>
          {rows.map((row) =>
            row.gauge ? (
              <div key={row.id} className="os-sess-panel__gauge">
                <Meter label={row.dim ? `${row.label} · ${row.dim}` : row.label} value={row.gauge.percent / 100} tone={row.gauge.tone} detail={row.gauge.detail} />
              </div>
            ) : (
              <dl key={row.id} className="os-sess-kv">
                <div className="os-sess-kv__row">
                  <dt>{row.label}</dt>
                  <dd>
                    {row.value === null ? (
                      <>
                        <span className="os-mono os-sess-kv__dash" aria-hidden="true">
                          —
                        </span>
                        <span className="os-visually-hidden">unknown</span>
                      </>
                    ) : (
                      <>
                        {row.id === "time" ? <span className="os-mono">{row.value}</span> : row.value}
                        {row.dim ? <span className="os-sess-kv__dim"> · {row.dim}</span> : null}
                      </>
                    )}
                  </dd>
                </div>
              </dl>
            )
          )}
        </section>
      </div>
      <footer className="os-sess-panel__foot">
        <div className="os-sess-panel__rec">
          <span className="os-sess-panel__recorded">
            <CircleDot size={15} aria-hidden="true" />
            Recorded
          </span>
          {!ended ? (
            <button type="button" className="os-btn os-btn--danger os-sess-panel__stop" onClick={onStop}>
              <OctagonX size={16} aria-hidden="true" />
              Stop session
            </button>
          ) : null}
        </div>
        {hints.length ? (
          <div className="os-sess-keys" role="group" aria-label="Keyboard shortcuts">
            {hints.map((hint) => (
              <span key={hint.keys}>
                <kbd className="os-kbd">{hint.keys}</kbd>
                {hint.word}
              </span>
            ))}
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </footer>
    </aside>
  );
}
```

```tsx
  // The desktop app's one-time note about notifications (K17), until "Got it" (kept in this browser; a webview that
  // refuses storage shows it again after a reload, which is harmless).
  const [notifyDismissed, setNotifyDismissed] = useState(() => {
    try {
      return window.localStorage.getItem(NOTIFY_NOTE_KEY) === "1";
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  });
  function dismissNotifyNote() {
    setNotifyDismissed(true);
    try {
      window.localStorage.setItem(NOTIFY_NOTE_KEY, "1");
    } catch {
      // A locked-down webview: the note stays hidden until the page reloads.
    }
  }
```

### Task U6: Split view (two panes, divider, panel follows the focused pane, no duplicate attach, ⌘\)

Today the Sessions page shows one terminal: the selected tab's (`src/pages/SessionsPage.tsx:436-448` at `548786d`), with its side panel on the right. The spec's SP4 "Split" item asks for two sessions side by side. This task builds it on the page only: no server change, no route, no new type in `src/types.ts`. The server already lets any number of windows attach to a session (`manager.js:1283-1290`), so "no duplicate attach of the same session in both panes" is a rule of the page, kept by one pure function (`alignSplit`) and checked by the logic test and the probe.

How it works, in plain words: the selected tab (`?session=`) is always the focused pane, so the side panel, Stop and Resume already follow it and need nothing new. Split view adds a second pane next to it. Clicking or typing in a pane makes it the focused pane. Clicking the tab of the session in the other pane only moves the focus; clicking any other tab puts that session in the focused pane. A pane is keyed by its terminal key, so turning split view on or off, or moving the focus, never reattaches a terminal that stays on screen. The Split view button sits in the tab bar (both modes); ⌘\ (Ctrl+Shift+\ on Windows and Linux) toggles it in the desktop app, and the panel footer gains the ⌘\ hint there. Split view is kept per window: `sessionStorage`, so a reload and leaving the page keep it, and a second window starts with one terminal.

Its tests never start a real agent: the logic test is pure, and the probe drives the TUI-like fake agent (`test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs`) on the UI audit harness's throwaway server.

The prototype instead leaves split view when another tab is clicked. Why: split view stays as the person set it; the other pane is untouched. Cost: someone who wanted to leave split view presses Split view.
   - **U6-e Turning split view on** puts the selected tab on the left (the focused pane, where the keyboard already is) and the first of `secondPaneChoices` on the right (the next open tab in tab order, else an ended one). Cost: the person picks another right pane by focusing it and clicking a tab.
   - **U6-f Ended and dismissed sessions.** An ended session may sit in a pane (it keeps its last screen while that pane shows it, like SP3's single terminal). A pane whose session leaves the tabs (dismissed) gets the next of `secondPaneChoices`; with fewer than two tabs split view ends, and the button can't be pressed ("Split view needs two sessions."). Cost: none.
   - **U6-g The divider** keeps the left pane at 28 % to 72 % of the width (prototype), moves 2 % per arrow key, and Home or a double click put it back in the middle (prototype). The share is stored as a fraction rounded to 0.001. Cost: none.
   - **U6-h Focus follows focus.** A pane becomes the focused pane when anything in it gets the keyboard focus or a pointer press (its terminal, its header, its Reconnect button), like the tabs' automatic activation. Cost: tabbing through a pane's header shows its details on the way.
   - **U6-i While the tab asked for is not listed yet** (a session started a moment ago, the list is read every 5 s), split view is not realigned; the page shows another tab meanwhile, as SP3 does. Why: otherwise the focus would jump to the fallback tab and the new session would land in the wrong pane. Cost: for at most one list read the panes show the old pair.
   - **U6-j The focused pane's frame is cobalt in split view** (prototype `.ss-pane.is-focus .term`), also while the keyboard is on the divider or the panel. One-pane view keeps SP3's `:focus-within` rule.
   - **U6-k Small screens.** At ≤ 1320 px the button shows only its icon (prototype); at ≤ 900 px (the off-canvas range, where the panel already goes under the terminal) the two panes stack, half each, without the divider. The panel footer's hints may wrap (three hints with "Ctrl+Shift+…" do not fit in 304 px).
5. **Risks.** Two xterm instances (and two WebGL contexts where WebGL is on) in one window: both are disposed when their pane goes, and WebGL falls back to the DOM on a lost context (SP3). A divider drag re-renders the page on every pointer move; the terminals' own effects do not re-run (their props do not change) and their fit is throttled to one per frame. The probe runs on a Mac, so Ctrl+Shift+\ is covered by the logic test only. The anchors in `SessionsPage.tsx` can move under U5's edits (Step 0).
6. **For E1:** the screenshots `split/1470x956/{split,split-dragged,split-ended,split-desktop}.png`, `split/1280x720/split.png` and `split/1024x640/split.png` go into the Q32 message; `.github/release-notes.md` "Known limits" still says there is no split view (E1 updates it with the other SP4 lines); spec line 495 "Split view comes in SP4 (SP3 ships tabs)" is Task D1's.

```js
test("SPLIT_KEY and clampSplit: the left pane keeps 28 % to 72 % of the width, the middle to start", () => {
  assert.equal(split.SPLIT_KEY, "agentos.sessions.split.v1");
  assert.equal(split.clampSplit(0.5), 0.5);
  assert.equal(split.clampSplit(0.1), 0.28);
  assert.equal(split.clampSplit(0.95), 0.72);
  assert.equal(split.clampSplit(0.30000000000000004), 0.3, "rounded, so the arrow keys never pile up tiny errors");
  assert.equal(split.clampSplit(Number.NaN), 0.5);
  assert.equal(split.clampSplit(Infinity), 0.5);
  assert.equal(split.clampSplit("0.4"), 0.5, "not a number (a broken stored value): the middle");
  assert.deepEqual(split.SPLIT_OFF, OFF);
});

test("secondPaneChoices and canSplit: every other tab, open ones first; split view needs two tabs", () => {
  const tabs = [s("a"), s("e", "exited"), s("b", "idle"), s("c", "waiting")];
  assert.deepEqual(split.secondPaneChoices(tabs, "a").map((t) => t.id), ["b", "c", "e"]);
  assert.deepEqual(split.secondPaneChoices(tabs, "b").map((t) => t.id), ["a", "c", "e"]);
  assert.deepEqual(split.secondPaneChoices([s("a")], "a"), []);
  assert.equal(split.canSplit([s("a")]), false);
  assert.equal(split.canSplit([]), false);
  assert.equal(split.canSplit([s("a"), s("e", "exited")]), true, "an ended tab can sit in a pane");
});

test("toggleSplit: on puts the selected tab left and the next open tab right; off keeps the width; one tab does nothing", () => {
  const tabs = [s("a"), s("e", "exited"), s("b")];
  const on = split.toggleSplit({ ...OFF, ratio: 0.4 }, tabs, "e");
  assert.deepEqual(on, { on: true, panes: ["e", "a"], focus: 0, ratio: 0.4 }, "the selected tab stays where the keyboard is: the left, focused pane");
  assert.deepEqual(split.toggleSplit(on, tabs, "e"), { on: false, panes: null, focus: 0, ratio: 0.4 }, "off keeps the width for next time");
  const alone = { ...OFF };
  assert.equal(split.toggleSplit(alone, [s("a")], "a"), alone, "one tab: the very same state");
  assert.equal(split.toggleSplit(alone, tabs, "missing"), alone, "no selected tab: the very same state");
});

test("alignSplit: picking the other pane's tab moves the focus only, never the same session in both panes", () => {
  const tabs = [s("a"), s("b"), s("c")];
  const state = { on: true, panes: ["a", "b"], focus: 0, ratio: 0.5 };
  assert.deepEqual(split.alignSplit(state, tabs, "b"), { on: true, panes: ["a", "b"], focus: 1, ratio: 0.5 });
  assert.deepEqual(split.alignSplit({ ...state, focus: 1 }, tabs, "a"), { on: true, panes: ["a", "b"], focus: 0, ratio: 0.5 });
  // Every way through: whatever is picked, the picked tab is the focused pane and the panes never hold one session twice.
  let current = state;
  for (const pick of ["b", "c", "a", "c", "b", "b", "a", "c"]) {
    current = split.alignSplit(current, tabs, pick);
    assert.equal(current.on, true);
    assert.notEqual(current.panes[0], current.panes[1], `after picking ${pick}`);
    assert.equal(current.panes[current.focus], pick, `the picked tab is the focused pane (${pick})`);
  }
});

test("alignSplit: a tab in neither pane takes the focused pane's place (a click, ⌘1-9, a link, a new session)", () => {
  const tabs = [s("a"), s("b"), s("c")];
  assert.deepEqual(split.alignSplit({ on: true, panes: ["a", "b"], focus: 1, ratio: 0.6 }, tabs, "c"), { on: true, panes: ["a", "c"], focus: 1, ratio: 0.6 });
  assert.deepEqual(split.alignSplit({ on: true, panes: ["a", "b"], focus: 0, ratio: 0.6 }, tabs, "c"), { on: true, panes: ["c", "b"], focus: 0, ratio: 0.6 });
});

test("alignSplit: a pane whose session left the tabs gets the next one; with one tab left split view ends", () => {
  const state = { on: true, panes: ["a", "b"], focus: 0, ratio: 0.4 };
  // b was dismissed: the open c takes its place before the ended e.
  assert.deepEqual(split.alignSplit(state, [s("a"), s("e", "exited"), s("c")], "a"), { on: true, panes: ["a", "c"], focus: 0, ratio: 0.4 });
  // a (the focused pane) was dismissed and the page picked b: b is the focused pane now, and a's place goes to c.
  assert.deepEqual(split.alignSplit(state, [s("b"), s("c")], "b"), { on: true, panes: ["c", "b"], focus: 1, ratio: 0.4 });
  // Only an ended tab is left next to a: it is still a session, so it takes the place.
  assert.deepEqual(split.alignSplit(state, [s("a"), s("e", "exited")], "a"), { on: true, panes: ["a", "e"], focus: 0, ratio: 0.4 });
  assert.deepEqual(split.alignSplit(state, [s("a")], "a"), { on: false, panes: null, focus: 0, ratio: 0.4 }, "one tab: split view ends");
  assert.deepEqual(split.alignSplit(state, [], ""), { on: false, panes: null, focus: 0, ratio: 0.4 }, "no tabs");
  const off = { on: false, panes: null, focus: 0, ratio: 0.4 };
  assert.equal(split.alignSplit(off, [s("a"), s("b")], "a"), off, "off stays off, the very same state");
});

test("alignSplit returns the very same object when nothing changes, and again after its own answer", () => {

  for (const pick of ["a", "b", "c"]) {
    const once = split.alignSplit(state, tabs, pick);

  const broken = { on: true, panes: null, focus: 0, ratio: 0.5 };

test("split view is kept per window: parse and serialize, and anything broken reads as off", () => {
  const on = { on: true, panes: ["a", "b"], focus: 1, ratio: 0.4 };
  assert.equal(split.serializeSplitState(on), '{"v":1,"on":true,"panes":["a","b"],"focus":1,"ratio":0.4}');
  assert.deepEqual(split.parseSplitState(split.serializeSplitState(on)), on);
  const offWide = { on: false, panes: null, focus: 0, ratio: 0.66 };
  assert.deepEqual(split.parseSplitState(split.serializeSplitState(offWide)), offWide, "off keeps its width");
  for (const raw of [null, "", "{", "null", "[]", '"on"', '{"v":2,"on":true,"panes":["a","b"]}', '{"on":true,"panes":["a","b"]}']) {
    assert.deepEqual(split.parseSplitState(raw), OFF, String(raw));
  }
  assert.deepEqual(split.parseSplitState('{"v":1,"on":true,"panes":["a","a"],"focus":0,"ratio":0.5}'), OFF, "the same session twice is never restored");
  assert.deepEqual(split.parseSplitState('{"v":1,"on":true,"panes":["a"],"focus":0,"ratio":0.5}'), OFF);
  assert.deepEqual(split.parseSplitState('{"v":1,"on":true,"panes":["a",""],"focus":0,"ratio":0.5}'), OFF);
  assert.deepEqual(split.parseSplitState('{"v":1,"on":true,"panes":["a","b"],"focus":7,"ratio":3}'), { on: true, panes: ["a", "b"], focus: 0, ratio: 0.72 });

test("nextLiveShown: an ended session keeps its last screen while a pane shows it", () => {
  const empty = new Set();
  const one = split.nextLiveShown(empty, [{ key: "a:0", status: "live" }]);
  assert.deepEqual([...one], ["a:0"]);
  assert.equal(split.nextLiveShown(one, [{ key: "a:0", status: "exited" }]), one, "it ended on screen: kept, the very same set");
  const both = split.nextLiveShown(one, [{ key: "a:0", status: "exited" }, { key: "b:0", status: "idle" }]);
  assert.deepEqual([...both].sort(), ["a:0", "b:0"], "split view on: the ended pane keeps its screen");
  assert.deepEqual([...split.nextLiveShown(both, [{ key: "b:0", status: "idle" }])], ["b:0"], "it left the screen: gone");
  assert.deepEqual([...split.nextLiveShown(empty, [{ key: "e:0", status: "exited" }])], [], "a pane opened on an ended session shows the ended view");
});
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write `src/ui/splitShared.ts`.**

```ts
// Split view on the Sessions page (spec SP4, Split; Task U6): two panes side by side, each with its own header, a
// divider to drag between them, and the side panel following the focused pane. One terminal per pane, and the same
// session is never in both panes. The selected tab (?session=) is always the focused pane, so the side panel, Stop
// and Resume need nothing new. Split view is kept per window: the page stores serializeSplitState in sessionStorage
// under SPLIT_KEY, so a reload and leaving the page keep it, and a second window starts with one terminal.
// `import type` only (decision P14): test/sessions-split-logic.test.js loads this file straight from src/, so the key
// names in splitKeys are written here again, and that test keeps them equal to shortcutHints in sessionsShared.ts.
import type { SessionSummary } from "../types";

type Pane = Pick<SessionSummary, "id" | "status">;

export const SPLIT_KEY = "agentos.sessions.split.v1";
// The left pane's share of the width: the prototype's 28 % to 72 %, the middle to start, 2 % per arrow key.
export const SPLIT_MIN = 0.28;
export const SPLIT_MAX = 0.72;
export const SPLIT_DEFAULT = 0.5;
export const SPLIT_KEY_STEP = 0.02;

// on: split view is shown. panes: the two sessions, left then right (null while off). focus: the pane whose session
// is the selected tab (the side panel follows it). ratio: the left pane's share, kept while split view is off.
export interface SplitState {
  on: boolean;
  panes: [string, string] | null;
  focus: 0 | 1;
  ratio: number;
}
export const SPLIT_OFF: SplitState = { on: false, panes: null, focus: 0, ratio: SPLIT_DEFAULT };

function splitOff(ratio: number): SplitState {
  return { on: false, panes: null, focus: 0, ratio };
}

// The left pane's share, kept between SPLIT_MIN and SPLIT_MAX and rounded to 0.001 (so the arrow keys never pile up
// tiny errors). Anything that is not a finite number, a broken stored value for example, is the middle.
export function clampSplit(ratio: number): number {
  if (typeof ratio !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(ratio)) return SPLIT_DEFAULT;
  return Math.round(Math.min(SPLIT_MAX, Math.max(SPLIT_MIN, ratio)) * 1000) / 1000;
}

// The sessions that can go next to `firstId`: every other tab, open ones first, then ended ones, each in tab order.
export function secondPaneChoices<T extends Pane>(sessions: readonly T[], firstId: string): T[] {
  const others = sessions.filter((session) => session.id !== firstId);
  return [...others.filter((session) => session.status !== "exited"), ...others.filter((session) => session.status === "exited")];
}

// Split view needs two tabs (an ended tab counts: it is still a session, with its last screen).
export function canSplit(tabs: readonly Pane[]): boolean {
  return tabs.length >= 2;
}

// The Split view button and ⌘\. Off → on: the selected tab on the left (the focused pane, where the keyboard already
// is) and the first of secondPaneChoices on the right. On → off: the focused pane's session stays on screen alone, and
// the width is kept for next time. With no selected tab or no second tab, the very same state comes back.
export function toggleSplit(state: SplitState, tabs: readonly Pane[], selectedId: string): SplitState {
  if (state.on) return splitOff(clampSplit(state.ratio));
  const first = tabs.find((tab) => tab.id === selectedId);
  const second = first ? secondPaneChoices(tabs, first.id)[0] : undefined;
  if (!first || !second) return state;
  return { on: true, panes: [first.id, second.id], focus: 0, ratio: clampSplit(state.ratio) };
}

// Keeps split view true to the tabs and the selected tab, after every change of either:
// - the selected tab is always the focused pane: when it is the other pane's session only the focus moves; when it is
//   in neither pane (a tab clicked, ⌘1-9, a link, a session just started) it takes the focused pane's place;
// - a pane whose session left the tabs (dismissed) gets the next of secondPaneChoices; with fewer than two tabs, or
//   no listed selected tab, split view ends;
// - the same session is never in both panes.
// The very same object comes back when nothing changes, so the page can store the answer without looping.
export function alignSplit(state: SplitState, tabs: readonly Pane[], selectedId: string): SplitState {
  if (!state.on) return state;
  const listed = new Set(tabs.map((tab) => tab.id));
  if (!state.panes || tabs.length < 2 || !listed.has(selectedId)) return splitOff(state.ratio);
  const [left, right] = state.panes;
  let focus: 0 | 1 = state.focus;
  let panes: [string, string] = [left, right];
  if (selectedId === left) focus = 0;
  else if (selectedId === right) focus = 1;
  else panes = focus === 0 ? [selectedId, right] : [left, selectedId];
  const other: 0 | 1 = focus === 0 ? 1 : 0;
  if (!listed.has(panes[other]) || panes[other] === panes[focus]) {
    const next = secondPaneChoices(tabs, panes[focus])[0];
    if (!next) return splitOff(state.ratio);
    panes = focus === 0 ? [panes[0], next.id] : [next.id, panes[1]];
  }
  if (focus === state.focus && panes[0] === left && panes[1] === right) return state;
  return { on: true, panes, focus, ratio: state.ratio };
}

// A new width from the divider; the very same state when it does not change.
export function withRatio(state: SplitState, ratio: number): SplitState {
  const next = clampSplit(ratio);
  return next === state.ratio ? state : { ...state, ratio: next };
}

// What this window kept (sessionStorage). Anything broken, of another version, or holding one session twice is off,
// with the middle width unless a good width was kept.
export function parseSplitState(raw: string | null): SplitState {
  if (!raw) return splitOff(SPLIT_DEFAULT);
  let value: unknown;
  try {
    value = JSON.parse(raw);
  } catch {
    return splitOff(SPLIT_DEFAULT);
  }
  if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) return splitOff(SPLIT_DEFAULT);
  const stored = value as { v?: unknown; on?: unknown; panes?: unknown; focus?: unknown; ratio?: unknown };
  if (stored.v !== 1) return splitOff(SPLIT_DEFAULT);
  const ratio = clampSplit(typeof stored.ratio === "number" ? stored.ratio : SPLIT_DEFAULT);
  const ids: unknown[] = Array.isArray(stored.panes) ? stored.panes : [];
  const [a, b] = ids;
  const panes: [string, string] | null =
    ids.length === 2 && typeof a === "string" && typeof b === "string" && a !== "" && b !== "" && a !== b ? [a, b] : null;
  if (stored.on !== true || !panes) return splitOff(ratio);
  return { on: true, panes, focus: stored.focus === 1 ? 1 : 0, ratio };
}

export function serializeSplitState(state: SplitState): string {
  return JSON.stringify({ v: 1, on: state.on, panes: state.on ? state.panes : null, focus: state.focus, ratio: clampSplit(state.ratio) });
}

// The terminals that stay on screen after their session ended (SP3: a session that ends while it is on screen keeps
// its last screen until it leaves the screen). `shown` is what the panes show now: an open session's terminal key is
// added, a key no pane shows any more is dropped, and an ended one stays only if it was there already. The very same
// set comes back when nothing changes.
export function nextLiveShown(prev: ReadonlySet<string>, shown: ReadonlyArray<{ key: string; status: string }>): ReadonlySet<string> {
  const next = new Set<string>();
  for (const pane of shown) if (pane.status !== "exited" || prev.has(pane.key)) next.add(pane.key);
  if (next.size === prev.size && [...next].every((key) => prev.has(key))) return prev;
  return next;
}

// The divider: where the pointer is, as the left pane's share of the panes' box (null for a box with no width), and
// the keys (ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move it 2 %, Home puts it back in the middle; any other key is not the divider's).
export function ratioFromPointer(clientX: number, left: number, width: number): number | null {
  if (!Number.isFinite(clientX) || !Number.isFinite(left) || !(width > 0)) return null;
  return clampSplit((clientX - left) / width);
}
export function dividerKeyRatio(key: string, ratio: number): number | null {
  if (key === "ArrowLeft") return clampSplit(ratio - SPLIT_KEY_STEP);
  if (key === "ArrowRight") return clampSplit(ratio + SPLIT_KEY_STEP);
  if (key === "Home") return SPLIT_DEFAULT;
  return null;
}

// The words (Task U6; the owner reviews them at E1): the button's name and tooltip, the divider's name, and a pane
// header's name. The key is named only where the page receives it (the desktop app), like the New session button.
export const SPLIT_LABEL = "Split view";
export const SPLIT_NEEDS_TWO = "Split view needs two sessions.";
export const SPLIT_DIVIDER_LABEL = "Resize the two terminals";
const SPLIT_HINT = "Show two sessions side by side";
export function splitKeys(isMac: boolean): string {
  return isMac ? "⌘\\" : "Ctrl+Shift+\\";
}
export function splitButtonHint({ isMac, desktop, possible }: { isMac: boolean; desktop: boolean; possible: boolean }): string {
  if (!possible) return SPLIT_NEEDS_TWO;
  return desktop ? `${SPLIT_HINT} (${splitKeys(isMac)})` : SPLIT_HINT;
}
export function paneHeadLabel(title: string): string {
  return `${title}, show its details`;
}
```

```ts
// The only keys a terminal leaves to Agent OS: ⌘K, ⌘T and ⌘1-9 on a Mac; Ctrl+Shift+K/T/1-9 elsewhere.
// Everything else goes to the agent, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+R included. A browser keeps ⌘T and ⌘1-9 (Ctrl+T,
// Ctrl+1-9, Ctrl+Shift+T) for itself, so in browser mode only the palette key is Agent OS's. ⌘\ (split)
// arrives with SP4 and is not taken yet.
export function isAppShortcut(event: KeyLike, { isMac, desktop }: { isMac: boolean; desktop: boolean }): AppShortcut | null {
  if (event.altKey) return null;
  const held = isMac ? event.metaKey && !event.ctrlKey && !event.shiftKey : event.ctrlKey && event.shiftKey && !event.metaKey;
  if (!held) return null;
  if (isLetter(event, "k")) return { action: "palette" };
  if (!desktop) return null;
  if (isLetter(event, "t")) return { action: "new-session" };
  const digit = rowDigit(event);
  return digit === null ? null : { action: "switch", index: digit - 1 };
}
```

with

```ts
// The backslash key, by its place first: Shift turns it into "|" (Ctrl+Shift+\ on Windows and Linux).
function isBackslash(event: KeyLike): boolean {
  return event.code === "Backslash" || event.key === "\\";
}

// The only keys a terminal leaves to Agent OS: ⌘K, ⌘T, ⌘1-9 and ⌘\ on a Mac; Ctrl+Shift+K/T/1-9/\ elsewhere.
// Everything else goes to the agent, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+R and Ctrl+\ (the terminal's quit key) included. A browser keeps
// ⌘T and ⌘1-9 (Ctrl+T, Ctrl+1-9, Ctrl+Shift+T) for itself, so in browser mode only the palette key is Agent OS's;
// split view has its Split view button there (Task U6).
export function isAppShortcut(event: KeyLike, { isMac, desktop }: { isMac: boolean; desktop: boolean }): AppShortcut | null {
  if (event.altKey) return null;
  const held = isMac ? event.metaKey && !event.ctrlKey && !event.shiftKey : event.ctrlKey && event.shiftKey && !event.metaKey;
  if (!held) return null;
  if (isLetter(event, "k")) return { action: "palette" };
  if (!desktop) return null;
  if (isLetter(event, "t")) return { action: "new-session" };
  if (isBackslash(event)) return { action: "split" };
  const digit = rowDigit(event);
  return digit === null ? null : { action: "switch", index: digit - 1 };
}
```

```tsx
// One pane's header in split view (the prototype's .ss-phd; spec SP4, Split): the session's title, its branch and its
// state as icon and word. It is a button: pressing it, or clicking anywhere in the pane, makes this the focused pane,
// and the side panel shows its details. aria-pressed says which pane the panel follows.
import { SquareTerminal } from "lucide-react";
import type { SessionSummary } from "../../types";
import { sessionStateWord, sessionTitle } from "../sessionsShared";
import { paneHeadLabel } from "../splitShared";
import StatusWord from "./StatusWord";

export default function SessionPaneHead({
  session,
  focused,
  onPick
}: {
  session: SessionSummary;
  focused: boolean;
  onPick: () => void;
}) {
  const title = sessionTitle(session);
  const word = sessionStateWord(session);
  return (
    <button type="button" className="os-sess-pane__head" aria-pressed={focused} aria-label={paneHeadLabel(title)} title={title} onClick={onPick}>
      <SquareTerminal size={16} aria-hidden="true" />
      <span className="os-sess-pane__title">{title}</span>
      {session.branch ? <code className="os-mono os-sess-pane__branch">{session.branch}</code> : null}
      <span className="os-sess-pane__state">
        <StatusWord state={word.state} label={word.label} />
      </span>
    </button>
  );
}
```

Create `src/ui/components/SplitDivider.tsx`:

```tsx
// The divider between the two panes of split view (the prototype's .ss-div; spec SP4, Split): drag it, or use the
// arrow keys (2 % a press) and Home (back to the middle); a double click puts it back in the middle too. It reports the
// left pane's share of the panes' width (28 % to 72 %, splitShared.ts); the page keeps it with the rest of split view.
// The pointer is captured while dragging, so moving over a terminal never selects text or reaches the agent.
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import type { KeyboardEvent, PointerEvent, RefObject } from "react";
import { SPLIT_DEFAULT, SPLIT_DIVIDER_LABEL, SPLIT_MAX, SPLIT_MIN, dividerKeyRatio, ratioFromPointer } from "../splitShared";

export default function SplitDivider({
  ratio,
  containerRef,
  onRatio
}: {
  ratio: number;
  containerRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement>;
  onRatio: (ratio: number) => void;
}) {
  const dragging = useRef(false);
  const [drag, setDrag] = useState(false);

  function stop() {
    dragging.current = false;
    setDrag(false);
  }
  function follow(event: PointerEvent<HTMLDivElement>) {
    const box = containerRef.current?.getBoundingClientRect();
    const next = box ? ratioFromPointer(event.clientX, box.left, box.width) : null;
    if (next !== null) onRatio(next);
  }
  function onKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) {
    const next = dividerKeyRatio(event.key, ratio);
    if (next === null) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    onRatio(next);
  }

  return (
    <div
      className={drag ? "os-sess-split__divider is-drag" : "os-sess-split__divider"}
      role="separator"
      aria-orientation="vertical"
      aria-label={SPLIT_DIVIDER_LABEL}
      aria-valuemin={Math.round(SPLIT_MIN * 100)}
      aria-valuemax={Math.round(SPLIT_MAX * 100)}
      aria-valuenow={Math.round(ratio * 100)}
      tabIndex={0}
      onPointerDown={(event) => {
        if (event.button !== 0) return;
        event.preventDefault();
        event.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId);
        dragging.current = true;
        setDrag(true);
      }}
      onPointerMove={(event) => {
        if (dragging.current) follow(event);
      }}
      onPointerUp={stop}
      onPointerCancel={stop}
      onLostPointerCapture={stop}
      onDoubleClick={() => onRatio(SPLIT_DEFAULT)}
      onKeyDown={onKeyDown}
    >
      <i aria-hidden="true" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// Split view is kept per window (this browser tab, or this desktop window): sessionStorage survives a reload and
// leaving the page, and a second window starts with one terminal (Task U6). A locked-down webview keeps it until the
// page reloads.
function readSplit(): SplitState {
  try {
    return parseSplitState(window.sessionStorage.getItem(SPLIT_KEY));
  } catch {
    return parseSplitState(null);
  }
}
function writeSplit(state: SplitState) {
  try {
    window.sessionStorage.setItem(SPLIT_KEY, serializeSplitState(state));
  } catch {
    // A locked-down webview: split view lasts until the page reloads.
  }
}
```

```tsx
  // The terminal keys a pane showed while their session was open (see the comment at the top and nextLiveShown).
  const [liveShown, setLiveShown] = useState<ReadonlySet<string>>(() => new Set<string>());
  // Split view, kept per window (readSplit). `aligned` is that state made true to the tabs and the selected tab
  // (alignSplit): the selected tab is the focused pane, a pane whose session left the tabs gets another one, and the
  // same session is never in both panes. While the tab asked for is not listed yet (a session started a moment ago),
  // the page shows another tab meanwhile, so split view waits for it instead of moving the focus there and back.
  const [split, setSplit] = useState<SplitState>(readSplit);
  const aligned = body && (!wanted || wantedListed) ? alignSplit(split, tabs, selectedId) : split;
  const splitPanes =
    aligned.on && aligned.panes && aligned.panes.includes(selectedId)
      ? aligned.panes.map((id) => tabs.find((tab) => tab.id === id)).filter((tab): tab is SessionSummary => Boolean(tab))
      : [];
  const splitOn = splitPanes.length === 2;
  // What the panes show: the two sessions of split view, or the selected one.
  const paneSessions: SessionSummary[] = splitOn ? splitPanes : selected ? [selected] : [];
  const otherPaneId = splitOn ? (splitPanes.find((session) => session.id !== selectedId)?.id ?? "") : "";
```

In `.superpowers/ui-audit/probes/sessions.mjs`, replace (line 533)
`      check(!keys.includes("\\"), "no split hint (split view is SP4)", keys);`
with
`      check(/⌘\\/.test(keys) && /split/.test(keys), "(Task U6) desktop on a Mac: ⌘\\ split", keys);`

Create `.superpowers/ui-audit/probes/split.mjs`:

```js
// Task U6: split view on the Sessions page (spec SP4, Split). Run (after `npm run build`), from the worktree root:
//   node .superpowers/ui-audit/audit.mjs probe .superpowers/ui-audit/probes/split.mjs
// Real PTY sessions of the TUI-like fake agent (test/fakes/tui-agent.mjs prints "FAKE_ARGV {...}" and a "> " prompt,
// echoes what is typed and answers each line with "you said: <text>"), started through the API on the harness's
// throwaway server. It checks the two panes and their headers, the side panel following the focused pane, typing
// reaching only the focused pane, that no session is ever attached twice at once in a window (the page's own attach
// sockets are counted), the divider (drag, the 28 % limit, double click, keys), that split view is kept per window (a
// reload keeps it, a second window does not get it), Split view off without a reattach, ⌘\ and its hint in the
// desktop app, the layout at 1280×720 and 1024×640, and an ended, then dismissed pane. Nothing here starts a real
// agent, and every session it started is stopped at the end.
import { mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

const W = 1470, H = 956;
const BANNER = "FAKE_ARGV";
// Chrome logs refused requests as "Failed to load resource"; anything else is a real console error.
const realErrors = (errors) => errors.filter((e) => !/Failed to load resource/.test(e));

export default async function ({ browser, shot, pass, fail, api, BASE, TOKEN, HOME }) {
  const check = (ok, name, why = "") => (ok ? pass(name) : fail(name, String(why)));
  if (!HOME) {
    fail("harness", "audit.mjs does not pass HOME to probes");
    return;
  }
  const folders = {};
  for (const name of ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]) {
    folders[name] = path.join(HOME, "projects", name);
    mkdirSync(folders[name], { recursive: true });
  }
  const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
  const waitFor = async (fn, ms = 10000) => {
    const end = Date.now() + ms;
    while (Date.now() < end) {
      try { if (await fn()) return true; } catch {}
      await sleep(250);
    }
    return false;
  };
  const startViaApi = async (agentId, folder) => {
    const made = await api("POST", "/api/sessions", { agentId, folder });
    return made.status < 300 && made.json.id ? made.json.id : "";
  };
  // Past "starting" (the fake agent prints its first screen at once).
  const started = (id) => waitFor(async () => { const answer = (await api("GET", `/api/sessions/${id}`)).json; return Boolean(answer.status) && answer.status !== "starting"; }, 10000);
  async function stopEverything() {
    const answer = await api("GET", "/api/sessions?kind=all");
    for (const x of answer.json.sessions || []) if (x.status !== "exited") await api("POST", `/api/sessions/${x.id}/stop`);
  }
  const sessionParam = (tab) => new URL(tab.url()).searchParams.get("session") || "";
  const paneIds = (tab) => tab.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll(".os-sess-pane[data-session]")].map((el) => el.getAttribute("data-session")));
  const sameIds = async (tab, ids) => JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)) === JSON.stringify(ids);
  const pane = (tab, id) => tab.locator(`.os-sess-pane[data-session="${id}"]`);
  // The DOM renderer (the default on macOS, decision Q45) keeps each screen's text in .xterm-rows.
  const paneText = (tab, id) => tab.evaluate((sid) => document.querySelector(`.os-sess-pane[data-session="${sid}"] .xterm-rows`)?.textContent || "", id);
  const panelFolder = async (tab) => ((await tab.getByRole("complementary", { name: "Session details" }).locator("h2").textContent()) || "").trim();
  const splitButton = (tab) => tab.getByRole("button", { name: "Split view", exact: true });
  const divider = (tab) => tab.getByRole("separator", { name: "Resize the two terminals" });
  const tabNamed = (tab, name) => tab.getByRole("tab", { name, exact: true });
  const tabMarkedInSplit = (tab, id) => tab.evaluate((sid) => Boolean(document.getElementById(`os-sess-tab-${sid}`)?.closest(".os-sess-tab")?.classList.contains("is-in-split")), id);
  const isFocusPane = (tab, id) => pane(tab, id).evaluate((el) => el.classList.contains("is-focus"));
  const sideways = (tab) => tab.evaluate(() => document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth > document.scrollingElement.clientWidth);
  const leftShare = (tab) => tab.evaluate(() => {
    const box = document.querySelector(".os-sess-panes")?.getBoundingClientRect();
    const first = document.querySelector(".os-sess-panes > .os-sess-pane")?.getBoundingClientRect();
    return box && first && box.width ? first.width / box.width : NaN;
  });
  // Every attach socket this window opens, per session: open now, how many in all, and the most ever open at once
  // for one session.
  function watchAttaches(tab) {
    const open = new Map(), total = new Map();
    let most = 0;
    tab.on("websocket", (ws) => {
      const match = /\/api\/sessions\/([^/?]+)\/attach/.exec(ws.url());
      if (!match) return;
      const id = match[1];
      open.set(id, (open.get(id) || 0) + 1);
      total.set(id, (total.get(id) || 0) + 1);
      most = Math.max(most, open.get(id));
      ws.on("close", () => open.set(id, Math.max(0, (open.get(id) || 0) - 1)));
    });
    return { open: (id) => open.get(id) || 0, total: (id) => total.get(id) || 0, most: () => most };
  }
  // A window whose sockets are watched from its first page load (the harness's openPage would start counting late).
  async function openWatched(width, height, page) {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width, height } });
    const tab = await context.newPage();
    const errors = [];
    tab.on("console", (m) => { if (m.type() === "error") errors.push(m.text()); });
    tab.on("pageerror", (e) => errors.push(String(e)));
    const attaches = watchAttaches(tab);
    await tab.goto(`${BASE}/?launch=${TOKEN}`);
    await tab.goto(`${BASE}/?page=${page}`);
    await tab.waitForTimeout(1200);
    return { context, tab, errors, attaches };
  }

  try {
    const A = await startViaApi("claude", folders.alpha);
    const B = await startViaApi("codex", folders.beta);
    const C = await startViaApi("claude", folders.gamma);
    check(Boolean(A && B && C) && new Set([A, B, C]).size === 3, "setup: three sessions (alpha, beta, gamma)", `${A} ${B} ${C}`);
    for (const id of [A, B, C]) await started(id);

    // 1-6 run in one browser window (browser mode), opened on alpha.
    {
      const { context, tab, errors, attaches } = await openWatched(W, H, `sessions&session=${A}`);

      // 1. The Split view button, two panes with their own headers, the focused pane, the divider.
      const btn = splitButton(tab);
      check(await btn.isVisible(), "the Split view button is in the tab bar");
      check((await btn.getAttribute("aria-pressed")) === "false", "split view starts off");
      check((await btn.getAttribute("title")) === "Show two sessions side by side", "browser tab: the button names no key", await btn.getAttribute("title"));
      check((await btn.locator("kbd").count()) === 0, "browser tab: no key on the button");
      check((await tab.locator(".os-sess-keys").count()) === 0, "browser tab: still no shortcut hints in the panel footer");
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await paneText(tab, A)).includes(BANNER), 15000), "one pane: alpha's terminal is up");
      check(await sameIds(tab, [A]), "one pane before split view", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));
      const alphaAttaches = attaches.total(A);
      await btn.click();
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await paneIds(tab)).length === 2, 5000), "Split view shows two panes");
      check(await sameIds(tab, [A, B]), "alpha (the selected tab) on the left, beta (the next open tab) on the right", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));
      check((await btn.getAttribute("aria-pressed")) === "true", "the button says split view is on");
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await paneText(tab, B)).includes(BANNER), 15000), "the right pane shows beta's own terminal");
      check(attaches.total(A) === alphaAttaches, "turning split view on keeps alpha's terminal attached (no reattach)", `${alphaAttaches} -> ${attaches.total(A)}`);
      check(attaches.total(B) === 1, "the right pane attached beta once", String(attaches.total(B)));
      check(await pane(tab, A).getByRole("button", { name: "Claude Code · alpha, show its details" }).isVisible(), "the left pane has its own header");
      check(await pane(tab, B).getByRole("button", { name: "Codex · beta, show its details" }).isVisible(), "the right pane has its own header");
      check((await pane(tab, A).locator(".os-sess-pane__head").getAttribute("aria-pressed")) === "true", "the left pane is the focused one");
      check((await pane(tab, B).locator(".os-sess-pane__head").getAttribute("aria-pressed")) === "false", "the right pane is not");
      check((await panelFolder(tab)) === "alpha", "the side panel shows the focused pane", await panelFolder(tab));
      check(await tabMarkedInSplit(tab, B), "beta's tab is marked as shown in the other pane");
      const sep = divider(tab);
      check(await sep.isVisible(), "the divider sits between the panes");
      check((await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow")) === "50", "it starts in the middle", await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow"));
      check(Math.abs((await leftShare(tab)) - 0.5) < 0.03, "the left pane takes half the width", String(await leftShare(tab)));
      check(!(await sideways(tab)), "no sideways scroll (split view)");
      await shot(tab, "split", W, H, "split");

      // 2. The side panel follows the focused pane, and typing reaches only that pane's agent.
      await pane(tab, B).locator(".xterm").click();
      check(await waitFor(async () => sessionParam(tab) === B, 3000), "a click in the right pane makes it the focused pane", sessionParam(tab));
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await panelFolder(tab)) === "beta", 3000), "the side panel follows it", await panelFolder(tab));
      check((await tabNamed(tab, "Codex · beta").getAttribute("aria-selected")) === "true", "beta's tab is the selected tab");
      check(await tabMarkedInSplit(tab, A), "and alpha's tab is the one marked as shown");
      check((await isFocusPane(tab, B)) && !(await isFocusPane(tab, A)), "only the right pane's frame is the focused one");
      await tab.keyboard.type("hello-right");
      await tab.keyboard.press("Enter");
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await paneText(tab, B)).includes("you said: hello-right"), 5000), "typing reaches the focused pane's agent", (await paneText(tab, B)).slice(-160));
      check(!(await paneText(tab, A)).includes("hello-right"), "and never the other pane's");
      await pane(tab, A).locator(".os-sess-pane__head").click();
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await panelFolder(tab)) === "alpha", 3000), "the left pane's header shows its details", await panelFolder(tab));

      // 3. The same session is never in both panes: its tab moves the focus there; a tab in neither pane takes the
      //    focused pane's place.
      await tabNamed(tab, "Codex · beta").click();
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await panelFolder(tab)) === "beta", 3000), "the other pane's tab moves the focus to that pane", await panelFolder(tab));
      check(await sameIds(tab, [A, B]), "and both panes stay as they were", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));
      await tabNamed(tab, "Claude Code · gamma").click();
      check(await waitFor(async () => sameIds(tab, [A, C]), 5000), "a tab in neither pane takes the focused pane's place", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await paneText(tab, C)).includes(BANNER), 15000), "and shows its terminal there");
      check((await panelFolder(tab)) === "gamma", "the side panel follows it", await panelFolder(tab));
      const ids = await paneIds(tab);
      check(new Set(ids).size === ids.length, "never the same session in both panes", JSON.stringify(ids));
      check(attaches.most() <= 1, "no session was ever attached twice at once in this window", String(attaches.most()));
      check(await waitFor(async () => attaches.open(B) === 0, 5000), "beta, now off screen, is no longer attached here", String(attaches.open(B)));

      // 4. The divider: drag, the 28 % limit, double click, keys.
      const panesBox = await tab.locator(".os-sess-panes").boundingBox();
      const drag = async (toX) => {
        const grip = await sep.boundingBox();
        const y = grip.y + grip.height / 2;
        await tab.mouse.move(grip.x + grip.width / 2, y);
        await tab.mouse.down();
        await tab.mouse.move(toX, y, { steps: 8 });
        await tab.mouse.up();
      };
      await drag(panesBox.x + panesBox.width * 0.3);
      check(Math.abs(Number(await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow")) - 30) <= 2, "dragging the divider moves it (about 30 %)", await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow"));
      check(Math.abs((await leftShare(tab)) - 0.3) < 0.03, "and the left pane follows", String(await leftShare(tab)));
      await shot(tab, "split", W, H, "split-dragged");
      await drag(panesBox.x + 10);
      check((await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow")) === "28", "it stops at 28 %", await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow"));
      await sep.dblclick();
      check((await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow")) === "50", "a double click puts it back in the middle", await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow"));
      await sep.focus();
      await tab.keyboard.press("ArrowRight");
      check((await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow")) === "52", "ArrowRight moves it 2 %", await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow"));
      await tab.keyboard.press("Home");
      check((await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow")) === "50", "Home puts it back in the middle", await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow"));
      for (let i = 0; i < 5; i += 1) await tab.keyboard.press("ArrowLeft");
      check((await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow")) === "40", "ArrowLeft five times: 40 %", await sep.getAttribute("aria-valuenow"));
      check((await panelFolder(tab)) === "gamma", "using the divider leaves the focused pane as it was", await panelFolder(tab));

      // 5. Kept per window: a reload keeps split view as it was; a second window starts with one terminal.
      await tab.reload();
      await tab.waitForTimeout(1500);
      check(await waitFor(async () => sameIds(tab, [A, C]), 8000), "a reload keeps both panes", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));
      check((await divider(tab).getAttribute("aria-valuenow")) === "40", "and the divider's place", await divider(tab).getAttribute("aria-valuenow"));
      check((await panelFolder(tab)) === "gamma", "and the focused pane (the address keeps its session)", await panelFolder(tab));
      const second = await context.newPage();
      await second.goto(`${BASE}/?page=sessions&session=${A}`);
      await second.waitForTimeout(1500);
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await paneIds(second)).length === 1, 8000), "a second window of the same browser starts with one terminal", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(second)));
      check((await splitButton(second).getAttribute("aria-pressed")) === "false", "its Split view button is off");
      await second.close();
      check(await sameIds(tab, [A, C]), "and the first window keeps its split view", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));

      // 6. Split view off keeps the focused pane, without a reattach.
      await waitFor(async () => (await paneText(tab, C)).includes(BANNER), 15000);
      const gammaAttaches = attaches.total(C);
      await splitButton(tab).click();
      check(await waitFor(async () => sameIds(tab, [C]), 5000), "Split view off keeps the focused pane's session", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));
      check(attaches.total(C) === gammaAttaches, "without reattaching it", `${gammaAttaches} -> ${attaches.total(C)}`);
      check((await tab.locator(".os-sess-pane__head").count()) === 0 && (await tab.locator(".os-sess-split__divider").count()) === 0, "one pane: no pane header and no divider");
      check(realErrors(errors).length === 0, "console clean (browser mode)", errors.join(" / "));
      await context.close();
    }

    // 7. The desktop app (?desktop=1, a Mac here): ⌘\ split in the panel footer, the key on the button, and ⌘\ itself,
    //    pressed inside a terminal, where the agent never gets it.
    {
      const { context, tab, errors } = await openWatched(W, H, `sessions&desktop=1&session=${A}`);
      const keys = (await tab.locator(".os-sess-keys").textContent()) || "";
      check(/⌘\\/.test(keys) && /split/.test(keys), "desktop on a Mac: the panel footer shows ⌘\\ split", keys);
      check((await splitButton(tab).getAttribute("title")) === "Show two sessions side by side (⌘\\)", "the button names its key", await splitButton(tab).getAttribute("title"));
      check(((await splitButton(tab).locator("kbd").textContent()) || "") === "⌘\\", "and shows it", await splitButton(tab).locator("kbd").textContent());
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await paneText(tab, A)).includes(BANNER), 15000), "setup: alpha's terminal is up");
      await pane(tab, A).locator(".xterm").click();
      await tab.keyboard.press("Meta+Backslash");
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await paneIds(tab)).length === 2, 5000), "⌘\\ inside the terminal turns split view on", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));
      check(await tab.evaluate(() => Boolean(document.activeElement?.closest(".xterm"))), "the keyboard stays in the terminal");
      await waitFor(async () => (await paneText(tab, B)).includes(BANNER), 15000);
      await shot(tab, "split", W, H, "split-desktop");
      await tab.keyboard.press("Meta+Backslash");
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await paneIds(tab)).length === 1, 5000), "⌘\\ again turns it off");
      await tab.keyboard.type("after");
      await tab.keyboard.press("Enter");
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await paneText(tab, A)).includes("you said: after"), 5000), "the agent never got ⌘\\ (its line is exactly what was typed)", (await paneText(tab, A)).slice(-160));
      check(realErrors(errors).length === 0, "console clean (desktop app)", errors.join(" / "));
      await context.close();
    }

    // 8. Laptop and minimum window sizes: both panes on screen, a pane title stays in its pane, no sideways scroll,
    //    and Stop session still on screen.
    for (const [w, h] of [[1280, 720], [1024, 640]]) {
      const { context, tab, errors } = await openWatched(w, h, `sessions&session=${A}`);
      await splitButton(tab).click();
      check(await waitFor(async () => (await paneIds(tab)).length === 2, 5000), `${w}x${h}: two panes`);
      await waitFor(async () => (await paneText(tab, B)).includes(BANNER), 15000);
      const fits = await tab.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll(".os-sess-pane")].every((el) => { const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(); return r.width > 150 && r.left >= 0 && r.right <= window.innerWidth; }));
      check(fits, `${w}x${h}: both panes are on screen`);
      check(!(await sideways(tab)), `${w}x${h}: no sideways scroll`);
      const head = await tab.locator(".os-sess-pane__title").first().evaluate((el) => ({ ellipsis: getComputedStyle(el).textOverflow === "ellipsis", inside: el.getBoundingClientRect().right <= el.closest(".os-sess-pane").getBoundingClientRect().right + 1 }));
      check(head.ellipsis && head.inside, `${w}x${h}: a pane title stays inside its pane and ends in "…" when it must`, JSON.stringify(head));
      const stopBox = await tab.getByRole("complementary", { name: "Session details" }).getByRole("button", { name: "Stop session" }).boundingBox();
      check(Boolean(stopBox) && stopBox.y + stopBox.height <= h, `${w}x${h}: Stop session is on screen`, JSON.stringify(stopBox));
      await shot(tab, "split", w, h, "split");
      check(realErrors(errors).length === 0, `${w}x${h}: console clean`, errors.join(" / "));
      await context.close();
    }

    // 9. An ended pane keeps its last screen and its panel offers Resume; a dismissed pane gives its place to the next
    //    open tab; with one tab left, split view ends and its button says why it can't be pressed.
    {
      const { context, tab, errors } = await openWatched(W, H, `sessions&session=${A}`);
      await splitButton(tab).click();
      check(await waitFor(async () => sameIds(tab, [A, B]), 5000), "setup: alpha and beta side by side", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));
      await waitFor(async () => (await paneText(tab, B)).includes(BANNER), 15000);
      await api("POST", `/api/sessions/${B}/stop`);
      check(await waitFor(async () => /Ended/.test((await tab.locator(`#os-sess-tab-${B}`).textContent()) || ""), 15000), "setup: beta ended");
      check((await pane(tab, B).locator(".os-sess-term").count()) === 1 && (await paneText(tab, B)).includes(BANNER), "an ended pane keeps its last screen");
      check(await sameIds(tab, [A, B]), "and split view stays", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));
      await pane(tab, B).locator(".os-sess-pane__head").click();
      check(await waitFor(async () => await tab.getByRole("complementary", { name: "Session details" }).getByRole("button", { name: "Resume conversation" }).isVisible(), 5000), "focusing the ended pane shows its ended panel (Resume conversation)");
      await shot(tab, "split", W, H, "split-ended");
      await pane(tab, A).locator(".os-sess-pane__head").click();
      await waitFor(async () => (await panelFolder(tab)) === "alpha", 3000);
      await api("POST", `/api/sessions/${B}/dismiss`);
      check(await waitFor(async () => sameIds(tab, [A, C]), 12000), "a dismissed pane gives its place to the next open tab", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));
      await api("POST", `/api/sessions/${C}/stop`);
      await waitFor(async () => /Ended/.test((await tab.locator(`#os-sess-tab-${C}`).textContent()) || ""), 15000);
      await api("POST", `/api/sessions/${C}/dismiss`);
      check(await waitFor(async () => sameIds(tab, [A]), 12000), "with one tab left, split view ends", JSON.stringify(await paneIds(tab)));
      check(await splitButton(tab).isDisabled(), "Split view can't be pressed with one tab");
      check((await splitButton(tab).getAttribute("title")) === "Split view needs two sessions.", "and its tooltip says why", await splitButton(tab).getAttribute("title"));
      check(realErrors(errors).length === 0, "console clean (ended and dismissed panes)", errors.join(" / "));
      await context.close();
    }
  } finally {
    // Leave nothing running, even when a section above threw: every session this probe started is stopped.
    await stopEverything().catch(() => undefined);
  }
  const left = await api("GET", "/api/sessions?kind=all");
  check((left.json.sessions || []).every((x) => x.status === "exited"), "the probe leaves no session running", JSON.stringify((left.json.sessions || []).map((x) => x.status)));
}
```

### Task X7: Changes panel (server)

Agent OS shows which files a session changed, with their +/− line counts, and a read-only diff when the person clicks one (spec "SP4 Session extras", "Changes panel"). Every change is also kept as a "files changed" moment for the recording (spec "Recordings in Runs"). Today there is no git process helper on the server at all: `readGitBranch` (manager.js, line 201 at HEAD `548786d`) reads git's files and never runs git, and meta.json gets its `markers` list only from Task X1a.

This task builds the server half:
- `server/runtime/sessions/git.js`: a small git runner. It is argv only (never a shell), always `git -C <folder>` with options that stop git from taking the index lock or running the person's file monitor, cut at 5 s, and run with the session's own environment minus Agent OS's own variables (never the server's environment, which holds `AGENT_OS_TOKEN`). It asks `runCli` for git's error text with X3's `captureStderr`, and Task X9 reuses it for separate copies.
- `server/runtime/sessions/changes.js`: reads `git status --porcelain=v2` and `git diff --numstat` into a list of changed files (at most 200, with the full count), reads one file's diff (only a path that is in the session's current changes, checked again before git runs), and works out the "files changed" marker.
- The session manager polls each agent session's repository: once at the start (the baseline, which never makes a marker), then every 3 s while the session runs, and soon after Claude's PostToolUse(Edit|Write) hook. It runs one read at a time per session, so a big or slow folder never piles up git processes, and `GET /api/sessions/:id/changes` always answers the last result at once.
- Two read-only routes: `GET /api/sessions/:id/changes` and `GET /api/sessions/:id/changes/diff?path=<path>`.

Nothing here writes to the person's folder or to git: no `add`, `reset`, `checkout`, `stash` or `commit` is ever run, and git never refreshes the index. The tests run real git only inside temp repositories under a temp HOME (with `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`), and drive the manager with injected fakes for the terminal, so no agent and no terminal program ever starts. U7 builds the panel on top of this.

**Worker notes:**
- Run every command from the worktree root `<worktree>`. Never commit, push, tag, stash or set `CI=true`. Never start a real agent. Never read `.env` files or `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.cursor`, `~/.openclaw`, `~/.hermes`. Never signal or inspect a process the tests did not start.
- A PreToolUse hook ("Fact-Forcing Gate") may refuse the first Bash command, the first Write of a new file or an `rm`. State the facts it asks for, then retry the same call.
- In zsh, quote separator strings such as `"====="`.
- Stay inside the file list below. If a test outside it fails or hangs because of the new git reads, stop and report it; do not edit that test.

1. **Spec sentences this task serves (word for word, spec "Changes panel"):** "`git status --porcelain=v2` and `git diff --numstat` in the session folder, every 3 s while the session is running, and immediately on Claude's PostToolUse(Edit|Write) hooks;" / "click a file for a read-only diff;" / "each change is also stored as a "files changed" recording marker;" / "not a git folder: "Changes appear when this folder is a git project"." and, from "Recordings in Runs", "files changed (path and +/−, from the changes panel);". NEW SENTENCE (Q32) (already in the contract's Errors table). The Error text inside `readChanges` ("Agent OS could not read the changes from git (<code>).") is developer-only: the manager catches it and it never reaches a person or an HTTP answer.
3. **Rulings and choices applied:** K12 (the whole repository with paths from its top level; the first read after a start is the baseline; a marker lists only files whose counts changed, at most 20, `more` counts the rest; the list stops at 200 files; `--no-optional-locks`, `core.fsmonitor=false`, `--no-ext-diff`, `--no-textconv`); K20 (markers go through X1a's `addMarker`, which keeps the newest 500); R5 (a PostToolUse(Write) body over 256 KB is dropped unprocessed, so it asks for no read; the 3 s poll still sees the change); R27 (the hooks router is unchanged: the refresh runs inside `onHook`, which X2a runs on `setImmediate` after the 204, so a hook reply never waits for git); R28 (the one new sentence goes to E1); R30 (pacing). Global Constraints: "CLI calls" (git only through `runGit` and `runCli`, the session's own environment, never `process.env`; an ended session uses the login-shell environment), "Local mode" (the routes sit behind the existing `requireLocalMode` mount), "Signals scope" (markers for `agent` sessions only), "PTY writes" (none added), "Files on disk" (no new file; markers live in meta.json through X1a), "Tests" (real git only in temp repositories). The contract reads the spec's "immediately" as "within `CHANGES_REFRESH_DEBOUNCE_MS` (300 ms)", so a burst of edits makes one read.
4. **Review Focus 4 (a big or slow git folder)** is covered by two tests named after it: part 1 (every git run is cut at 5 s, with mocked timers) and part 2 (one read at a time, 200 files with the full total, a cut read keeps the last result, and `GET /api/sessions/:id/changes` answers at once while git runs).
5. **Decisions this task makes** (the orchestrator can overturn any of them):
   - git runs in the repository's top folder (`-C <top>`) after one `rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the session folder, so a person's `diff.relative` setting cannot narrow the list, and untracked paths line up with numstat paths.
   - `status` gets `--branch`, so `# branch.oid (initial)` shows a repository with no commit yet without another git call; then numstat is `diff --cached` plus `diff` (contract), added together per path.
   - `HEAD --` always carries the `--`: without it a file named `HEAD` in the folder makes `git diff HEAD` fail as ambiguous (checked with git 2.39.5).
   - A renamed entry's counts add its old path's numstat counts when git's diff did not pair the rename itself (then the old path shows as removed lines), so the row still shows what changed.
   - `git diff --no-index` exits 1 both for "different" and for "could not read the file"; exit 1 with nothing printed counts as the file being gone (`change_missing`).
   - Git that cannot start is tried once per session: `rev-parse` that never started (code null) or answered anything other than 0 or 128 (128 is git's own "not a git repository") stops that session's poll, so a Mac without Apple's command line tools is not asked to install them every 3 s.
   - Untracked text files are counted only up to 512 KB each and 4 MB per read; the rest show `null` ("—"). Files are opened with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, so a link is never followed and a pipe never blocks.
   - A status-only change (staging with the same counts) and a file that left the list (committed or put back) make no marker. There is no last read at exit, so a change in the last 3 s before a session ends gets no marker.
   - `runGit` keeps at most 4096 characters of git's error text (X3's `captureStderr` caps it at `maxChars` only).
   - Both routes answer `Cache-Control: no-store`, as the recording stream does (a diff holds file contents).
6. **Risks:**
   - Every existing test that creates an agent session through a manager with the default `runGit` now runs one `git rev-parse` per session (their temp folders are not git projects, so git answers 128 at once; on Windows without git it never starts and the poll stops). Under mocked timers the read waits until the test ticks. No frame or summary changes, but the full suite run in Step 10 is the check.
   - Clean filters (Git LFS, for example) still run during `git status`, as in the person's own `git status`; K12's "helpers" covered here are the file monitor, external diff tools and text converters (a test proves those stay off).
   - A file name that is not valid UTF-8 comes back with replacement characters, so its diff answers `change_missing`.
   - The exit code of macOS's "install the developer tools" stand-in for `/usr/bin/git` is not verified (the owner's Mac has the tools, so E2 cannot see it); the rule treats any code other than 0 and 128 as "git can't run here".

```js
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import test from "node:test";

import {
  CHANGES_MAX_FILES,
  CHANGES_POLL_MS,
  CHANGES_REFRESH_DEBOUNCE_MS,
  CHANGE_MISSING_MESSAGE,
  DIFF_MAX_BYTES,

  filesMarker,

} from "../server/runtime/sessions/changes.js";
```
